# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

- **The WebAuthn browser suite prints the xkmsd log when it fails.** `run-server.sh` keeps xkmsd's full output in the git-ignored `.runtime/xkmsd.log`, and `make integration-test-webauthn-browser` runs the suite through `run-suite.sh`, which prints the log's last 400 lines when Playwright fails and keeps its exit status (CA m2529).

### Fixed

- **Devcontainer image job: a hung step fails fast (CA m2536).** Main run 42965847875 sat two hours in `make coverage` until it was cancelled at the job's 240 min. Every `scripts/in-toolchain-image.sh` step of the Devcontainer image job now carries its own `timeout-minutes` below the job's, and the four `npm ci` calls of `make test-web` pass `--fetch-timeout=60000 --fetch-retries=2`, so a stalled registry fetch errors out instead of hanging.

### Security

- **Go toolchain 1.27.4 for GO-2026-6859, `net/http` (#2058).** govulncheck reports GO-2026-6859 in the go1.27.3 standard library, fixed in go1.27.4 (2026-11-02). The `go` line of `go.mod`, `sdk/go`, `web/desktop` and `xkey`, every workflow `GO_VERSION`, every `golang:` builder and test image tag, the Go tarball downloads in `xkey`, and the digest-pinned `GO_IMAGE` (`scripts/tool-pins.sh`, `Dockerfile.cli`, `release.yml` `GO_IMAGE_DIGEST`, now the `golang:1.27.4-bookworm` index `sha256:4fa7c968…`) move to 1.27.4. No dependency or code change.

## [0.64.0-alpha] - 2026-10-25

### Security

- **echo bumped to v4.16.1.** `github.com/labstack/echo/v4` moves from v4.15.3 to v4.16.1 in every module (root, `sdk/go`, `web/desktop`, `xkey`) for GHSA-cxf3-9h37-7rr8 (critical) and the three high advisories trivy reports on v4.15.3.

### Added

- **`x509-svid` through ACME** (#1547) -- a newOrder may name `profile: "x509-svid"` (draft-aaron-acme-profiles, listed in the directory's `meta.profiles`) with one `spiffe` identifier, `spiffe://<tenant>/svc/<name>`. An account bound to that tenant is authorized without a challenge, and the tenant's own CA signs the SVID: the SPIFFE ID is its one URI SAN, OU[0] is the tenant, and the subject has no CN. Another tenant's name, an unbound account or a tenant without its own CA is `unauthorized`, and an unknown profile is `invalidProfile`. SVIDs are linted by their own issuer, which admits a URI SAN whose host is a tenant rather than an FQDN (`linter.Identifiers.SVID`). Tenant-signed ACME certificates are now verified against the tenant CA, not the global pools. A test pins that one tenant's bundle never verifies another tenant's SVID. See `docs/workload-identity/engineering.md`.

- **Attestation Verifier and reference-values store (go-xkms#1608).** The
  go-quicbaas Verifier moved here with its history, as
  `pkg/attestation/appraisal`. It appraises TPM quotes (`AppraiseQuote`),
  hosts (`AppraiseHost`) and container launches (`AppraiseContainer`) against
  a tenant's endorsements (AK roots and reference-value signers) and signed
  CoRIM reference values, kept per tenant in the qrdb DAO database
  `attestation`. `XKMSService` serves the endorsement, reference-value and
  appraisal verbs scoped to the caller's tenant. They are gated by the new
  permissions `attestation_endorsements`, `attestation_reference_values` and
  `attestation_verifier`, and return `ErrNotConfigured` until
  `SetAttestationAppraiser` wires an Appraiser. `sdk/go` re-exports the
  package as `NewAttestationAppraiser`, `NewAttestationAppraisalStore`, the
  request and result types and the `ErrAttestation*` errors, so go-quicbaas
  can consume it. The REST, gRPC and MCP routes are not yet in. Code:
  `pkg/attestation/appraisal`, `pkg/xkms/servicer_attestation.go`; docs:
  `docs/attestation-verifier/architecture.md#appraisal-the-rfc-9334-verifier`.
- **SPEC row `password-vault-usb` (planned)**: the USB transport carries the five per-user vault verbs (`PasswordVaultStatus`, `PasswordVaultEnroll`, `PasswordVaultRotate`, `PasswordVaultRemoveFactor`, `PasswordVaultRecover`) to the paired phone, with the `transport` request and response types as params and results. The row answers the seven design questions of xkey-android #15: the xkey CLI calls it through a `usb://` scheme, and the phone's embedded xkmsd runs the `pkg/staticpw` vault keyed to the paired desktop's Noise static key. Every `pkg/staticpw` factor is accepted, passkey PRF is checked by the unwrap, and the recovery code is `pkg/staticpw`'s (owner item 148 (a), ruling 130; consumers xkey-android #15 and #55). Docs: `docs/password-vault/architecture.md` §"Design decisions (#15)", `docs/password-vault/api.md` §"USB transport: vault verbs (planned)".
- **`remote.createBackup` and `remote.restoreBackup` take a password (#1693)** — both params carry a required `password`. The xkey bridge derives the backup key exactly as `xkey backup` does: `backup.NewPasswordKey` on create, and on restore the envelope's KDF record through `backup.DerivePasswordKey`. A phone-made backup therefore opens on the laptop, and the reverse, with the same password. An empty password is refused as invalid params (`ErrBackupPasswordRequired`). A wrong password or malformed envelope is refused as a restore failure, and nothing is written. A backup that includes the OATH or password store needs the same desktop export decision as `remote.sync*` (`--allow-sync`, overridden by a sealed enterprise policy), taken before either store is read. The restore result's new `items` field reports each category's restored and skipped counts and per-entry errors. `success` is true only when no entry was skipped. Restored trust-store certificates are phone-supplied, so they are quarantined under `PurposeSynced`, the same as synced certificates, and reported as `quarantined` rather than `restored`. A response larger than one transport message is refused with `-32040` `ErrorCodeMessageTooLarge`, which asks for fewer categories. The pairing router now answers a request whose response it cannot send with an error, instead of only logging the failure. The bridge archives and restores the trust store, OATH and password stores that `xkey device listen` opens for sync. The live `remote.oath*` handlers share that OATH store instance, so a credential added over `remote.oathAdd` is in the next backup and a restored one is served at once. It reads the CA category from xkmsd. `remote.listBackups` still reports the feature unavailable. Docs: `xkey/docs/phone-hsm/engineering.md`.
- **Per-repository signing keys (go-xkms#1697).** A tenant's images and
  signed CoRIM verify under its release key (`release-signing`) unless a
  binding names another tenant key for the repository. The bindings are kept
  in the qrdb DAO database `attestation`. A CoRIM that names a repository,
  and an image verified with `image.VerifierConfig.SigningKeys`, must be
  signed by that repository's key. Anything else is refused with
  `ErrSigningKeyRefused` or `image.ErrSigningKeyMismatch`. `XKMSService`
  serves set, get, list, delete and resolve on the caller's tenant over REST
  (`/api/v1/attestation/signing-keys`), gRPC, Unix, QUIC, MCP
  (`attestation.signing_key.*`) and embedded. They are gated by the new
  permissions `attestation_signing_keys:{bind,get,list}`, which the service
  enforces as well as the wire gate. `sdk/go` re-exports the types under an
  `Attestation` prefix, and the TypeScript SDK adds `client.signingKeys`.
  Code: `pkg/attestation/appraisal/signing_keys.go`,
  `pkg/xkms/servicer_signing_keys.go`; docs:
  `docs/attestation-verifier/architecture.md#repository-signing-keys`.
- **Transparency log checkpoints as C2SP signed notes, with a registrable signature algorithm (#1546)** — `pkg/ca/checkpoint`, re-exported as `sdk/go/checkpoint`, encodes and strictly parses the c2sp.org/tlog-checkpoint body and signs and opens it as a c2sp.org/signed-note (owner ruling 122). It also builds and parses verifier keys. Open ignores unknown keys and refuses a known key's bad signature or a note with no verified signature. Signing goes only through a `crypto.Signer`, and the algorithm follows from the key: Ed25519 (`0x01`) and witness ECDSA (`0x02`) use their assigned type bytes; ECDSA P-224 and digest-bound P-384/P-521, RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS, and ML-DSA-44/65/87 use `0xff || len || identifier`. `Register` adds an application's own algorithm and refuses duplicates and reserved type bytes. The tests include the specification's Ed25519 known-answer vector. Docs: `docs/transparency-log/engineering.md`.

### Changed

CI: a push to main no longer cancels the main run still in progress; integration jobs run on the bigdisk runners.
CI: the Security Scan job's timeout is 30 minutes, since gosec takes 9 to 15 minutes on the minis and omega and the 15-minute limit failed runs 64485, 64577 and 64578 (Infra #1206).
- **Wire change for go-quicbaas and trusted-firmware: the OTA image signature is RFC 9053 §2.1 fixed-width `r || s` (ruling 136)** — `SignOTAImage` (REST `POST /api/v1/ota-image-keys/{board}/sign`, gRPC/Unix `SignOTAImage`, MCP `xkms.signOTAImage`, the SDK and `xkmsctl key ota-image sign`) now returns the OTA_AUTH signature as 32-byte big-endian `r` then 32-byte big-endian `s`, each left-padded with zeros: 64 bytes for ES256, where it returned ASN.1 DER. The 328P and 32U4 boards carry no DER parser. A backend signature that does not convert is refused with `ErrOTASignatureEncoding`. Every other signature, the generic sign on the same board key included, stays DER. Docs: `docs/key-management/engineering.md#per-board-ota-image-keys`.

### Fixed

- **Host and container appraisal keep AK intermediates.** `HostEvidence` and `ContainerEvidence` gain `AKIntermediates`, which `AppraiseHost` forwards after the AK certificate, so an attestation key issued by an intermediate CA now chains to a tenant's root-only `ak-root` endorsement instead of failing as forged. A nil intermediate is refused with `ErrInvalidAKIntermediate` (`sdk/go`: `ErrAttestationInvalidAKIntermediate`). (#1608)

- **Make targets read `GO_BUILD_TAGS`.** `make lint|build|coverage|security|integration-test GO_BUILD_TAGS='a b'`, as ci-template calls them, now adds those tags to every `-tags` / `--build-tags` list the target already uses (comma-joined, duplicates dropped; gosec and govulncheck gain `-tags`), so tag-gated code is compiled, linted and covered in CI. One join, `scripts/go-build-tags.mk`, shared by the root Makefile and `xkey/Makefile`; an empty or unset `GO_BUILD_TAGS` leaves every command line unchanged. `test/scripts/go-build-tags.test.sh` (run by `make test-scripts`) checks it. (#1603)

## [0.63.0-alpha] - 2026-10-23

### Added

- **Issuer-stamped fleet agent claim (go-xkms#1686).** `SignOptions.FleetAgent`
  stamps `tp-fleetAgent` (1.3.6.1.4.1.29377.101.25, non-critical, value NULL)
  into the certificate, and only the issuing call sets it. Every CSR path
  refuses a CSR that requests the extension with `ErrFleetAgentClaimRequested`:
  400 on REST, `InvalidArgument` on gRPC and unix, invalid params on MCP.
  `ExtraExtensions` may not carry it either (`ErrFleetAgentClaimReserved`).
  `VerifyFleetAgentClaim` accepts the claim only on a certificate that chains
  to roots the caller supplies, so another CA's claim is rejected. `sdk/go`
  re-exports the option, the verifier, `OIDFleetAgent` and the
  `ErrCAFleetAgentClaim*` errors for go-quicbaas fleet enrolment
  (go-quicbaas#1821). Code: `pkg/ca/fleet_agent.go`; docs:
  `docs/certificate-authority/engineering.md#fleet-agent-claim`.

## [0.62.0-alpha] - 2026-10-23

### Security

- **BREAKING: factor proofs bind go-qrdb's ChallengeMessage** (#1684). The `mtls`, `pkcs11` and `piv` factors no longer verify a signature over SHA-256 of the bare nonce. They verify a signature over `qrdbsdk.QuorumChallengeMessage(ChallengeID, purpose, Nonce)`, built by the new `pkg/factor/internal/challenge.Message`. The purpose is `MethodData[qrdbsdk.QuorumChallengePurposeKey]` (`""` when none), the same value go-qrdb's own `mtls` factor reads. A proof therefore binds the challenge ID and the quorum purpose, and a proof made for one purpose no longer answers a challenge for another with the same nonce. Each of the three factors now refuses a challenge with an empty nonce. The prover is `qrdbsdk.SignQuorumChallenge`. `piv.Factor.SignNonce` is replaced by `SignChallenge(ctx, slot, challengeID, purpose, nonce)`, which refuses an empty nonce with the new `EmptyNonceError`. There is no compatibility path: a signature over the bare nonce is refused. The `fido2` factor is unchanged, because its WebAuthn challenge is the nonce. Docs: `docs/auth-factors/api.md`, `docs/auth-factors/engineering.md`.

## [0.61.0-alpha] - 2026-10-23

### Added

- **ACME CT precertificates and SCT embedding at finalize** — with a CT log enabled under `acme.ct` (xkmsd and the TrustedCA), finalize submits each precertificate to every enabled log (RFC 6962 §4.2 add-pre-chain), waits for all logs, verifies each SCT, enforces `min_scts`, `min_operators` and `require_rfc6962_log`, and embeds the verified SCTs in the final certificate as the RFC 6962 §3.3 SCT list extension; each submission is audited as `CERTIFICATE_TRANSPARENCY`, an unmet policy fails issuance with a `serverInternal` problem (RFC 8555 §6.7) whose detail names the unmet requirement and whether a log refused or timed out (never a log's URL), and submissions run behind the `acme.resilience.ct_submitter` circuit breaker. EK certificates (endorse-01) and TCG-CSR-IDEVID IAK/IDevID certificates are never CT-logged (RFC 6962 §1; TCG DevID v1.1 §3.11, §11); device-attest-01 certificates are logged when CT is enabled. Files: pkg/acme/issuance, pkg/acme/ct, pkg/acme/ct/cttest, pkg/acme/server/handlers, pkg/acme/server/circuitbreaker, pkg/config/acme_ct.go, cmd/xkmsd/acme.go, pkg/acme/client/trustedca.go; docs docs/acme-issuance/engineering.md (#745).
- **ACME CT verifies every SCT and is enabled per log** — `pkg/acme/ct` verifies each SCT's RFC 6962 §3.2 signature over the precert_entry (including Precertificate Signing Certificate chains) and refuses a wrong log ID, an unsupported algorithm or a bad signature with typed errors. Each log is configured with its URL, public key, a log ID derived from the key and an `Enabled` flag; CT is off when no log is enabled, and invalid or duplicate logs are refused. `MockLogSubmitter` moved to test code. (#745)
- **ACME finalize issues through `pkg/acme/issuance`: goodkey, a reserved serial, and linted precertificate and certificate** — a weak CSR key is refused as `badPublicKey`; the CA lints each tbsCertificate with zlint before signing it (CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements §4.3.1.2), refusing an error or fatal finding as `badCSR` and logging and auditing warnings (`CERTIFICATE_LINTED`); the precertificate and the certificate share one reserved serial and must match apart from the RFC 6962 §3.1 poison and SCT list extensions. xkmsd runs `linter.PrivatePKIConfig` plus the operator's `acme.lint.exclude_lints` / `exclude_sources`. The CA's default key usage asserts `keyEncipherment` for RSA subject keys only (RFC 5480 §3, RFC 8410 §5). Files: `pkg/acme/issuance`, `pkg/acme/linter`, `pkg/acme/goodkey`, `pkg/ca`, `pkg/acme/server/handlers`, `pkg/config/acme.go`, `cmd/xkmsd/acme.go`; docs `docs/acme-issuance/engineering.md` (#744).
- **Key policy and crypto utilities in `xkms.v1`.** go-quicbaas served key policy and crypto utilities over its own `quicbaas.kms.v1` services, which wrapped the go-xkms library; with those wrappers unregistered its clients failed with `unknown service`. `xkms.v1` KeystoreService now serves the crypto utilities (Rewrap, EncryptBatch, DecryptBatch, GenerateDataKey, GenerateWrappedDataKey, GenerateHMAC, VerifyHMAC, GenerateRandom, Hash) on gRPC, unix, REST, QUIC, MCP and the embedded transport, each with its permission and tenant-scoped, reachable through `sdk/go` for go-quicbaas to re-export; a hash or HMAC the standard library refuses under `GODEBUG=fips140=only` fails with a typed InvalidArgument error. It also serves the key-management RPCs the same way: GetPublicKey, RevokeKey, UpdateKeyStatus, Get/UpdateKeyMetadata, Set/Get/DeleteKeyPolicy, Set/Get/DeleteKeyRotationPolicy, Set/ClearKeySafety, SafetyCheck, SafetyReport, GetSupportedAlgorithms, BackendStatus and BackendTest. Key policies, rotation policies, AEAD usage limits (NIST SP 800-38D §8.3, RFC 8439 §4), status and metadata persist in the go-qrdb datastore through the `pkg/keypolicy` DAO store, and a service without that store refuses them with a typed Unavailable error. Every key-use path is admitted through the key's status and policy: sign, verify, encrypt, decrypt, MAC, seal, unseal, derive, ECDH, wrap and unwrap by ID, and export, export of key material, copy and the key a wrap releases refuse a revoked or disabled key and an operation its policy does not allow, and wrapping under an AES-GCM key counts toward its usage limits; a key whose policy restricts its operations is never exported. AEAD usage counters belong to one key version, so a rotation racing an encryption never erases a use charged to the new version; deleting a key deletes its policy record, so a key created again under the same ID starts enabled with no inherited metadata, limits or counters; BackendTest never creates the default sealing key (a backend without one is refused with a typed error) and admits its seal and unseal through the key's status, policy and usage count. GetPublicKey returns the public key of a cloud KMS key whose private key never leaves the KMS, and of an X25519 key. GetSupportedAlgorithms and the Algorithms RPC both list the key algorithms each backend declares in its capabilities (`types.KeyAlgorithms`: RSA sizes, ECDSA curves, Ed25519, X25519, AEADs, HMAC hashes, ML-DSA and ML-KEM parameter sets) instead of expanding generic capability flags, so they agree, Azure Key Vault no longer advertises Ed25519 and AWS KMS lists AES-256-GCM only; under `GODEBUG=fips140=only` GetSupportedAlgorithms leaves out ChaCha20-Poly1305, XChaCha20-Poly1305 and X25519. DEK management is go-qrdb's `DEKClient` (#1681).
- **Trust write permissions `trust:publish_dane` and `trust:auto_import_aia`.** go-xkms assigned no permission to DANE TLSA publication or AIA issuer import, so a consumer serving those verbs (go-quicbaas's `POST /api/v1/trust/publish-dane` and `/api/v1/trust/auto-import-aia`) had to refuse them on every transport. `pkg/auth` now declares `ResourceTrust` with `ActionPublishDANE` and `ActionAutoImportAIA`; the service module registers both, cross-scoped and of governance duty, and grants them to Admin (and so Owner), like the `trust_roots` writes. sdk/go re-exports the names as `PermissionResourceTrust`, `PermissionActionPublishDANE` and `PermissionActionAutoImportAIA`. go-xkms's own REST, gRPC and MCP surfaces serve neither verb. (`pkg/auth/permissions.go`, `pkg/apimodule/module_grants.go`, `pkg/apimodule/module_scopes.go`, `sdk/go/permissions.go`, `docs/rbac/architecture.md`; #1674)
- **`xkmsctl acme gui` hosts the desktop ACME admin GUI (`gui` build tag).** `pkg/acme/gui/admin` had no host binary since go-trusted-ca's `cactl` was never migrated. `xkmsctl acme gui` opens the Wails window, connected through the same SDK client and `--acme-server`/`--acme-transport`/`--tls-*` flags as every other `acme` verb, and refuses a missing server (`ACMEAdminAddressRequiredError`) or mTLS identity (`ACMEGUIIdentityRequiredError`) before connecting. The verb is compiled only with `-tags gui`; `make build-cli-gui` builds it (cgo, webkit2gtk-4.1). The default `xkmsctl` is unchanged. The window's Linux program name is now `xkmsctl`. The desktop router now serves the ACME admin API's paths, which the embedded admin SPA calls: `/admin/{status,stats,certificates,accounts,orders}` replace `/api/v1/{status,stats,certificates,accounts,orders}`, intermediate-CA status moves to `PUT /api/v1/tenants/{id}/intermediate-cas/{caId}/status`, `/admin/certificates` takes `expires_days`, and the routes the SPA never called (`/certificates/expiring`, listing and getting intermediate CAs, getting one EAB) are gone. `GET /admin/audit` and `PUT /api/v1/tenants/{id}/default-intermediate-ca` stay unserved on the desktop until the SDK has operations for them. (`cmd/xkmsctl/acme_gui.go`, `cmd/xkmsctl/acme.go`, `pkg/acme/gui/admin/api/router.go`, `docs/acme-issuance/cli.md`, `docs/acme/gui/admin/api.md`; #746)

### Changed

- **A CSR-signed login certificate carries the caller's tenant SPIFFE SAN** (go-xkms#1602, #1622): with a trust domain configured, `SignCSR` under the `client` profile or no profile stamps `spiffe://<tenant>/user/<CN>` for the authenticated caller's tenant, so go-qrdb login derives the tenant from the certificate. Other profiles (`code-signing`, `server`, ...) get the SAN only when the request names a tenant, so code-signing and server CSRs, including an empty or wildcard CN, issue without an explicit tenant.
- **go-qrdb v0.51.0-alpha** (#1635): the tenant is now the SPIFFE trust domain, so issued SANs take go-qrdb's `spiffe://<tenantID>/<kind>/<name>` form, and PIV login and ACME admin mTLS bind the tenant through `TenantFromClientCert`'s two-value form, which requires the OU and the SAN to name the same tenant. A certificate logs in only when its first OU and its SPIFFE ID SAN name the same tenant: OU-only and SAN-only certificates are refused, and there is no implicit system tenant. A system identity is OU `system` plus `spiffe://system/user/<cn>`. Tenant names must be valid SPIFFE trust-domain names. `ca.SignOptions.RawSubjectURIs` carries the ceremony's SPIFFE ID onto raw-subject holder certificates, and the init CA adapter refuses to issue a login certificate without a SPIFFE trust domain (`ErrNoSPIFFETrustDomain`).
- **The `x509-svid` profile refuses a SPIFFE ID whose trust domain is not the tenant** (go-xkms#1602): the one URI SAN must be `spiffe://<tenant>/...`, the tenant being the subject's OU[0], so a tenant's SVID subordinate is name-constrained to its own trust domain. Tenant SPIFFE synthesis under a cluster trust domain that names the tenant fails with `ErrSigningFailed` wrapping `spiffe.ErrTenantIsClusterTrustDomain`. SPEC: trust-domain-grammar.
- **xkey authorizes audit reads over go-qrdb RBAC instead of uid 0** (go-xkms#1605): `AdminService.GetAuditLogs` and `ExportAuditLogs` ask the go-qrdb authorizer set with `SetAuthorizer` whether the go-qrdb identity bound to the request context holds `audit:read`. A missing authorizer, a missing identity or a denial refuses with `*AuditReadDeniedError`, which matches `ErrAdminNotAuthorized` and unwraps to the authorizer's denial. The uid-0 `IsAdmin` and its Wails binding are removed. `sdk/go` re-exports go-qrdb's `Authorizer`, `Identity`, `PermissionAuditRead` and the identity and permission helpers as `QRDB*`. SPEC: authz-xkey-uid0.
- **BREAKING (wire): the xkey pairing protocol carries a `generation` on every request and response** (#128), closing duplicate-response cross-talk between requests that reuse an `id`. This is a flag day with `jeremyhahn/xkey-android#10`. `pairingproto.Request` and `pairingproto.Response` (`pkg/pairingproto/protocol.go`, re-exported by `sdk/go/pairingproto`) gain `Generation uint64` (JSON `generation`). `MessageRouter.SendRequest` assigns it from a per-connection counter that starts at 1 and never repeats. `routeResponse` delivers a response only when both `id` and `generation` match; it drops and logs at `Warn` a stale or missing (`0`) generation. Every Go responder echoes the request's generation, including on errors: `Bridge.HandleRequest`, `xkey device listen` (`cmd/xkey/cmd/device_listen_handler.go`) and the phone-role test fakes. `EncodeResponse` and `EncodeErrorResponse` take a `generation` argument. Generation matching replaces the abandoned-ID tombstone from #39/#66, so `retired`, `maxRetiredIDs` and `ErrTooManyAbandonedRequests` are deleted; `ErrDuplicateRequestID` is unchanged. There is no compatibility path: an unpatched peer's responses are all dropped and its requests time out. Docs: `xkey/docs/device/api.md`, `xkey/docs/phone-hsm/architecture.md`, `xkey/docs/phone-hsm/engineering.md`.

### Fixed

- **The `xkmsd init` admin certificate authenticates on gRPC, MCP and unix, not only REST and QUIC (go-xkms#794).** The unified listener now carries its client-CA pool, the init ceremony root among it, as the static `ClientCAs` that go-qrdb's client-trust pool verifies every client chain against, so the node's mTLS authenticator accepts the bound admin on every transport. `/api/v1/auth/me` reports `auth_method: mtls` for an identity that mTLS authenticated. The SPIFFE trust domain the CA issues under is resolved in one place and always pinned on the node. Docs: `docs/init-ceremony/architecture.md`.
- **SDK clients and `xkmsctl` send the `xkmsd init` admin certificate (go-xkms#794).** `xkmsd run` advertises the init ceremony root from `<datastore.path>/ca-bundle.pem` among its client CAs, so a static client-certificate list no longer withholds the init-issued admin certificate; identity still binds by SPKI thumbprint. A present but unparsable bundle, or a malformed `tls.ca_file`/`tls.client_cas`, now fails start-up instead of being skipped. Docs: `docs/init-ceremony/architecture.md`.
- **A FIPS GCM refusal is no longer reported as a server fault.** Under `GODEBUG=fips140=only`, an AES-GCM request with a caller-supplied nonce or a truncated tag is refused (`ErrArbitraryIVGCMUnavailable`), and so is a tag size outside NIST SP 800-38D §5.2.1.2 in any mode. These refusals now reach the caller as a client-correctable error on every transport: gRPC `InvalidArgument`, REST `400`, MCP Invalid params. Before, gRPC and MCP returned `Internal` and REST returned `500`. All three read one classification, `apierrors.AEADSentinelClasses`. See `docs/fips/gcm-sites.md` (part of #23).
- **The Go SDK re-exports the Noise FIPS refusal.** `sdk/go/bootstrap` now carries `ErrNoiseFIPSUnsupported`, the typed error every Noise key and session entry point returns under `GODEBUG=fips140=only`, so a consumer recognises the X25519 refusal with `errors.Is` without importing `pkg/trust/bootstrap`. The `sdk/go/bootstrap` Noise composition test and the `sdk/go/client/ssh` session-dial tests on every transport assert the refusal (a typed `*session.HandshakeError` for the curve25519 key exchange) under `fips140=only` and the round trip under `fips140=off` (part of #23).
- **Running under `GODEBUG=fips140=only` no longer crashes or seals with a refused GCM.** xkmsctl FROST dealer packages are sealed as JWE `ECDH-ES+A256KW` / `A256CBC-HS512` (RFC 7518 §5.2.5) rather than `A256GCM`, because go-jose seals GCM under its own arbitrary IV, which the FIPS module refuses; packages sealed with `A256GCM` no longer import, so re-export them. The personal-vault HKDF (`pkg/staticpw`) uses stdlib `crypto/hkdf`, so a secret under 112 bits, such as a mistyped recovery code, is a `*VaultCryptoError` instead of a panic. Tests that exercise X25519 (Noise NK in `pkg/trust/bootstrap`, `pkg/pairingproto`, `pkg/trust/clusterca`, `xkmsctl bootstrap noise`) or arbitrary-IV GCM (vault BYOK, Azure Key Vault nonces) assert the stdlib refusal under fips140=only and the round trip outside it, through the new `fipstest.OutsideFIPSAfterRefusal`. See `docs/fips/gcm-sites.md` (part of #23).
- **PKCS#11 refusals under `GODEBUG=fips140=only` (go-xkms#23).** The PKCS#11 module refuses exactly what the Go standard library refuses (HKDF `C_DeriveKey`, unhashed `CKM_RSA_PKCS` Sign/SignRecover and caller-IV `CKM_AES_GCM`), returning `CKR_MECHANISM_INVALID` or `CKR_MECHANISM_PARAM_INVALID`.
- **The `pkcs11test` mock refuses explicit-IV AES-GCM decrypt under `GODEBUG=fips140=only` with a typed error.** `CryptoMockClient.Decrypt` returns `aead.ErrArbitraryIVGCMUnavailable` instead of the raw `crypto/cipher` text when the request's `GCMNonceMode` is not random, and checks the nonce length first, so a malformed request reports `ErrInvalidNonceSize` in either mode. A sweep of every root-module package under `fips140=only` found no other failure outside `pkg/pkcs11` and `pkg/ssh/console`; see `docs/fips/README.md` (part of #23).
- **The AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault and PKCS#11 backend suites pass under `GODEBUG=fips140=only`.** These backends run the SHA-1 signatures, PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption and SHA-1 RSA-OAEP that the remote KMS or token performs, so the tests' software oracles stand in for that remote party and run outside the local module's enforcement (`fips140.WithoutEnforcement`). A local SHA-1 wrap (Azure `RSA_AES_KEY_WRAP_SHA_1`, PKCS#11 `WrapKey`) is checked to fail with the stdlib's refusal. The AWS KMS nil-options decrypt test checks that the backend asks KMS for `RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256` (part of #23).
- **The xkey module reports the stdlib's refusals under `GODEBUG=fips140=only`.** The OATH SHA-1 and short-key gate keys on `crypto/fips140.Enforced`, the flag `crypto/hmac` checks, so SHA-1 HOTP/TOTP still work under `fips140=on`. The browser-extension handshake (`NewSessionCrypto`) and the phone TCP pairing server (`NewTCPPairingServer`) now wrap the stdlib's X25519 refusal instead of dropping it. Tests that run X25519 (Noise in `xkey/pkg/phone`, `pairing`, `attestation`, `attesttest`, `e2eprobe`; nativemsg; the sshechod curve25519 key exchange; the `xkey device relay` command tests) assert the refusal under `fips140=only` and the round trip outside it. The `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd` device-resolution and OATH multi-backend tests no longer run X25519 or SHA-1 incidentally. The GUI phone service joins its pairing and connect errors with the cause, so the Noise refusal reaches the caller, and `ParseCertificate` leaves the SHA-1 and MD5 fingerprints empty under `fips140=only`. The `xkey/pkg/gui` and `xkey/pkg/gui/services` tests assert the Noise, NSS database and native-messaging refusals, echo `GCMNonceMode` over the PKCS#11 IPC round trip, expect the FIPS-aware password-backup KDF and seed OATH with HMAC-SHA-256. See `docs/fips/xkey.md` (part of #23).
- **The SSH console's `Dial` returns a typed `*console.DialError` when the connection or SSH handshake fails (go-xkms#23).** Under `GODEBUG=fips140=only` the `curve25519-sha256` key exchange fails when `crypto/ecdh` refuses X25519; `Dial` now wraps that refusal, and every other dial or handshake failure, in `*console.DialError` instead of passing the `pkg/ssh/session` error through bare. The cause stays reachable through `errors.Is` and `errors.As`.
- **The SSH console refuses the WebSocket upgrade under `fips140=only` instead of panicking (go-xkms#23).** RFC 6455 §4.2.2 requires SHA-1 for the `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` header, which the Go Cryptographic Module refuses under `GODEBUG=fips140=only`. The `pkg/ssh/console` handler now asks `crypto/sha1` before the upgrade and answers `501 Not Implemented` with a typed `*console.UpgradeRefusedError`; outside `fips140=only` the console is unchanged.
- **`pkg/ssh/session`'s `DialClient` returns the SSH handshake error without a stray closed-connection error (go-xkms#23).** `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` closes the connection itself when the handshake fails, so the second `Close` returned `net.ErrClosed` ("use of closed network connection"), which was joined to the `*session.HandshakeError`. That expected error is now dropped, so under `GODEBUG=fips140=only` the caller sees only the module's X25519 refusal; any other close error is still returned.
- **`ek create` after a TPM clear no longer refuses with "carry no creation template".** A successful TPM2_Clear (TCG TPM 2.0 Part 3 §24.6) through `Clear`, `ClearForReprovision` (LOCKOUT or PLATFORM) or `FactoryResetWithClear` now drops every cached Owner and Endorsement hierarchy value in `pkg/tpm2`: the EK, IAK, IDevID, LAK, SSRK and Platform SRK attributes and the EK public keys. `EKAttributes()` re-derives the EK from the config, with its TCG default creation template, instead of returning the pre-clear value. `FactoryReset` drops the same set, the EK values included. A refused clear leaves the cache as it was (#1667).
- **`xkmsd run` starts with the admin module, and starts again after `xkmsd init` (go-xkms#794).** Core is now the only owner of tenant create, list, get and delete at `/api/v1/tenants`, behind the tenant gate. The admin module keeps tenant update, status and the CA, EAB, roles and users sub-resources, so the duplicate route registration no longer panics at start-up. `xkmsd init` now seeds the built-in roles with the xkms role grants, so first boot on `xkmsd run` adopts the existing admin role instead of failing with `role: name already exists`.

## [0.60.0-alpha] - 2026-10-22

### Added

- **`xkey oath` stores credentials per backend (`--backend`).** The CLI and the GUI now open OATH as a `CompositeStore` with one partition per OATH-capable backend in the unified config (`software`, plus every `backends.local` entry of category `software` or `pkcs11`, via `backendregistry.ConfiguredFor`). `xkey oath add --backend <id>` stores the credential in that backend; without it the credential goes to `backends.defaults.oath`, else `software`. `list`, `generate` and `remove` reach every backend, and `list` shows each credential's backend. An unknown backend is refused with a typed `*oath.BackendError` naming it, and a name or ID already held by any backend is refused. The `software` partition is the historical location (`oath/` barrier keys, `oath.json`), so existing credentials keep working; other backends use `oath@<id>/` keys or a `<stem>@<id><ext>` file beside the store file (`oath@token1.json` beside `oath.json`; `--store /tmp/a.json` gets `/tmp/a@token1.json`), and a store path whose file name contains `@` is refused with `oath.ErrInvalidStorePath`. One constructor, `oath.OpenStores`, opens the partitions for the CLI, the GUI, `xkey extension serve` and `xkey backup`: backups carry every partition and record each credential's backend, and restore returns it to that backend. `CompositeStore.Add` holds its write lock across the duplicate check and the insertion, so concurrent adds of one name to two backends cannot both succeed. New `xkey/pkg/oath/backends.go` (`OpenStores`, `FilePartitionPath`), `xkey/pkg/backendregistry/capabilities.go`; wired in `cmd/xkey/cmd/oath.go`, `backup.go`, `extension_serve.go` and `pkg/gui/app.go`. Tested by `oath_multibackend_864_test.go`, `backends_test.go`, `capabilities_test.go`. (#864)

### Changed

- **go-qrdb v0.51.0-alpha** (#1635): the tenant is now the SPIFFE trust domain, so issued SANs take go-qrdb's `spiffe://<tenantID>/<kind>/<name>` form, and PIV login and ACME admin mTLS bind the tenant through `TenantFromClientCert`'s two-value form, which requires the OU and the SAN to name the same tenant. A certificate logs in only when its first OU and its SPIFFE ID SAN name the same tenant: OU-only and SAN-only certificates are refused, and there is no implicit system tenant. A system identity is OU `system` plus `spiffe://system/user/<cn>`. Tenant names must be valid SPIFFE trust-domain names. `ca.SignOptions.RawSubjectURIs` carries the ceremony's SPIFFE ID onto raw-subject holder certificates, and the init CA adapter refuses to issue a login certificate without a SPIFFE trust domain (`ErrNoSPIFFETrustDomain`).

### Fixed

- **SDK clients and `xkmsctl` send the `xkmsd init` admin certificate (go-xkms#794).** `xkmsd run` advertises the init ceremony root from `<datastore.path>/ca-bundle.pem` among its client CAs, so a static client-certificate list no longer withholds the init-issued admin certificate; identity still binds by SPKI thumbprint. A present but unparsable bundle, or a malformed `tls.ca_file`/`tls.client_cas`, now fails start-up instead of being skipped. Docs: `docs/init-ceremony/architecture.md`.

## [0.59.0-alpha] - 2026-10-21

### Added

- **`rest.HostConfig.AuditLogger` (go-xkms#1618).** A module hosted through `rest.NewHostServer` records its login audit events, refusal reasons included, to the host's `qrdbsdk.NodeAuditLogger`; nil records none, as before. Docs: `docs/host-embedding/engineering.md`.

### Fixed

WrapKeyByID refuses a stored target that is not an exportable symmetric key with `ErrWrapTarget` (`ErrWrapTargetNotSymmetric`, invalid-argument / 400); AES-KW, AES-KWP and AES-GCM unwrap failures match `ErrUnwrapCiphertextRejected`; the symmetric backend lists keys that have both a tenant and a partition (#1634).

## [0.58.0-alpha] - 2026-10-21

### Security

Go toolchain 1.27.3 for GO-2026-6809, crypto/x509 intermediate distrust.

### Added

- **One ES256 OTA image-signing key per trusted-firmware board id.**
  `XKMSService.CreateOTAImageKey`, `RotateOTAImageKey` and `SignOTAImage`
  (`pkg/xkms/ota_image_keys.go`) map a board id to the key `ota-image-<board>`
  and create, rotate and sign through the existing key-management path, so a
  rotated board key keeps verifying the images its earlier versions signed. A
  malformed board id is refused with `ErrInvalidBoardID` and any algorithm or
  key other than ECDSA P-256 with `ErrOTAImageAlgorithm` (#1606). REST serves
  them at `POST /api/v1/ota-image-keys/{board}`, `.../rotate` and `.../sign`,
  gRPC as the `CreateOTAImageKey`, `RotateOTAImageKey` and `SignOTAImage`
  RPCs, and MCP as `xkms.createOTAImageKey`, `xkms.rotateOTAImageKey` and
  `xkms.signOTAImage`, under the `keys:create`, `keys:rotate` and `keys:sign`
  permissions; both refusals are a 400, `InvalidArgument` or JSON-RPC -32602.
  xkey reaches them through the SDK as `xkey key ota-image create`, `rotate`
  and `sign`, with the same flags and output as xkmsctl.

### Changed

- **xkey backups are sealed with AES-256-GCM, so they work under FIPS 140-3 (#23).** The backup envelope moves to version 3: the archive is sealed with AES-256-GCM under a fresh random 96-bit nonce (`cipher.NewGCMWithRandomNonce`, NIST SP 800-38D §8.2.2) instead of XChaCha20-Poly1305, which `GODEBUG=fips140=only` refuses. The header stays the AEAD additional data and the password KDF is unchanged (Argon2id, or PBKDF2-SHA256 in FIPS mode). Version 2 (XChaCha20-Poly1305) files are refused with `backup.ErrVersionMismatch` and are not migrated; re-create them. `xkey/pkg/backup/service.go`, golden fixture `xkey/pkg/backup/testdata/backup-v3.golden.json`.

### Fixed

PIV login resolves a tenant user's certificate in the tenant the certificate names, not the system tenant (#1628).

## [0.57.0-alpha] - 2026-10-19

### Security

- **A cluster node's transport key now lives in the backend `KeyBackend` names, or the node refuses to provision.** The key used to resolve through CA key custody, which falls back to software. That let a node configured for `pkcs11` mint a disk-backed software key under a certificate that claimed PKCS#11 provenance. `clusterca.Options.NodeKeyBackends` (built by `clusterca.NewNodeKeyBackends`) is now required. It resolves `software` to the node-local store, `tpm2` to the TPM, and any other name to the daemon backend of that name. A backend the node lacks fails with `*clusterca.ErrKeyBackendUnavailable` wrapping `*clusterca.ErrNodeKeyBackendNotConfigured` or `*clusterca.ErrNoTPM`. A restarted local-CA `tpm2` node now reloads its own named transport key instead of the IDevID. Only an ACME joiner signs with the IDevID, and its certificate must match `IDevID()` (go-xkms#1381).
- **A `pkcs11` transport key opens its token before the qrdb node starts.** Raft mTLS is provisioned before the backend registry exists, so `raft_enrollment.key_backend: pkcs11` was always refused. xkmsd now opens `backends.pkcs11` before the node with the TPM-sealed PIN (`xkmsd seal-pkcs11-pin`). The barrier-held configured PIN is not open yet at that point. The backend registry reuses that one login. `clusterca.NodeKeyBackendsParams.Hardware` is now a `map[string]types.KeyProvider`. A token that cannot be opened, or a missing sealed PIN, is a startup error. Software never stands in.
- **A client certificate's OU no longer grants roles; it names only the tenant.** The ACME admin plane's REST and gRPC mTLS paths now share one resolver, `admin.MTLSAuthHandler`: the tenant is the one `qrdbsdk.TenantFromClientCert` names, and the roles are those of the go-qrdb user the certificate binds to. A user of another tenant is refused with `*admin.CertificateTenantMismatchError`. Breaking: `admin.MTLSAuthMiddleware`, `MTLSAuthConfig` and `NewMTLSAuthMiddleware` are removed. `server.UnaryMTLSIdentityInterceptor` now takes an `*admin.MTLSAuthHandler` (set through `ServerConfig.MTLSAuth`) in place of an authenticator and a role extractor. A certificate whose OU named a role such as `Admin` now gets only its bound user's roles (go-xkms#1557). SPEC: authz-cert-ou-roles.
- **TPM 2.0 device enrollment no longer panics under `GODEBUG=fips140=only` (#1591).** go-tpm v0.9.8 encrypts session parameters with AES-CFB, which `crypto/cipher` refuses in FIPS 140-only mode, so provisioning, `CreateIDevID` and every other parameter-encrypted TPM command panicked (`tpm2/sessions.go:634`). go-tpm is now pinned to the `jeremyhahn/go-tpm` fork at `v0.9.9-0.20261015005355-56ec25c36102` (go-tpm#2, FIPS-approved parameter encryption) by a `replace` in `go.mod`, `sdk/go`, `xkey` and `web/desktop`, per the owner ruling of 2026-10-14; the pin is dropped once the fix lands upstream. A `replace` does not reach consumers: go-quicbaas, go-trusted-platform and any other module that builds go-xkms needs the same `replace`. `TestFIPS140Only_IDevIDSignerSignsWithTheTPMKey` (`pkg/tpm2`, `tpm_simulator`) re-runs provisioning, `CreateIDevID` and an IDevID and IAK signature in a `fips140=only` child process on every simulator run.
- **A SHA-1 PCR bank returns an error under `GODEBUG=fips140=only` instead of panicking (#1591).** `pkg/tpm2.GetHashFunction` asks the Go Cryptographic Module whether it refuses the algorithm and returns `*tpm2.HashRefusedError` for SHA-1, so `ExtendPCR` (which used to ignore the refused write and return the digest of nothing) and `TPM2.ExtendPCR` (which panicked in `crypto/sha1.Sum`) now both return it, as do `PCRCompositeDigest`, `ComputePolicyPCRDigest` and `CalculateName`. `CalculatePCRs` leaves a refused bank empty, as it does for SM3_256.

### Changed

- **The TrustedCA is go-qrdb's cluster CA, signing through its `crypto.Signer`.** When `ca` is configured, xkmsd hands the TrustedCA to the qrdb node as Key A through `WithClusterCAKeyProvider` on standalone nodes and on every cluster whose Raft mTLS is not operator-supplied. Node leaves, `ceremony-sign-csr` and the client trust pool are then signed through the TrustedCA's keystore signer, and no CA key bytes are read, returned or written (go-xkms#1381).
- **No mode writes `ca-key.pem`.** Local-CA mode (`raft_enrollment` without ACME, any `key_backend`, `software` by default) issues its Raft leaf from the TrustedCA; the software self-signed cluster CA and its key-PEM path are deleted with no fallback. Local-CA mode needs `ca` configured and refuses to join with `ErrLocalCAJoin` (was `ErrHardwareKeyJoin`); joiners use ACME. A key backend the `Backends` seam cannot supply fails with `ErrKeyBackendUnavailable` (go-xkms#1381).
- **Embedders must supply `RaftMTLSResolver` for multi-node nodes.** `embeddednode` (and `sdk/go`) has no built-in software resolver; a multi-node node without one fails with `ErrNilRaftMTLSResolver`. Removed with it: `RaftTLSCacheSubdir`, `NodeOptions.StoragePath`, the `ClusterOptions` fields `TrustDomain`, `AdvertiseNoisePort`, `AdvertiseNoiseHost` and `Bootstrap`, and `ClusterOptions.ClusterEnrollOptions` (go-xkms#1381).
- **TPM policy branches are named, and a branch update names its branch** -- every branch of a TPM policy carries a `name` (1-64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, unique within the policy; `branch-N` when a create leaves it out, N counted from 1), set in a branch spec with `name=NAME` (`--branch 'name=next;pcr=0,7'`). `tpm policy update <name> --branch <name> --reference-values <corim>` (xkmsctl, xkey, the xKey GUI, REST `{"branch":"next"}`, gRPC `TPMPolicyUpdateRequest.branch` = 5, MCP `tpm.policy.update`, SDK) approves only the named branch from a signed CoRIM, so a policy with `current` and `next` branches lets a platform update proceed with both images unsealing; `verify` reports each branch by name with the reference values it is approved for. The integer branch index is removed (gRPC field 3 reserved; a numeric REST `branch` is a malformed request). Invalid or duplicate names are refused as invalid arguments (`tpmpolicy.ErrInvalidBranchName`, `ErrDuplicateBranch`, `*InvalidBranchError`; SDK `ErrTPMPolicyInvalidBranchName`, `ErrTPMPolicyDuplicateBranch`, `TPMPolicyInvalidBranchError`, `ErrTPMPolicyBranchName` for a branch spec with more than one name) (go-xkms#1443).
- **The Android device-key verifier moved from xkey into `pkg/attestation` (#1548).** The hardware policy a paired handset's key must meet now lives in the library, so any caller can apply it, not just xkey. `attestation.VerifyAndroidDeviceKey` checks that the chain anchors in the trusted roots, that the key is in at least a TEE, was generated there and may sign, that the bootloader is locked with a verified boot state, and that an allow-listed application holds it. The SDK exposes it as `xkms.VerifyAndroidDeviceKey`, with `xkms.AndroidDeviceTrust` and `xkms.AndroidDeviceKey`. Its parts are `android.DeviceVerifyOptions`, `android.RequireAttestedBootState`, `RequireAttestedKeyOrigin`, `RequireAttestedApplication` (through the new `android.ApplicationMatcher`), `KeyDescription.AttestedApplication`, `attestation.ParseDERChain`, `VerifiedTrustAnchor` and `FormatTrustAnchor`. Each has its own typed error: `android.ErrNoRootOfTrust`, `ErrBootloaderUnlocked`, `ErrKeyOriginNotGenerated`, `ErrKeyPurposeNotSign`, `ErrApplicationRefused` and `attestation.ErrCertificateParseFailed`. `xkey/pkg/attestation` drops `Trust`, `VerifyOptions`, `RequireAttested*`, `VerifiedTrustAnchor`, `ParseDERChain`, `FormatTrustAnchor` and its `ErrAttestationKey*` errors, and `pairing.AttestedApplication` is gone. `VerifyDeviceAttestation` keeps only the pairing protocol's checks (version, genesis challenge, fingerprint, live transcript signature) on top of the SDK call. Tests: `pkg/attestation/android_device_test.go`, which verifies a real Galaxy S23 Ultra StrongBox chain, and `pkg/attestation/android/device_test.go`.
- **`/api/v1/auth/me` reports the permissions RBAC lists** -- the fixed `uiPermissionMatrix` and its one `Authorize` call per pair are gone. The `permissions` map now holds every permission qrdb's `RBACClient.ListPermissions` grants the caller, each `true`; a permission not held is absent instead of `false`, and a listing failure answers 500 (go-xkms#1557).
- **Authorization follows go-qrdb's tenant and grant rules** -- system-tenant checks use `qrdbsdk.IdentityIsSystemTenant` and target tenants resolve through `qrdbsdk.OwnTenant`, refusing with `*qrdbsdk.CrossTenantDeniedError`; xkms module permissions are granted per role with declared duties; each ACME admin route in `admin.Routes()` is mounted under its own permission, by the unified server through qrdb `Handle` and by a standalone host through `RegisterRoutes`. The tenant lifecycle routes, whose permission depends on the tenant they reach, are mounted identity-gated on the unified server and authorized by the admin router (`RegisterAuthorizedRoutes` now takes the `PermissionGate`); `apimodule.AdminRoute` gains `SelfPermission` for them. Creating a tenant from a tenant-scoped identity is refused with `403` (go-xkms#1557).
- **Method permissions are declared where each method is defined, not in hand-kept maps** -- every ACME `AdminService` RPC carries the go-qrdb `(qrdb.v1.permission)` option in `api/proto/admin.proto`, and the ACME admin gRPC interceptor and MCP surface read it from the generated descriptor; the ACME `MethodPermissions` map and its own `Permission` type are gone. The xkms JSON-RPC/MCP methods register their permission with `handle(resource, action, handler)` (or `handlePublic`) in the `rpcMethods` dispatch table, so a dispatchable method without a permission cannot exist; `methodPermissions`, `publicMethods`, `ErrMethodPermissionUnmapped` and the separate `frost.*` switch are deleted. A build without `-tags frost` still registers the `frost.*` methods, with stubs that refuse as "FROST support not compiled". Permissions are `qrdbsdk.Permission` values, reported through `qrdbsdk.ModuleMCPToolPermissioner` and enforced by `qrdbsdk.Authorizer` (go-xkms#1557).
- **`pkg/qrdbrole` removed; built-in role reconciliation is go-qrdb's alone** -- go-xkms no longer carries its own copy of go-qrdb's built-in role convergence. Callers that imported `pkg/qrdbrole.Reconcile` call `ReconcileBuiltInRoles` on a go-qrdb `sdk/go/transport` client instead, which go-qrdb's transports serve. The in-memory `testutil.QRDBFakeTransport` now answers `ReconcileBuiltInRoles` with `transport.CapabilityUnsupportedError` rather than converging roles itself (go-xkms#1557).
- **go-qrdb v0.50.0-alpha** -- `github.com/jeremyhahn/go-qrdb` and `github.com/jeremyhahn/go-qrdb/sdk/go` move from v0.48.0-alpha to v0.50.0-alpha in every module (root, `sdk/go`, `xkey`, `web/desktop`); minimum version selection also raises go-quicraft to v0.22.0-alpha, prometheus/client_golang to v1.25.0, klauspost/compress to v1.20.1 and golang.org/x/{crypto,sync,sys,term,text}. What changes for go-xkms users:
  - The platform credential store hands secrets out in protected memory: `credentials.Service.RetrieveCredential` is replaced by `RetrieveCredentialBuffer`, which returns a `*secure.Buffer` the caller must `Destroy`, matching go-qrdb's `secret.CredentialRetrieveFunc`.
  - The `sdk/go` re-export `WithTenantStrategyRegistry` is removed with go-qrdb's `tenant.WithStrategyRegistry`. Hardware tenant barriers take their keys through go-qrdb's barrier key seam: `sdk/go` re-exports `BarrierKeyProvider`, `NewBarrierKeyProvider` and `WithTenantBarrierKeyProvider`, and `seal.NewHardwareTenantService` installs the provider over the hardware strategy registry.
  - `xkms.proto` takes the `(qrdb.v1.permission)` method option from go-qrdb's SDK (`qrdb/v1/permission.proto`, Go package `github.com/jeremyhahn/go-qrdb/sdk/go/proto/qrdb/v1`); `make proto` includes the `sdk/go` module's `proto/` directory. The option's name and field number are unchanged.
  - Tenant barrier init over a go-qrdb transport is two calls, `init/begin` and `init/complete`, proving possession of the first admin's key (`TenantBarrierInitRequest.Signer`); the single-call init route, RPC, QUIC method and MCP tool are gone.
  - A caller go-qrdb resolves to an account carries that account's immutable user id as its Subject, so every go-xkms reader of that Subject (the audit actor, shared-password ownership, the key-version actor) names the id, not the username. ABAC `subject.id` is the id and `subject.name` the account name.
  - A sealed node refuses everything but unseal; deleting a role removes it from every holder; the built-in User role also holds `passwords:write` and `passwords:delete`.
  - `UserAuthFactorClient` gains go-qrdb's hard `DeleteAuthFactor`, so an implementation of that interface must provide it.

### Fixed

- **A CA that loses a concurrent key-generate race now gets the winner's key on
  every backend.** `getOrGenerateKey` (`pkg/ca/csr.go`) recovers only on
  `errors.Is(err, backend.ErrKeyAlreadyExists)`, but most backends reported
  "already exists" with their own sentinel, so the losing caller failed. The
  awskms, azurekv, gcpkms, pkcs8 and frost `ErrKeyAlreadyExists`, phone's
  `ErrKeyExists` and the keystore's `xkms.ErrKeyAlreadyExists` are now
  `backend.ErrKeyAlreadyExists` itself. `xkms.KeyExistsError` unwraps to it.
  The awskms and azurekv `Save` report an existing key with it, not
  `backend.ErrFileAlreadyExists`. gcpkms maps Cloud KMS's gRPC `AlreadyExists`
  from `CreateCryptoKey` to it (#1599).
- **A reopened TPM signs with the IAK's own signature scheme.** The IAK is
  Restricted, so its public area fixes RSASSA or RSA-PSS (Template H-1, TCG
  "TPM 2.0 Keys for Device Identity and Attestation" section 7.3.4), but a
  restarted process described it by the configured algorithm instead. After
  `xkey tpm iak create --template rsa2048` on an RSA-PSS configuration the next
  `Quote` failed unpacking an RSASSA signature as RSA-PSS. `KeyAttributes` now
  reads the signature algorithm from the key's public area, and the
  configuration only names it for a key that fixes none, such as an RSA IDevID
  (`pkg/tpm2/key.go`, `pkg/tpm2/sigscheme.go`, #704).
- **TPM key attributes carry the key size and curve.** `KeyAttributes` read
  a key's public area but left `RSAAttributes` and `ECCAttributes` empty, so
  `xkey tpm lak show` (and every other reader of the generic attributes) never
  printed an RSA size or ECC curve. They are now filled from the public area's
  `TPMS_RSA_PARMS.keyBits` and `TPMS_ECC_PARMS.curveID`, and an object of any
  other type is refused with `ErrInvalidKeyAlgorithm` before it is parsed
  (`pkg/tpm2/key.go`, #704).
- **The xkey GUI can start the agent server.** The GUI's agent service was never
  given an enrollment service, so starting the agent server always failed. When
  the GUI connects to xkmsd it now enrolls agents through the xkmsd certificate
  authority (`agent.XKMSdCA`, the same adapter the CLI uses). Enrollment records
  live in the CLI's store under the xKey data directory, so agents enrolled from
  either the CLI or the GUI show up in both. A disconnect or shutdown stops the
  running agent server. Without a connection, starting it fails with
  `ErrAgentServiceNotReady` (#704).
- **The xkey GUI's FIDO2 authenticator writes its audit records.** The audit
  logger was attached in `NewApp`, but there the authenticator does not exist
  yet, so it never got one. The logger is now attached where the authenticator
  is built, and PIN establishment and credential creation are recorded in the
  GUI's audit store (#704).
- **`xkey tpm iak create` and `xkey tpm idevid create` honour `--template`.**
  The flag was validated and then ignored, so every key came from the
  configuration. An explicitly set `--template` now selects the key's suite,
  mapped in one place onto the TCG "TPM 2.0 Keys for Device Identity and
  Attestation" section 7.3.4 templates: `rsa2048` (H-1, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5),
  `rsa-pss` (H-1, RSASSA-PSS) and `ecc256` (H-2, P-256); left unset, the
  configuration decides as before (`xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/tpm_devid_template.go`).
  `CreateIDevID` no longer forces an RSA IDevID on a device whose EK is RSA:
  the IDevID is its own configured algorithm (`pkg/tpm2/key.go`, #704).
- **xkey no longer leaks the xkms TPM2 backend's own TPM connection.** When the
  local key store hands the tpm2 backend the GUI's shared TPM, the connection
  `AutoInitialize` opened was dropped without being closed. `SetTPM` leaves that
  connection to its caller. The leak held a TPM device handle for the life of the
  process, and with the simulator it held go-tpm-tools' process-wide lock, so the
  next simulator open hung. `initLocalKeyStore` now closes the replaced
  connection (`xkey/pkg/gui/app.go`). Verified by the gui tests that bring up a
  simulated tpm2 backend twice in one run (#704).

## [0.56.0-alpha] - 2026-10-17

### Security

- **The xkms session JWT authenticates on every transport and the admin plane refuses anonymous callers** -- xkmsd now builds on go-qrdb v0.48.0-alpha and registers its authenticator in the node's unified chain (`WithAuthenticators`), so a session JWT reaches xkms module RPCs over gRPC, MCP and HTTP/3 as well as REST. The `/admin` and `/api/v1/tenants` routes are permissioned module routes instead of public ones, and `auth.enabled: false` / `auth.type: none` are refused at boot (`ErrAuthenticationDisabled`) rather than falling back to a no-op authenticator. A clustered xkmsd waits for its shard leader as the node service principal, which now holds `admin:shard_state`. Tenant-scoped user and role management by the platform admin returns 403 under strict tenant isolation (go-xkms#1380).
- **xkmsd's unix socket speaks TLS and authenticates every caller** -- the plaintext unix gRPC listener and the qrdb control plane it hosted are gone; the socket is now the embedded qrdb node's TLS unix listener, which serves the xkms module and qrdb's own services through the same authentication chain as every network transport, so an anonymous caller is refused. `protocols.unix` therefore requires `tls.enabled` (the bootstrap certificate serves when no cert files are set; it names localhost only with `tls.include_localhost_sans`), and the `unix.enabled`, `unix.socket_mode` and `unix.protocol` keys are removed. `xkmsctl` (including `cluster`, `rebalance` and `auth factor`) dials `unix://` with TLS and its `--tls-cert`/`--tls-key`/`--tls-ca` flags, and `cluster` and `rebalance` present `--token` as a bearer on every control-plane RPC, so a token with `--tls-ca` and no client certificate authenticates (a token is refused for plaintext `grpc://`); the PKCS#11 module needs `tls_enabled` with `tls_cert`/`tls_key`/`tls_ca` to reach xkmsd. The sign server's socket is unchanged (go-xkms#1380).
- **device-attest-01 holds the measurements claim to its one shape** -- a possession request's measurements (273) must be exactly one measurements-format `[258, bstr .cbor evidence CoSWID]` whose evidence holds one file `"app"` with a SHA-256 hash-entry of 32 bytes, in core deterministic CBOR and with no other field; the device and the server refuse anything else with `ErrPossessionMeasurementsShape`, where before only the claim's presence was checked. The CoSWID's tag-id, tag-version, software-name and tag-creator entity are the producer's (RFC 9393 §2.3, CA m463): a missing or mistyped one is refused, but their values are not compared, so arduino-generic's alias certificates enroll. `ParsePossessionCSR` returns the 32 bytes as `PossessionRequest.ApplicationEvidence`.
- **No secret or authorization value is logged, at any level** -- `pkg/tpm2` no longer logs the SO PIN / hierarchy authorization, hierarchy passwords, sealed HMAC secrets, NV secrets or credential-activation secrets (raw or hex) at Debug, and the `tpm2.Params.DebugSecrets` option that enabled that logging is removed. Lengths of auth values are secret-derived too: `CreateSRK` logs `hierarchy_auth_set`/`user_auth_set` presence flags instead of `hierarchy_auth_len`/`user_auth_len`, and the platform-password unseal byte count, the CA enrollment `secret_size`, the CTAP2 `pinUvAuthParam_len`/`pinHashEnc_len` and xkey pairing's `secretLen` are no longer logged (CA m417).

### Added

- **The attested-caller gate runs on the node.** `attestation.peer_gate: optional|required` (default `off`, standalone datastore only) installs `peergate.Gate` on the embedded go-qrdb node through `node.WithPeerAttestationGate`, with the embedder's policy from `server.WithAttestedCallerPolicy`; go-xkms ships no PCR golden values. Peer evidence moves from the per-process `MemoryStore` to `peergate.DAOStore` in the node's datastore (database `peergate`). Challenge and Submit are module verbs on REST (`/api/v1/peer-attestation/challenge`, `/evidence`), gRPC (`PeerAttestationChallenge`, `SubmitPeerAttestation`) and MCP (`peer.attestation.challenge`, `peer.attestation.submit`), granted to User and Operator and never gated themselves. Hosts of the xkms module install the same gate with `sdk/go` `WithAttestedCallerGate(policy)` and `PeerAttestationGate()`, and bind the module's storage to the node's service principal with `WithServiceModuleServiceContext(node.ServiceContext)`, without which a node that enforces authentication refuses it. Covered by gate on/off and required-refuses-unattested tests, DAO round-trip and eviction tests, and the verb permission goldens. SPEC: attested-caller-gate.
- **DICE evidence reports its root of trust: hardware or software.** A device's alias chain declares where its UDS lives in DiceTcbInfo (TCG DICE Attestation Architecture r0.23 §6.1.1): `vendorInfo` is the DER OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.29377.101.24.1 (hardware, a secure element) or .24.2 (software, device storage), and a set `notSecure` flag is a software root whatever `vendorInfo` says. `dice.Verify` reports it as `Evidence.RootType`. CA m452: it is read only from the certificates on the paths that verified to a configured trusted root (`dice.RootTypeFromPaths`, sdk `DICERootTypeFromPaths`), so an unanchored chain, including a device-attest-01 raw DeviceIDKey record, reports unreported and certificates off the verified path are never read; a software root on any layer makes the identity software, and it is refused unless the policy permits `NotSecure`. `attestation.Verifier` anchors a `dice` statement through `dice.VerifyChain`, which handles the critical DiceTcbInfo. `attestation.Verifier.Verify` now returns the `*Result` with `RootType` (breaking: it returned only an error), device-attest-01's `VerifiedAttestation` and its persisted record carry it (`RegisteredDeviceVerifier.VerifyRegisteredDevice` now returns the `*VerifiedAttestation`), as does the AVR backend's `Attestation`; `sdk/go` re-exports it as `DICERootType`. Docs: `docs/dice-device-identity/`. SPEC: dice-device-identity.
- **Container images are signed and verified with KMS keys.** `pkg/image` signs an image with a KMS `crypto.Signer` certified under `TrustedCA`'s code-signing profile, producing a DSSE envelope over an in-toto statement that names the image digest. The envelope is pushed both as an OCI 1.1 referrer and into cosign's `sha256-<hex>.att` tag, with an optional RFC 3161 timestamp. `VerifyImage` checks an image's attestations against the trusted image-signer roots, at the timestamp's time when one verifies. The registry client follows a registry's Bearer token challenge and every page of the referrers index, and a timestamp is trusted only from a TSA certificate whose sole extended key usage is a critical id-kp-timeStamping. `pkg/signing` gains `Verify`, the RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 check over SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 through `types.SimpleVerifier`. The SDK exposes both as `xkms.ImageVerifier` and `xkms.VerifySignature`. SPEC: image-signing.
- **The static TPM policy resolver refuses unsigned approvals, and the SDK classifies its refusals.** `NewTPMStaticPolicyResolver` refuses a binding record whose approval carries no signature (`ErrTPMPolicyApprovalInvalid`), and sdk/go now exports `TPMPolicyBindingFormatError`, `ErrTPMPolicyApprovalInvalid` and `ErrTPMPolicyApprovalMismatch`, so a consumer such as an initrd tells a corrupt, unsigned or foreign record apart without importing `pkg/*`. A key is usable with only its `.tpmpolicy` record, and a tampered signature, a record re-signed by a foreign authority, stripped approvals and an unknown policy authorize nothing on the TPM simulator (`TestStaticPolicyResolver_AuthorizesFromTheRecord`, `TestStaticPolicyResolver_Refusals`, `TestNewTPMStaticPolicyResolver_Refusals`). SPEC: tpm-policies. (#1550)
- **A TPM policy branch can be approved for an update before it boots, from signed reference values.** `tpm policy update <name> --branch <n> --reference-values <corim>` (REST `{branch, reference_values}`, gRPC, MCP, xkmsctl, xkey CLI and GUI) verifies a COSE-signed CoRIM against the new `backends.tpm2.reference_signer` (`public_key` or `roots`), predicts the branch's PCR values by replaying the boot event log with the CoRIM's component digests (or takes its final values), re-approves the branch and records the CoRIM's id, signer and digest, which `verify` reports. An unsigned, foreign or tampered CoRIM, a missing branch or pcr condition, or a node without a reference signer is refused and leaves the approvals unchanged; a live re-capture drops the reference. The permission is `tpm_policy:update`. On the TPM simulator the registered image unseals and an unregistered one stays refused (`TestService_UpdateBranchFromReferenceValues`, `TestService_UpdateBranchRefusals`). SPEC: tpm-policies, attestation-verifier. (#1443)
- **TPM policy registries belong to a node, and named policies authorize without a database.** Scope, policy and assignment keys are prefixed by the node ID (`<node>/<tenant>/...`), so nodes sharing one datastore keep separate registries; xkmsd passes `cluster.node_id`, and `compose.TPMPolicyParams` gains `NodeID`. Records written before this change are not read (`TestRegistry_NodesOwnTheirRecords`). The `.tpmpolicy` binding record (now version 3) carries the scope authority's public area and the policy's approvals, refreshed on update, revoke and authority rotation; `NewTPMStaticPolicyResolver` (sdk/go) builds a resolver from records, installed with the new `TrustedPlatformModule.SetPolicyBindingResolver`. Older records are refused (`TestService_OfflineAuthorization`, `TestStaticPolicyResolver`). SPEC: tpm-policies. (#1533)
- **Trust roots are one persisted, purpose-classified store served as module verbs.** xkey's truststore moved with its history to `pkg/attestation/truststore` (`xkey/pkg/truststore` is gone; xkey imports the new path), and its `DAOStore` persists every root in the qrdb `trust_roots` database. `XKMSService` serves list, get, import, quarantine and remove on REST (`/api/v1/trust-roots`), gRPC and Unix (`KeystoreService.TrustRoot*`), QUIC, MCP (`trust.root.*`) and the embedded transport, behind the new system-scope `trust_roots` permissions granted to Admin and Owner. A quarantined (`synced`) root stays listed but anchors nothing, and re-importing a held certificate never changes its purpose. Docs: `docs/trust-roots/`. SPEC: trust-roots, rbac.

### Changed

- **ACME admin tenant lifecycle routes require qrdb's cross-scope tenant grants to reach another tenant** -- on the ACME admin plane, `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/v1/tenants/{id}` and `PUT /api/v1/tenants/{id}/status` need the self-scoped `tenants:*` grant on the caller's own tenant and `tenants:{read,update,delete}:cross` (`qrdbsdk.PermissionTenants*Cross`) on any other; `GET /api/v1/tenants` needs `tenants:list` from a tenant-scoped caller (which lists only its own tenant) and `tenants:list:cross` from a system-tenant caller; `POST /api/v1/tenants` needs `tenants:create:cross`, and `CreateTenant` no longer re-checks platform scope by hand. A system-tenant caller without the cross-scope grant is refused; a tenant-scoped caller naming another tenant is answered `404 Tenant not found`, as for a missing tenant (go-xkms#1557, go-xkms#1225).
- **Users carry every role they hold** -- `UserInfo` (Go transport, gRPC, TS SDK) replaces the single `role` with a `roles` list, and the server resolves role names with qrdb's `SystemRoleID` and `GetRoleByName` instead of reading only the first role ID and scanning `ListRoles`. A user with several roles keeps all of them; `xkmsctl user list` shows a ROLES column and its JSON carries `roles` (go-xkms#1557).
- **`xkmsctl user register --role` accepts custom roles** -- the CLI no longer keeps its own role list: it sends the role name as given, and the server refuses a role the tenant does not hold. The `ErrInvalidRole` client-side check is gone (go-xkms#1557).
- **One attestation verifier.** The purpose-pooled verifier moved from `xkey/pkg/attestation` to `pkg/attestation/purpose.go` and became methods on the existing `attestation.Verifier`: `VerifyTPMAttestation`, `VerifyAndroidAttestation`, `VerifyIDevID`, `VerifyPurposeChain` (was `VerifyChain`) and `BuildTrustPool`, backed by the new `WithTrustStore` option. The xkey sentinels map onto the root ones: `ErrEmptyCertChain` → `ErrEmptyCertificateChain`, `ErrChainVerification` → `ErrChainVerificationFailed`, `ErrNoTrustAnchors` → `ErrNoTrustAnchors`. New root sentinels: `ErrNilTrustStore`, `ErrNilCertificate`, `ErrUnsupportedPurpose`, `ErrTrustStoreQuery`, `ErrMissingNonce` and `ErrChallengeVerification`. xkey reaches the verifier only through `sdk/go` (`NewAttestationVerifier`, `WithAttestationTrustStore`, `AttestationVerificationResult`, `AttestationTrustLevel*`), and xkey/pkg/pairing reaches the Noise session through `sdk/go/bootstrap`. The xkey copy is deleted with no aliases. go-xkms#1548; SPEC rows attestation-verifier, trust-roots.
- **CA blobs live in a go-qrdb storage engine; go-xkms no longer requires go-objstore directly (#1556).** `ca.Params.ObjectStore` and `ObjectStoreFactory` now take a `qrdbsdk.Storage`, and the backend is chosen by configuration through go-qrdb. That covers cross-signed certificates, distribution-point CRLs and attestation evidence. A missing blob is `ca.ErrObjectNotFound`, and an engine failure wraps `ca.ErrStorageError`. In `sdk/go`, `ObjectStorage` is `qrdbsdk.Storage`, opened by `NewObjectStorage(provider, settings)` or `NewObjectStorageMemory()`. The go-objstore aliases (`ObjectMetadata`, `ObjectListOptions`, `ObjectInfo`, `ObjectListResult`, `ObjectArchiver`, `ObjectLifecyclePolicy`) and `NewObjectStorageLocal` are deleted with no replacement; open the local provider with `NewObjectStorage("local", map[string]string{"path": dir})`. go-objstore is now only an indirect requirement of the root and `sdk/go` modules, and the architecture gate rejects any direct import. SPEC row datastore.
- **One definition of the platform policy's PCR selection; breaking config key changes.** `tpm2.PlatformPCRSelection` (`PlatformPCRs`, `PlatformPCRBank`) is embedded in `tpm2.Config`, the TPM2 backend's `Config`, xkmsd's `backends.tpm2` and the seal autodetect probe, replacing their copies; `CreatePlatformPolicy` builds its selection with the same helper as the platform PCR read. **Breaking:** xkmsd's `backends.tpm2.platform_pcr` and `backends.tpm2.platform_pcr_bank` are replaced by `platform-pcrs` and `platform-pcr-bank`, with no compatibility path (the old keys are no longer read; the set's environment variable is `XKMS_BACKENDS_TPM2_PLATFORM_PCRS`). xkey's unread `tpm.platform_pcr_bank`, `tpm.seal_pcr_bank`, `gui.auto_unseal.pcrs`, `gui.auto_unseal.pcr_bank` and `policy.platform_pcr_bank` are removed. The defaults are PCRs 7 and 11 in the sha256 bank (`TestDefaultPlatformPCRs`). SPEC: platform-pcr-selection. (#1533)
- **The root module no longer imports xkey.** The pairing wire protocol (JSON-RPC messages, fragmentation, USB AOA transport) moved from `xkey/pkg/pairing` and `xkey/pkg/phone` to `pkg/pairingproto`, and the Noise XX session to `pkg/trust/bootstrap` (`NoiseSession`, `NewNoiseSession`). The virtual FIDO2 authenticator, its key backends, the UHID device and the virtual device moved from `xkey/pkg/{authenticator,uhid,virtualdevice}` to `pkg/fido2/{authenticator,uhid,virtualdevice}`. The authenticator now reports credential creation and PIN seeding through an `AuditLogger` seam that xkey satisfies with `audit.NewFIDO2Logger`, and the presence socket handler moved to `xkey/pkg/presence`. xkey production code reaches them only through the SDK re-exports `sdk/go/pairingproto`, `sdk/go/bootstrap`, `sdk/go/truststore` and `sdk/go/fido2/{authenticator,keybackend,uhid,virtualdevice}`; the xkey copies are deleted with no aliases, and root `go.mod` drops the `xkey` require and `replace`. Service plane lane 3; SPEC rows phone-hsm, virtual-authenticator, fido2-ctap2.
- **The platform policy seals to the board's boot PCRs, set once in `TPMConfig`** — the sealing PCR set is now `PlatformPCRs` (`tpm2.PCRSet`) in the one `tpm2.PlatformPCRSelection` embedded in `tpm2.Config`, defaulting to PCRs 7 and 11 and configurable per board; it replaces `PlatformPCR` and `DefaultPlatformPCR` (the resettable debug PCR 16). xkmsd's `backends.tpm2.platform-pcrs` (`XKMS_BACKENDS_TPM2_PLATFORM_PCRS`, replacing `platform-pcr`), `pkg/backend/tpm2.Config`, xKey's `tpm.platform-pcrs` and `--platform-pcrs`, and the SDK's `xkms.TPMPCRSet` / `xkms.DefaultPlatformPCRs` all carry the same type. Config load and `NewTPM2` refuse an empty set, duplicates, indexes above 23 and the resettable PCRs 16 and 23 with typed errors (`ErrPlatformPCRSetEmpty`, `ErrPlatformPCRDuplicate`, `ErrPlatformPCROutOfRange`, `ErrPlatformPCRResettable`, each in a `*PlatformPCRError`). xKey's config load refuses an invalid `tpm.platform-pcrs` (`XKEY_TPM_PLATFORM_PCRS`) the same way, and the GUI no longer warns and falls back to `{7, 11}`: it refuses to open the TPM. The CLI `tpm` commands seal to `tpm.platform-pcrs`, and `--platform-pcrs` overrides it. The platform policy pin records the set as a `PCRSelect` bitmap. Objects sealed under the old PCR 16 policy are not migrated (pre-release, no compatibility path). Simulator test `TestSealUnseal_BoardPCRSet_BindsOnlyConfiguredPCRs` shows a board set binds only its own PCRs (#1551, #1443).
- **Every issued certificate carries its tenant as the first subject OU.** `ca.StampTenant` sets `Subject.OrganizationalUnit[0]` to the request's tenant on every issuance path: `TrustedCA` `SignCSR`/`IssueCertificate*`, TCG EK/AK/IAK/IDevID enrollment, the ACME finalize paths and the `pkg/acme/issuance` pipeline, the init ceremony and first-boot admin enrollment. An OU the CSR carries is replaced, not appended to. The tenant is the authenticated caller's (xkms servicers), the ACME account's, or `system` for the node's own certificates, and `qrdbsdk.TenantFromClientCert` reads it back when no SPIFFE tenant SAN is present. A request without a tenant is refused with `ca.ErrTenantRequired`. Breaking: `SignOptions.TenantID`, `CertificateRequest.TenantID` and `issuance.Request.TenantID` are now required, and `SignCSRRaw`, `IssueEKCertificateRaw`, `IssueAKCertificateRaw`, `SignTCGCSRIDevIDRaw` and `EnrollDeviceRaw` take a trailing tenant. CA hierarchy certificates, the TCG LAK and FIDO2 attestation certificates are not stamped. SPEC: tenant-subject-ou.

### Removed

- **`AuthenticatedUser.Permissions` is gone from the ACME admin plane** -- the field copied the token's claimed permissions onto the request principal although nothing may authorize from it. Every ACME admin decision is made by qrdb's RBAC through `PermissionGate`; a permission listed in a bearer token's claims grants nothing (go-xkms#1557).

### Fixed

- **Every xkmsd unix-socket client dials gRPC over TLS with a client certificate** -- the socket is the qrdb node's TLS listener, which serves gRPC only, so the clients that still spoke plaintext or REST there failed. The Go SDK's unix transport carries its TCG calls over gRPC (credential submit and seal-strategy reads report not-supported on the socket), and `unix://` URLs passed to `NewFromURL` dial with TLS. The SDK SSH client and `xkmsctl ssh` present their client certificate on `unix://`. xkey reaches a `unix://` server, and the phone bridge reaches xkmsd, through the same TLS endpoint as its network transports. The bridge reads `xkmsd.tls_ca_file`, `xkmsd.tls_cert_file` and `xkmsd.tls_key_file`, and the CLI reads `XKMSD_TLS_CA`, `XKMSD_TLS_CERT` and `XKMSD_TLS_KEY`. `pkg/config`'s `CreateAuthenticator` refuses a disabled or empty auth type with `ErrAuthenticationDisabled` and accepts no `noop`/`none` type (go-xkms#1380).
- **`RequestCodeSigningCertificate` names the signer's tenant** -- `TrustedCA.SignCSR` refuses a request without a tenant (`ca.ErrTenantRequired`), so a code-signing certificate for image signing could not be issued by a real `TrustedCA`. The function now takes a `tenantID`, passes it to the code-signing profile, which stamps it as the certificate's first OU, and refuses a blank one (go-xkms#1546).
- **The loopback per-launch token identity holds the Admin@system role** -- its role is go-qrdb's deterministic system role ID (`SystemRoleID(SystemTenantID, RoleNameAdmin)`) instead of the bare name `admin`, which resolved to no role because `Identity.Roles` carries role IDs (go-xkms#1557).
- **The `timestamping` certificate profile issues its extended key usage critical** -- RFC 3161 section 2.3 requires a TSA certificate to carry id-kp-timeStamping as its sole, critical extended key usage, and the image verifier refuses one that does not. crypto/x509 encodes the usage non-critical, so certificates from the profile failed the verifier. The profile now supplies a critical extension listing id-kp-timeStamping alone (go-xkms#1563).
- **xkmsd shutdown drains in-flight requests before closing the datastore** -- `Server.Shutdown` stopped the embedded qrdb node, which serves every transport, only after it had dropped the shared datastore and storage backend, so a request still running (the first one builds the module REST binding through the datastore) could dereference a nil datastore or race the close. The node now stops and drains its transports first; the datastore and storage handles are atomic, and a caller that reaches for the datastore after shutdown gets `ErrNoDatastore` (go-xkms#2185).
- **A TPM device that never answers is an error, not an unprovisioned TPM.** `NewTPM2` probed the EK handle and then the EK certificate NV index, and treated any failure of either as "no EK yet", so a transport that failed before the TPM returned a response code (EOF from a dead or wrong device, a closed socket) came back as `ErrNotInitialized` with a live instance. Provisioning callers accept that error and went on to provision a device that was never there. Only a TPM response code now means unprovisioned; a transport failure returns the new `ErrDeviceNoResponse` with no instance and releases the device. `TestNewTPM2_DeviceNeverAnswersIsAnError` pins it. SPEC: tpm2. (#704)
- **A backend configured in xKey holds PIV certificates without a restart.** `AdminService.ConfigureBackend` gave new TPM 2.0 and PKCS#11 backends no PIV capability, so they were not listed as PIV-capable until the next start, and the PIV register hook never fired. A certificate imported in the meantime went to an on-demand `backends/<id>/` namespace and was gone after the restart, which reads `backends/<category>/`. The hook also registered the shared software store, so if it had fired, the new backend would have listed software certificates. Configured backends are now PIV-capable, and the hook registers the same isolated `backends/<category>/` store that `initLocalPIV` gives them at start (`newNamespacedPIVStore`). `TestApp_ConfigureTPM2Backend_PIVStoreMatchesRestart` pins it. SPEC: gui. (#704)
- **`xkey oidc login --provider <aws-provider> --no-browser` no longer opens a browser.** The login of a saved AWS provider passed a hard-coded `false` for `--no-browser`, so the flag was ignored and a browser was started on headless and SSH sessions. The flag now reaches the AWS login, which prints the authorization URL instead. `TestRunOIDCLogin_AWSProviderHonoursNoBrowser` pins it. SPEC: oidc. (#704)
- **A FIDO2 touch request whose audit record fails no longer stays pending.** `presence.SocketHandler.RequestUserPresence` published the request before writing its `user_presence_requested` audit record, so when that write failed the call returned the error but left the request pending: `HasPending` stayed true and the next `Approve` resolved an orphan nobody was waiting on. The audit record is now written first, and a failed write leaves nothing pending. `TestSocketHandler_Audit_RequestLogFailureLeavesNothingPending` pins it. SPEC: fido2. (#704)
- **`xkey tpm clear --force` schedules the clear on the TPM it was given.** The device name was trimmed of `tpmrm` before it was tested for it, so `/dev/tpmrm1` became `1` and fell back to `tpm0`: the Physical Presence Interface request, and the reboot after it, cleared the first TPM instead of the second. `/dev/tpmrmN` now maps to `tpmN`. `TestRunForceTPMClear_RequestsClearOnTheDevicesTPM` pins it. SPEC: tpm2. (#704)

## [0.55.0-alpha] - 2026-10-15
