A factory that does not serve it fails with `*dao.DatabaseUnavailableError`. `xkmsd` opens the database on its shared datastore, and the `xkmsd init` bootstrap CA stores its certificate through an in-memory factory. The file/KV certificate store is gone, and existing certificate data is not migrated.
- **The datastore hands out the go-qrdb client and a DAO factory** -- `datastore.Open` now returns a `*datastore.Datastore` instead of a `storage.Backend`, in standalone and remote mode alike. It carries `Client()` (the go-qrdb SDK client) and `DAOFactory()` (go-qrdb's DAO factory over the default database and every named database it has opened). `datastore.New` builds one over a client the caller owns. `DatabaseKVStore(ctx, name)` is now a method, and `DialRemote` returns the `*qrdbsdk.Client`; `ClientBackend` and `ErrClientUnavailable` are gone. New `dao.New` builds a go-qrdb `GenericDAO` from the factory and refuses a named database that is not open instead of falling back to the default one. Features not yet on DAOs get a `storage.Backend` over the factory from `compose.FactoryBackend` / `compose.FactoryStorage`; the API-module host's `"xkms/"` stores now open this way. The SDK's `OpenDatastore` returns the `*Datastore`; `DatastoreStorage(ds.DAOFactory())` gives the `StorageBackend` for `AutoConfig.Datastore`.
- **Key-version records are go-qrdb DAO entities, written as xkms's service principal** -- `keyversion.NewStore(daos)` now takes a `*qrdbsdk.DAOFactory` serving the `keyversion` database (`keyversion.DatabaseName`, SDK `KeyVersionDatabase`) instead of a `storage.Backend`, and stores one `key_versions` entity per rotated key, named `{tenant}/<backend>/<keyID>`. xkmsd opens the database on its datastore, whose `datastore.WithCallContext` runs the records' reads and writes as the embedded node's `xkms` service principal. `compose.BuildKeyVersionStore(daos)` replaces the storage form, and `compose.Databases` always names the key-version database. `datastore.DatabaseKVStore` now scopes before it ensures, so a client with no database plane is refused with `*datastore.ErrDatabaseScope` instead of panicking. `compose.StorageKeyVersions` and `keyversion.ErrNilStore` are gone (`keyversion.ErrNilDAOFactory` replaces the latter). Records written under the old `key-versions` storage are not read.
- **The root module runs on go-qrdb v0.46.0-alpha, go-quicraft v0.19.0, go-enclave v0.7.0-alpha and go-luks2 v0.5.0-alpha** -- the bump includes the go-qrdb v0.40.1-alpha migration, which deletes go-xkms's re-exposure of go-qrdb services (Backup, Barrier, Custodian/Share, SealStore, Credentials, Init, Invite and Audit query) from REST, gRPC, MCP, unix, the SDKs, the CLIs and the web console. Single-admin `xkmsd init` now runs through go-qrdb's `node.FirstBoot`. go-qrdb's secret APIs are now context-aware (`secure.NewSecret`, `Secret.Open`, `SecretValue.WithBytes`, `seal.CredentialsFor`/`MustCredentials`, `enclave.WipeAll`), and every caller passes its request or command context. Certificate issuance goes through go-qrdb's CSR-based `IssueCert`/`EnrollCert`, because the server-side key generation in `GenerateCert`/`ExportCert` is gone upstream. go-qrdb dropped the per-database `engine` setting, its volume-pool subsystem and the tenant `DataRoot`, so xkmsd no longer provisions a volume pool and its barrier registry serves prefix and barrier tenant isolation only. go-qrdb no longer re-exports Shamir split/combine, so the TPM `ShareSecret`/`SecretFromShares` helpers and the matching SDK aliases are removed. go-luks2 no longer models the systemd TPM2 token members, so `pkg/luks` writes and reads `tpm2-blob`, `tpm2-pcr-bank`, `tpm2-pcrs`, `tpm2-key-handle` and `tpm2-policy-hash` itself, under the same names, so existing tokens and systemd-cryptsetup are unaffected. The `certs:generate` permission is gone upstream: certificate issuance now requires `certs:issue` (and `certs:enroll` for enrollment), so roles granting `certs:generate` must be updated. File storage uses go-qrdb's hashed shard layout and writes every record owner-only (0600); `certs/*` is no longer world-readable. Its cross-process write lock is now taken on the store directory itself, so the directory no longer holds a `.lock` file, and it also covers opening the store, so processes opening one directory at the same time no longer fail on each other's temporary files. Role-membership checks resolve the role through the node's role store as the caller, so a caller without `roles:read` fails closed with a role-resolution error instead of a plain denial. Barrier and volume tenants are refused unless the node seals through the node-seal path. go-qrdb now publishes each node's member record itself, so xkmsd's cluster advertiser and the `cluster.advertise_host` setting are removed. A first boot without a CA configured leaves the node serving only the ceremony endpoints until an administrator certificate is bound. go-qrdb resolves a user or role only within the request context's tenant, so the admin plane scopes each tenant user and role operation to the tenant it addresses once the tenant binding admits the caller; a platform administrator's cross-tenant user and role management works as before. go-qrdb authorizes every embedded-client call, so xkms's own calls on its embedded node run as its service principal (see the service-principal entry). go-truststrap stays at v0.4.0-alpha because go-qrdb v0.45.0-alpha did not compile against v0.5.0-alpha. The integration-test module follows in its own change. Refs #1413, #1355, #1358, #1399.
- **The `sdk/go`, `xkey` and web/desktop modules run on the same go-qrdb, go-quicraft, go-enclave and go-luks2 releases** -- web/desktop needs no source change. xkey seals barrier credentials, PINs, USB passphrases and imported passwords under the command or GUI context, so `pwimport`'s `Parser.Parse`, `Import`, `Preview` and `ToStaticPassword` and `usb.CreateImage` now take a `context.Context`. xkey's data directory is a go-qrdb file engine, which stores each key under a hashed path and refuses a non-empty directory without its format marker. Because of that, `xkey barrier` probes and reads the sealed root key through storage instead of a `barrier/root_key` file. An xkey data directory written by an earlier release must be re-initialized; there is no migration. `xkey barrier status` (and the GUI's seal info) report the data directory and the engine entry holding the sealed root key (`root_key_entry`) instead of a `root_key_path` file. An explicit `--token-store` or `--session-store` on `xkey oidc` now names the directory of an unencrypted store rather than a single JSON file, and their defaults are `~/.xkey/tokens` and `~/.xkey/aws-session`. Known break: `xkey barrier init` is refused when the data directory already holds TPM key-store state from an earlier `xkey tpm` or `xkey pin` command, because the engine only claims an empty directory; initialize the barrier first. Refs #1413.
- **OIDC tokens persist through the injected DAO factory** -- `oidc.NewDAOStore` takes a `*qrdbsdk.DAOFactory` instead of a `KVStore` and refuses a nil factory, or one that does not serve the `oidc` database, with `ErrDAOCreation`; `ErrNilBackend` is gone. `MemoryTokenStore` (and the SDK's `NewMemoryTokenStore`) is deleted. New `dao.NewStoreFactory` (SDK `NewStoreDAOFactory`) serves one `KVStore` as the factory for every database, for hosts with no go-qrdb node: xkey's GUI builds its OIDC token store with it over the barrier backend, or over a memory store when there is no barrier. Tokens stored before this change are not migrated.
- **xkmsd has one barrier: the embedded qrdb node's** -- every hardware and cloud seal strategy (`tpm2`, `pkcs11`, `awskms`, `gcpkms`, `azurekv`, `vault`) is now injected into the node's own barrier through `node.WithSealStrategy` and `sdk.WithStrategyRegistry` (`embeddednode.NodeSealOptions`), and xkmsd adopts the node's registry and tenant service. The second, xkms-built barrier (`initializeBarrier`, `initializeBarrierRegistry` and the server's seal-strategy builders) is deleted. A cloud node seal keeps its key metadata under `<datastore.path>/node-seal/<strategy>`, needs its provider's build tag and fails closed without it; `vault` takes its token from the pre-barrier store, sealed once with the new `xkmsd seal-vault-token`. A hardware or cloud strategy that refuses the root key reports `*seal.RootKeyUnsealError`, which matches go-qrdb's `ErrInvalidCredentials`.
- **`seal.BarrierRegistry` is go-qrdb's registry, unwrapped** -- it is now a type alias for `qrdbsdk.BarrierRegistry`. `seal.WrapBarrierRegistry`, `Inner` and the forwarding methods are removed; `RegisterTenant(id)` becomes go-qrdb's `RegisterTenantDefault(id)`, and `RegisterTenantWithConfig` becomes `RegisterTenant(ctx, id, base, cfg, strategies...)`. `seal.NewBarrierRegistry` stays and refuses a nil system barrier with `ErrNilSystemBarrier`.
- **Remote PKCS#11 token state is stored as go-qrdb DAO entities, written as xkms's service principal** -- `pkcs11state.NewStore(daos)` now takes a `*qrdbsdk.DAOFactory` serving the `pkcs11state` database (`pkcs11state.DatabaseName`) instead of a `storage.Backend`, and keeps each record as one `pkcs11_state_records` entity named `<tenant>/<token>/<key>`. `PutIfAbsent`, `CompareAndSwap` and `CompareAndDelete` are the DAO's `SaveIfAbsent`, `CompareAndSwap` and `DeleteIfMatch`, so they work on every datastore; `pkcs11state.ErrNilBackend`, `ErrCompareAndSwapUnsupported` and `ErrCompareAndDeleteUnsupported` are gone (`pkcs11state.ErrNilDAOFactory` and `*pkcs11state.StoreError` replace them). `CompareAndSwap` now follows `storage.CompareAndSwapper`: an absent record refuses, where a nil `expected` used to mean "only if absent". xkmsd opens the database on its datastore, whose `datastore.WithCallContext` runs the records' calls as the embedded node's service principal; the principal's grant gains `kv:range`, which `List`'s paged scan needs. `signserver.Config.StateStorage` is replaced by `StateDAOs`, a DAO factory serving `signserver.StateDatabase`. State written under the old `pkcs11state/` storage prefix is not read; re-provision remote tokens.
- **One node builder: `pkg/daemon` is merged into `pkg/embeddednode`** -- `embeddednode.NewNode` is now the only code that constructs the embedded go-qrdb node, standalone or clustered (Raft mTLS plus the cluster-enrollment advertiser). `xkmsd`, `pkg/datastore` and SDK embedders all go through it. The package's types are renamed to `NodeOptions`, `NodeResult` and `ErrNilNodeOptions`. Its errors now read `embeddednode: ...` instead of `daemon: ...`. The SDK keeps `NewDaemonNode`, `DaemonOptions`, `DaemonNodeResult` and the related names, which now point at the merged builder. CI's raft matrix now also runs the builder's tests, including a three-replica cluster formed over Raft mTLS.
- **SoftHSM 2.7.0, built from a pinned, checksum-verified release, replaces the distribution's 2.6.1 in every image** -- SoftHSM 2.6.1 answers an AES-GCM tag mismatch with `CKR_GENERAL_ERROR`, the code PKCS#11 reserves for an unrecoverable token error, so PKCS#11 tamper could not be reported as `types.ErrSealedDataAuthentication` on any image this repository tests with; 2.7.0 answers `CKR_ENCRYPTED_DATA_INVALID`, which the PKCS#11 backend classifies. New `scripts/build-softhsm.sh` is the single pin (version plus the SHA-256 of the upstream release archive, verified before anything is extracted) and installs at Debian's paths (`/usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so`, `/usr/bin/softhsm2-util`, `/etc/softhsm`), stripped, file object store only. It is used by `Dockerfile.ci`, the devcontainer and `Dockerfile.virt-piv`, the integration-test `Dockerfile`, the Alpine SoftHSM sidecar (`test/docker/softhsm`, previously 2.6.1 from an unverified git tag), the `test/integration/{pkcs11,pkcs11/module,acmeadmin,storage}` images, xkey's e2e image, the published runtime images (`Dockerfile.{server,rest,grpc,mcp,quic,cli}` and the image `release.yml` generates) and the `ci.yml` jobs that initialize a token. Build-only images and stages (`Dockerfile.builder`, `release.yml`'s binary legs, the `ci.yml` build job) no longer install SoftHSM at all: the binaries `dlopen()` the module at run time. Builds whose context cannot reach `scripts/` get it as the named build context `softhsm-pin` from their compose files. `test/scripts/softhsm-pin.test.sh` (in `make test-scripts`) fails on any distribution SoftHSM install, any Dockerfile or workflow using SoftHSM without the script, and an archive that does not match the pin. New `TestSupportedSoftHSM_ReportsTamperAsSealedDataAuthentication` (`pkcs11` tag) proves it on the images: it requires SoftHSM 2.7.0 or later (an image regressed to 2.6.x fails, naming the script) and that a flipped ciphertext, tag or nonce, truncation, extension, a mismatched or omitted AAD and a foreign key each fail `Unseal` with `types.ErrSealedDataAuthentication` and the token's own `CKR_ENCRYPTED_DATA_INVALID`. The minimum SoftHSM version for PKCS#11 tamper classification, 2.7.0, is documented in `docs/pkcs11-backend/`. Closes #1418.
- **The TPM policy registry stores go-qrdb DAO entities** -- `pkg/tpmpolicy` moved to `pkg/tpm2/policy`, and `policy.NewRegistry` now takes the go-qrdb DAO factory instead of a `storage.Backend`. Scopes, policies and assignments are entities in the registry's own `tpmpolicy` database. A store failure is a `*policy.StoreError`. `compose.TPMPolicyParams` and `compose.Deps` gain a required `DAOs` field; when it is missing, `compose.Build` says so. A factory that does not serve the `tpmpolicy` database fails with `*dao.DatabaseUnavailableError`. `compose.Databases(deps)` names the databases a host must open first. A host without a go-qrdb node builds its factory over one KV store with `dao.NewStoreFactory`. The `tpm-policies` compose store name is gone. Existing registry data is not migrated.
- **WebAuthn credentials are go-qrdb DAO entities on the injected factory** -- `pkg/webauthn` has one credential store, built by `NewQRDBUserStoreAdapter` from its new required `DAOFactory` option (entity type `webauthn_credentials`, default database); users stay go-qrdb's, and session state is unchanged. `BackendUserStore`, `BackendCredentialStore`, `MemoryUserStore` and `MemoryCredentialStore` are gone, along with `rest.WebAuthnStores`/`WebAuthnStoresConfig`; the adapter no longer needs a guarded KV client. `rest.NewServer` refuses a WebAuthn config without a pre-built service (`ErrWebAuthnServiceRequired`); `rest.HostConfig` and `rest.WebAuthnServiceParams` take a `DAOFactory`, which the API-module host and xkmsd supply from the datastore. Credentials stored by the old stores are not migrated.

### Removed

- **`pkg/acme/qrdb`, the ACME subsystem's own go-qrdb client facade, is removed** -- its `Service`/`Provider`, `New`/`WithConfig`/`WithKVStore`, `NewKVStoreAdapter`, `MemoryKVClient`/`NewTestService`, `ShutdownManager`, `RaftMetricsCollector`, error codes and predicates are gone, together with the SDK's `CAQRDB*` re-exports in `sdk/go/acme`. ACME storage is built from the injected go-qrdb DAO factory: xkmsd uses `objstore.NewFactory(ds.DAOFactory())` over the server datastore (`objstore.NewTenantAwareFactory` for the tenant-aware form). `admin.NewTenantAwareAdminService` and `client.WithQRDB` take the go-qrdb SDK client directly through the new `admin.QRDBClient` interface (`KV`, `Users`, `Roles`), which `*qrdbsdk.Client` satisfies; not-found is matched with `qrdbsdk.IsErrorNotFound`. `TrustedCA.QRDBService` is renamed `QRDBClient`.
- **xkms no longer re-hosts go-qrdb's auth-factor and cluster services** -- the REST `/api/v1/factors/*` routes, `GET /api/v1/cluster/status` and `GET /api/v1/cluster/members`, their `XKMSService` passthroughs, the TypeScript SDK's `FactorsClient` and `ClusterClient`, and the web console's Auth Factors and Cluster pages are removed. go-qrdb's `UserAuthFactorService` and `AdminService` serve them, registered on xkmsd's gRPC server and Unix socket; use the qrdb SDK client's `AuthFactors()` / `UserAuthFactors()` and `Cluster()` accessors, or `xkmsctl auth factor` and `xkmsctl cluster`. `xkms.ClusterClient` shrinks to the leader-endpoint lookup the not-leader redirect needs, and `XKMSService.SetClusterClient` drops its node-ID argument. The `/auth/me` `cluster` capability flag stays, and the console dashboard renders it as "clustered" or "standalone"; the `factors` capability flag is gone.
- **The `manual` and `barrier` credential strategies are go-qrdb's credential service** -- `pkg/server/credentials` now delegates them to `qrdbsdk.NewVersionedCredentialService` instead of carrying its own in-memory and barrier stores, and keeps only the hardware platform strategies (`tpm2`, `pkcs11`, `awskms`, `gcpkms`, `azurekv`, `vault`, `passphrase`). Behaviour follows go-qrdb's contract: a manual credential is held in a sealed enclave, a barrier read failure reports `ErrCredentialNotFound` and deleting a barrier credential also removes its version history. Stored barrier credentials keep the same `credentials/` keys and stay readable. `credentials.ErrManualEntryRequired`, which nothing returned, is removed.
- **The init ceremony's go-qrdb state aliases are removed** -- `pkg/init`'s `CeremonyState`, `StateAwaitingInit`, `StateEnrolling` and `StateOperational`, and the SDK's `InitCeremonyState` and `InitState*` re-exports, are gone. Use go-qrdb's `qrdbsdk.CeremonyState` and its `State*` constants directly. `pkg/init` keeps `SPKIPin`, `CAAdapter`, `EnrollAdminFactors` and `NewAdminFactorRegistry`.

## [0.50.0-alpha] - 2026-10-02

### Security

- **`device-attest-01` followed neither the draft nor a deployable design: the server dialed the device, and the shipped `xkmsd` could not start with the challenge enabled** (#737, #789, #1370 review). Four changes, made together because each was a blocker for enrolling an AVR/DICE device.
  - **The client POSTs the attestation; the server never contacts the device (draft-ietf-acme-device-attest).** The client answers the challenge with the payload `{"attObj": "<base64url, unpadded, of the CBOR attestation object>"}` and the server verifies it from the payload. The dial path is removed: `challengePath`, the `validation.Client` parameter of `deviceattest01.Verify`/`VerifyAttestation`, and `startAttestServer` in the Go client are gone, `AttestationChallenge.DialTarget` and `Port` are empty for this challenge, and the loopback-identifier substitution applies to `enroll-01` and `endorse-01` only (`dialsDevice`). A device needs no listener and no address, so one on a serial port enrolls through a gateway holding the ACME account. **Breaking for callers of the package:** `VerifyAttestation(verifier, payload, keyAuth)` replaces `VerifyAttestation(client, verifier, host, port, token, keyAuth)`, `Verify` likewise, and `AttestationRequest` is `{AttObj string}` (`json:"attObj"`) in place of `{AttStmt []byte}`. New `ParseAttestationRequest` and `EncodeAttestationRequest`, and `ErrAttestationPayloadInvalid` naming the layer that failed. `ChallengeHandler` reads the payload from the verified JWS and hands it to the verifier as `AttestationChallenge.Payload`. Freshness is unchanged: the attestation must cover the key authorization (`TPMExtraData`, `DICENonce`). `EnrollmentConfig.IPAddress`, `Port` and `ListenHost` are unused by `DeviceAttest`, and `IPAddress` is no longer required for it.
  - **A production verifier: `deviceattest01.TrustAnchorVerifier`.** `xkmsd` with `acme.challenges.device_attest01` enabled aborted at startup because the shipped CA cannot implement `AttestationVerifier` (it would be an import cycle). The verifier is now built from configured anchors and injected: `handlers.NewDeviceAttestVerifier(verifier)` and `ACMEAttestingVerifiers(client, enroll, endorse, deviceAttest)` take it as an argument. A `tpm` chain is anchored to `tpm_roots` with `evidence.VerifyAKCertificate`; a `dice` chain to `dice_roots` with `dice.Verify` (nonce, `Ueid`, and the `dice_require_device_signed_leaf`/`dice_require_measurement`/`dice_require_tcb_info` policy). The root sets are separate and a format with no root is refused (`ErrNoTrustAnchors`). New config `acme.challenges.device_attest` (`tpm_roots`, `dice_roots`, `dice_require_*`); `device_attest01` with no anchor fails validation (`ErrACMEDeviceAttestNoAnchors`) and `xkmsd` refuses to start (`ErrACMEDeviceAttestAnchors`). `ErrDeviceAttestCAUnsupported` and `requireDeviceAttestCA` are removed. SDK: `ACMETrustAnchors`, `ACMEDICEPolicy`, `ACMETrustAnchorVerifier`, `ACMENewTrustAnchorVerifier`, `ACMEDeviceAttestRequest`, `ACMEParseDeviceAttestRequest`, `ACMEEncodeDeviceAttestRequest`, `ACMEDeviceAttestStatement`, `ACMEDICENonce`, `ACMETPMExtraData` and the sentinels `ACMEErrNoTrustAnchors`, `ACMEErrNoAttestationVerifier`, `ACMEErrAttestationPayloadInvalid`. The EK-to-manufacturer chain is not re-proven for `tpm` (the statement carries no EK); it is proven by whoever issued the AIK certificate, for a go-xkms CA by `enroll-01`.
  - **A missing authorization refuses finalize.** `deviceAttestations` skipped an order's referenced authorization that storage did not hold, so after a partial restore `refuseForeignRequestForAttestedOrder` read zero records as "not a device-attest-01 order" and let a TCG-CSR or an `endorse-01` EK request through the key binding. `orderAuthorizations` now returns `ErrOrderAuthorizationMissing` (a `serverInternal` 500 problem) and the request is refused. SDK alias `ACMEErrOrderAuthorizationMissing`.
  - **The issued certificate asserts the attested identity.** The CA copies no otherName a CSR requests, so a device-attest-01 certificate carried no device identity. New `ca.SignOptions.OtherNames` (an issuer-asserted subjectAltName otherName, never copied from a CSR) lets finalize hand the CA the evidence-derived RFC 4043 `permanentIdentifier`. Available to SDK users through `TrustedCASignOptions`.
  - Verified by `TestChallengeHandler_DeviceAttest01_NeverDialsTheDevice`, `TestTrustAnchorVerifier*` (`anchors_test.go`), `TestStartACMEServer_DeviceAttestAnchors`, `TestOrderFinalize_MissingAuthorizationRefusesFinalize` (fails without the fix) and the client-to-server round trip `TestDeviceAttestRoundTripAgainstTheRealServer`, which no longer rewrites the dial target and runs against a server given no way to reach the device. Docs: `docs/acme/challenges.md`.
  - **Open:** the IAK certificates a go-xkms CA issues at `enroll-01` carry a subject, which WebAuthn section 8.3.1 (enforced by `checkAIKCertificate`) forbids in `x5c[0]`, so an `enroll-01` IAK certificate is not yet accepted by the `tpm` format. `dice` is unaffected. Reconciling the profiles is a decision for the owner.
  - Closes the device-attest-01 blockers of #737 and #789.
- **`device-attest-01` never bound the attested key to the certificate request's key, and no attestation challenge bound the attested device's identity to the order's authorized identifier** (#789, #828). `deviceattest01.VerifiedAttestation.BindCSRKey` existed but nothing in the ACME server called it, so a permanent-identifier order's finalize request signed any CSR; and a client could complete an attestation challenge with device A while claiming device B's identifier.
  - **Owner ruling on #828, option B: an optional, additive attesting-verifier interface.** `common.ChallengeVerifierFunc`, `Params.ChallengeMap` and the existing SDK functions are unchanged, and `http-01`, `dns-01` and `tls-alpn-01` are untouched. New `common.AttestingVerifier` (`VerifyAttested(resolver, ca, AttestationChallenge) (*AttestedIdentity, error)`, plus the `AttestingVerifierFunc` adapter) returns the attested identity and the `*entities.DeviceAttestation` to persist. Attestation verifiers register in the new `Params.AttestingVerifiers`; `sdk/go/acme.ACMEAttestingVerifiers` builds the map and `cmd/xkmsd/acme.go` registers it.
  - **`ChallengeHandler` fails closed for `enroll-01`, `endorse-01` and `device-attest-01`.** A type with no attesting verifier is refused (`unauthorized`), even if a plain `ChallengeVerifierFunc` is registered for it, and is not offered to clients. An `ip` identifier is refused (`unsupportedIdentifier`, `ErrAttestationIdentifierType`) without running the verifier. A mismatch between the attested identity and the order's identifier (constant-time compare) is `unauthorized` (`ErrIdentityMismatch`, never shown to the client). There is no `device-attest-01` special case in the handler.
  - **Identity per type.** `device-attest-01`: the AIK certificate's RFC 4043 `permanentIdentifier` for `tpm` (an AIK without one is refused), the TCG `Ueid` for `dice`. `enroll-01` and `endorse-01` implement the interface but attest possession, not a name, and report the order's own identifier, so their identity comparison is a tautology today; see Open below.
  - **Persistence and finalize.** The verified evidence is persisted on the challenge (`entities.ACMEChallenge.DeviceAttestation`) through the existing DAOs. `OrderFinalizeHandler` refuses with `badCSR` a CSR whose key is not the attested key, and fails closed (`badCSR`) when no attestation record exists.
  - **Behavior change: `"ip"` has no default challenge candidates.** `enroll-01` and `endorse-01` are removed from the default `"ip"` list (`xkmsDefaultIdentifierChallengeTypes`) because attestation never authorizes an `ip` identifier. A new-order for an `ip` identifier is refused up front as `rejectedIdentifier` with a 400 (`ErrIPIdentifierNotValidatable`) when the policy offers no non-attestation challenge for `ip`; an operator who sets `IdentifierChallengeTypes` for `ip` to http-01 or similar keeps that path. Devices authorize with `permanent-identifier`, which is what `acme-client` and the cluster joiner send.
  - **Behavior change: attestation verifiers registered only through `ChallengeMap` are refused.** `sdk/go/acme.ACMEAttestationVerifiers` is kept for source compatibility and marked Deprecated; its output is refused for attestation types. Callers move to `ACMEAttestingVerifiers`. `pkg/acme/client` gains `WithAttestingVerifiers`.
  - `device-attest-01` also emits the `DEVICE_ATTESTATION` audit event on success, gated like the other attestation events. New config flag `acme.challenges.device_attest01`. Typed errors: `ErrAttestationIdentifierType`, `ErrAttestingVerifierRequired`, `ErrAttestationNoIdentity`, `ErrIdentityMismatch`, `ErrDeviceAttestationNotFound`, aliased in `sdk/go/acme`. `sdk/go/acme.ACMEAttestingVerifiers` takes the device-attest-01 trust policy as an `ACMEDeviceAttest01Verifier` (nil leaves the challenge unregistered) rather than asserting it from the CA handle.
  - **Open (go-xkms#828):** the cluster SPIFFE hook (`NewPermanentIdentifierURISANHook`) still stamps the order's client-declared `permanent-identifier`; and the `enroll-01`/`endorse-01` identity comparison does not yet bite. Both need `enroll-01`'s order identifier separated from the address the server dials, and a source of truth mapping an attested device to its Raft address.
  - #737 (wire device-attest-01) is deployable: the client POSTs its attestation and `xkmsd` builds a production verifier from configured trust anchors; see `security-device-attest-01-client-posts-attestation-737-789.md`.
  - Fixes #789. Advances #828 and #737.
- **`endorse-01` proved nothing and was unauthenticated by default: any ACME account could obtain an EK certificate for any public key** (#1392, #1370 review). The verifier returned `nil` unconditionally, the only control was External Account Binding, and EAB was off by default (every account was then authorized).
  - **EAB is required by default, failing closed.** `Params.EndorseEABOptional` waives it and its zero value requires it, so a server built with no setting fails closed; `Params.EndorseEABRequired` is kept for source compatibility and is deprecated. `acme.endorse_eab_required` is now a `*bool` read through `ACMEConfig.EndorseEABIsRequired`: unset means required. To waive it (a closed lab server only) set `endorse_eab_required: false` or `XKMS_ACME_ENDORSE_EAB_REQUIRED=false`; the server then logs a warning for every endorse-01 challenge. **Behavior change** for deployments that relied on the old open default.
  - **The EAB must name the EK it authorizes, and that is the attested identity.** `EndorseEABValidator` binds the EK by `deviceInfo.ekPublicKeyHash` (SHA-256 of the EK's PKIX DER in hex, optionally `sha256:`-prefixed as the admin API reference shows; the field existed and was documented for this but never read) and/or `endorse_device_id_meta_key`. A binding naming neither is refused (`ErrEndorseEABKeyNotBound`) because it authorizes its account for any key; a different EK is refused (`ErrEndorseEABKeyMismatch`). `ChallengeHandler` hands the EAB-authorized identity to the verifier (`AttestationChallenge.AuthorizedIdentity`) and the new `handlers.NewEndorseVerifier` reports it, refusing without one (`ErrEndorseNoAuthorizedIdentity`); the endorse-01 verifier no longer echoes the order's identifier. **Behavior change:** a batch binding that names no EK, previously accepted when EAB was required, is refused; register each device's EK with it. `endorse01.Verify` is deprecated.
  - **What kind of order it is comes from the challenge that validated it, in one decision.** Finalize classified an order as endorse-01 from the bytes of its identifier in two places (the checks and issuance), so a device-attest-01 identity that decodes as a public key was checked as a device order and then issued an EK certificate for the identifier's key. Both now follow the same decision, derived from the validated challenge.
  - **An endorse-01 authorization may finalize only the EK-certificate path.** The EK-certificate request now requires endorse-01 to be the only attestation challenge that validated the order (the converse of the #789 check, which only excluded device-attest-01), and an endorse-01-validated order cannot finalize a TCG-CSR-IDEVID, IDevID, cluster node or device-attest-01 certificate request (`ErrFinalizeRequestNotPermitted`, `badCSR`). Commit 36c830bd began this.
  - **No MakeCredential proof of possession.** It needs the server to reach the device (the order's identifier is the EK, not an address, so there is nothing to dial; the separation of identifier and address is the open question on #828) or a second request on the challenge, and either changes the protocol. EAB bound to the key is the control; documented in `docs/acme/challenges.md`.
  - SDK: `ACMENewEndorseVerifier`, `ACMEErrEndorseEABKeyNotBound`, `ACMEErrEndorseEABKeyMismatch`, `ACMEErrEndorseNoAuthorizedIdentity`, `AttestationChallenge.AuthorizedIdentity`. #1393 (SPIFFE) is out of scope.
  - Verified by `TestChallengeHandler_Endorse01_RefusedWithoutEABByDefault`, `TestChallengeHandler_Endorse01_AnotherEKThanTheBoundOneIsRefused`, `TestEndorseEABValidator_RefusesABindingThatNamesNoKey`, `TestOrderFinalize_EKCertificate_OnlyForAnEndorse01Order` and `TestOrderFinalize_TCGCSR_EndorseValidatedOrderIsRefused`, each failing without the fix; `TestNewRestService_EndorseEABRequiredByDefault` and `TestLoad_ACMEEndorseEABRequired`. Docs: `docs/acme/challenges.md`, `docs/acme-issuance/api.md`.
  - Closes #1392.
- **`enroll-01` finalize did not bind the TCG-CSR-IDEVID to the TPM that passed credential activation** (#1391, #1370 review). Activation at the challenge proves a TPM holding one endorsement key and one activation key answered, and nothing recorded which. The TCG-CSR arrives one request later, so a client that passed the challenge once could submit one built in software around another device's *public* EK certificate and be issued an IDevID carrying that device's identity.
  - **The challenge records the activated TPM.** `enroll01.VerifyActivation` (new; `Verify` is now a wrapper) returns the `Activation` (the EK certificate and the IAK's TPMT_PUBLIC read from the CSR the credential was made for), and the enroll-01 attesting verifier returns it as `AttestedIdentity.Attestation`, persisted on the challenge as an `entities.DeviceAttestation` with `Format: "enroll-01"`: `DeviceIdentityValue` is the EK certificate's TCG permanent identifier, `LeafDER` the certificate, `PubArea` the IAK. The identifier comparison is kept and is real for enroll-01: the dial that proved a genuine TPM answered reached the address the identifier names.
  - **Finalize refuses a TCG-CSR for any other TPM.** `bindEnrollActivation` requires the CSR's EK certificate to have the recorded permanent identifier and its IAK public area to be the recorded one; no record is refused too (`ErrEnrollActivationNotFound`, `ErrEnrollActivationMismatch`, `badCSR`). New `ca.EKCertificatePermanentIdentifier` is the single derivation of the identifier, shared with the IAK/IDevID issuance (`sdk/go` `EKCertificatePermanentIdentifier`).
  - **The validated challenge decides the finalize request** (`validatedAttestations.requireOnly`, `ErrFinalizeRequestNotPermitted`): a TCG-CSR-IDEVID needs enroll-01 to be the only attestation challenge that validated the order. An `endorse-01` or `device-attest-01` authorization can no longer be finalized as a TCG-CSR, and neither can an order no attestation challenge validated (an `ip` identifier `http-01` validated, which was issued an IDevID with no TPM check). **Behavior change** for any client that finalized a TCG-CSR for such an order.
  - SDK: `ACMEVerifyEnroll01Activation`, `ACMEEnroll01Activation`, `ACMEEnroll01Format`, `ACMEErrEnroll01ActivationUnreadable`, `ACMEErrEnrollActivationNotFound`, `ACMEErrEnrollActivationMismatch`, `ACMEErrFinalizeRequestNotPermitted`.
  - Verified by `TestOrderFinalize_TCGCSR_AnotherTPMsEKIsRefused` and `TestOrderFinalize_TCGCSR_AnotherIAKIsRefused` (activate TPM A, finalize a TCG-CSR built around TPM B's EK certificate or a software IAK; both fail without the fix), `TestVerifyActivation_*`, `TestBindEnrollActivation` and `TestACMEAttestingVerifiers_Enroll01RecordsTheActivatedTPM`. Docs: `docs/acme/challenges.md`.
  - Closes #1391.

### Added

- **`sdk/go` exports the request chain a host composes around an embedded go-qrdb node: the bearer bridge, the pre-authentication IP limiter, request correlation and the object scope rule.** `NewQRDBBearerAuthenticator` (`pkg/auth`, moved from xkmsd's internal `pkg/server/qrdb_bearer.go`) carries a host's session tokens into the node's chain through `WithAuthenticators`, reading the authenticator in force from an `AuthenticatorSource` (`*LiveAuthenticator` is one; `Authenticator`, `LiveAuthenticator` and `NewLiveAuthenticator` are exported too) and never admitting through the no-op authenticator or none (`ErrBearerNotAccepted`); xkmsd registers the same type. `NewIPRateLimiter`, `IPRateLimitMiddleware`, `IPRateLimit{Unary,Stream}ServerInterceptor`, `IPRateLimitKey`, `ParseTrustedProxies`/`TrustedProxies` and their errors export `pkg/ratelimit`. `CorrelationMiddleware`, `Correlation{Unary,Stream}ServerInterceptor` and the context helpers export `pkg/correlation`, which now owns the HTTP middleware and gRPC interceptors xkmsd's REST router and gRPC server install (they moved out of `pkg/api/rest` and `pkg/api/grpc`; a metadata key present with an empty value now counts as absent). `ObjectScope*`, `ScopePrincipal`, `ScopeTarget`, `ScopePrincipalOf` and the keyspace helpers and errors export `pkg/scope`. Exported-API growth.
- **A Local Attestation Key (LAK), certified by the IAK, carries the WebAuthn Level 2 §8.3.1 TPM attestation profile; the IAK's TCG DevID certificate is unchanged.** TCG DevID v1 r12/v1.10 r9 §8 requires the IAK certificate's Subject to be a unique X.500 DN; WebAuthn §8.3.1 requires the "tpm" attestation statement's AIK certificate Subject to be empty, and go-webauthn enforces this literally. Resolved per TCG "TPM 2.0 Keys for Device Identity and Attestation" v1.10 r9 §5.3/§6.3 ("Owner Creation of a LAK Certificate based on an IAK Certificate"): `pkg/tpm2.(*TPM2).CreateLAK` creates the LAK as a Restricted, Sign-only child of the Platform SRK (not an Endorsement-hierarchy primary like the IAK/IDevID) and persists it via `TPM2_EvictControl`; `CertifyLAK` has the IAK certify it via `TPM2_Certify`; `ca.IssueLAKCertificate` verifies that evidence (the IAK certificate chains to a trusted signer and is within its validity period, then `tpm2.VerifyCertifyByCertificate`) and issues a certificate with an empty Subject, a critical subjectAltName directoryName carrying tcg-at-tpmManufacturer/tpmModel/tpmVersion, the tcg-kp-AIKCertificate (2.23.133.8.3) EKU alone, and Basic Constraints CA:false (`ca.NewTCGLocalAttestationKeyProfile`). xkey's TPM-backed WebAuthn/FIDO2 authenticator (`keybackend.TPM2AttestingBackend`) now attests with the LAK via `CertifyKeyWithLAK`, never the IAK. `pkg/certstore`'s `StoreCertificate`/`StoreCertificateChain` key a certificate with an empty Subject by its SPKI SHA-256 thumbprint (`certstore.CertificateKey`, using qrdb's canonical `ComputeSPKIThumbprint`) instead of refusing it with `ErrInvalidCN`. Verified on the TPM simulator: LAK creation and IAK-TPM2_Certify-LAK, `ca.IssueLAKCertificate`'s success and failure paths (tampered certify info, wrong IAK, an IAK not chained to a trusted root, missing device attributes, a non-empty-Subject certificate refused the way go-webauthn's own verifier refuses it), and an end-to-end "tpm" attestation statement produced from the LAK verifying under go-webauthn. See `docs/tpm2/engineering.md` and `docs/certificate-authority/engineering.md`. (go-xkms#715)
- **A backend-held secret key's `CKA_VALUE` stays sealed until the C boundary** -- `pkcs11/module.Attribute` gains `Secret *secure.Buffer`, `ValueLen`, `WithValue` and `Release`, and `ReleaseAttributes` releases a slice of them. `GetAttributeValue` returns a revealable backend key's value in `Secret` rather than `Value`, the C export copies it out and releases it, and a Go caller reads it with `ValueLen` or `WithValue` and releases it with `ReleaseAttributes`. The value never sits on the ordinary heap between the backend and the C caller. Part of #1398.
- **`pkg/attestation/peergate`: the verifier behind go-qrdb's attested-caller gate, with the evidence cache it reads and the collector that fills it.** go-qrdb's `PeerAttestationGate` (installed with `node.WithPeerAttestationGate`) asks a `PeerAttestationVerifier` whether the peer on a gated connection is currently attested; go-xkms now supplies it, so a host composes the gate from the two SDKs and writes no verification code. `Collector.Challenge` issues a single-use 32-byte nonce to the peer named by the connection's verified client certificate (go-qrdb's SPKI thumbprint), `Collector.Submit` accepts the evidence answering it, bound to the submitting TLS session through the exporter and stamped with the receipt time, into an `EvidenceStore` (`MemoryStore`: bounded, evicting only evidence past its retention, never aliasing). `Verifier.VerifyPeer` re-verifies the stored evidence on every call with `pkg/attestation/peer` under the provisioned policy bound to the session it arrived on, and maps the verdict onto go-qrdb's absence/cryptographic classes; with `DeviceIdentity` set it also requires the connection certificate to be an IDevID naming the same TPM as the attestation key (new `peer.VerifySameDevice`, `*peer.DeviceMismatchError`), closing the relay a channel binding alone leaves open. `QuoteEvidence` is the quoting side over any `Quoter` (`*tpm2.TPM2` is one) and re-quotes when a PCR is extended between the quote and the read. Exported through `sdk/go` (`NewPeerGateVerifier`, `NewPeerEvidenceCollector`, `NewPeerMemoryEvidenceStore`, `PeerQuoteEvidence`, `PeerVerifySameDevice` and their types and errors). `make integration-test-peergate` composes a go-qrdb node with the verifier and drives quotes from swtpm: the gated route admits the peer after a valid bound quote and refuses it with no evidence, after a forged quote, after a quote bound to another TLS session and with evidence older than the gate's maximum age. Docs: `docs/attested-peer/`. Exported-API growth.

### Changed

- **An audit query reads only the caller's own tenant, the system tenant included.** go-qrdb v0.28 removed `audit:read:cross` and confines every audit query to the caller's tenant on every transport, with no system-tenant exception. `XKMSService.QueryAudit` now does the same before the query reaches the node: the filter's tenant is always the caller's own (normalized; `system` for an absent identity or one with no tenant), whatever `tenant_id` the request named, and no Authorizer decision is consulted. A system-tenant Admin no longer reads other tenants' events or an empty "every tenant" filter; it reads the system tenant's events plus the untenanted platform events. `auth.ActionReadCross` is removed (breaking for a caller that named it). A narrowed query still succeeds with the narrower result rather than an error, on REST, gRPC, Unix, QUIC and MCP. Docs: `docs/audit-log/`, `docs/rbac/`.
- **The permitted-authentication-method check is go-qrdb's (BREAKING).** `pkg/auth.CheckAuthMethod`, `auth.MethodWebAuthn` and `auth.AuthMethodNotPermittedError` are removed. The mTLS authenticator, the PIV login and the WebAuthn account-standing check call `qrdbsdk.CheckAuthMethod`, the function qrdb's own middleware runs, and a refusal is `*qrdbsdk.AuthMethodNotPermittedError`. Stored policy entries are now compared in qrdb's canonical form (trimmed and lowercased) rather than as stored, so an entry written with different case or surrounding space now matches as it does on qrdb's planes.
- **OIDC token persistence moved onto go-qrdb's DAO/entity pattern** -- `pkg/oidc.BackendTokenStore` (a raw `storage.Backend` `Put`/`Get` pair) is deleted; `pkg/oidc.DAOStore` (`NewDAOStore(kv qrdbsdk.KVStore)`) replaces it with the same `TokenStore` behavior (`Save`/`Load`/`Delete`/`List`/`Close`, the same `ErrTokenNotFound`/`ErrInvalidIssuer`/`ErrStoreClosed` sentinels) over a go-qrdb DAO keyed by normalized issuer. `pkg/oidc.DatabaseName` ("oidc") names the go-qrdb database the DAO declares itself into. `pkg/datastore` gains `DatabaseKVStore`/`ClientBackend`, the one way a composition root resolves a feature's own named go-qrdb database (created on demand via go-qrdb's `Client.Database()`, scoped via `Client.DatabaseScoped`, with a per-database backend override through the new `datastore.databases:` config list) -- see docs/datastore/architecture.md's "Feature-owned databases". xkey, which hosts no go-qrdb node, reaches the same DAO through `sdk/go.NewKVStoreAdapter` over its existing barrier-backed backend (`xkey/pkg/gui/services/oidc_service.go`'s `SetBackend`); its default storage engine stays `file`. `sdk/go/oidc` re-exports `DAOStore`/`NewDAOStore`/`DatabaseName` in place of `NewBackendTokenStore`.
- **`types.Password.String()` no longer returns the secret** -- `String()` is now `String() string` (it was `String() (string, error)`) and every implementation (`ClearPassword` in `pkg/types`, `pkg/password` and `pkg/tpm2/store`, `RequiredPassword`, `PlatformPassword`, `backend.StaticPassword`, `backend.NoPassword`) returns `types.PasswordRedacted`, so formatting or logging a Password cannot leak it and no unwipeable Go string is minted from protected bytes. The interface gains `WithBytes(func([]byte) error) error`, a borrower that also carries the "unreadable" signal the error of `String()` used to (`RequiredPassword` returns `ErrPasswordRequired`, a cleared `pkg/password` password `ErrPasswordZeroed`, an unsealable `PlatformPassword` `ErrPlatformPasswordUnavailable`), so TPM session setup still fails closed. `Bytes()` is documented as a caller-owned copy the caller must wipe. Custom `Password` implementations must be updated. Closes #1401.
- **PINs and Seal/Unseal passwords cross the transports as `types.SecretBytes`** -- `PIVSignRequest.PIN`, `ImportPIVKeyRequest.PIN` and the password fields of the Seal and Unseal requests are `types.SecretBytes` (exported through `sdk/go` as `SecretBytes`) instead of `string`, in the transport types and in the REST, MCP and protobuf conversions, so a PIN or password is never a Go string that cannot be wiped. The JSON form is byte-identical, so existing clients and stored requests are unaffected; Go callers pass `[]byte`-backed values, and the consumer of a request wipes the PIN it carried on success and on every refusal. The gRPC `SealRequest.password` and `UnsealRequest.password` fields change from `string` to `bytes` for the same reason; both are length-delimited on the wire, so existing gRPC clients interoperate unchanged, and the generated `xkms.pb.go` is regenerated for those two fields only. Part of #1398.
- **Ceremony holder certificates name the registered holder, never the CSR (go-qrdb v0.28 contract).** Officer, custodian and `init sign-csr` certificates signed by the init ceremony and by the ACME admin plane's ceremony are now `CN=<registered username>`, `OU=<scope tenant>`, `OU=<profile>` (one RDN each), with no subject alternative name and only the CSR's key; previously the CSR's subject and names were copied, so registering an officer with a CSR for `CN=admin, OU=system` minted a login as the system tenant's admin. `pkg/init.CAAdapter.SignCSR` and the ACME admin adapter pass go-qrdb's `SignCSROptions.RawSubject` through the new `ca.SignOptions.RawSubject` (`TrustedCASignOptions.RawSubject` in `sdk/go`), which the CA writes verbatim while copying none of the CSR's names; combining it with another source of names is `ca.ErrRawSubjectWithNames`, a malformed one `ca.ErrInvalidRawSubject` (`ErrCARawSubjectWithNames`, `ErrCAInvalidRawSubject`). No SPIFFE SAN is stamped on a holder certificate any more (go-qrdb refuses one); the SO certificate the CA issues keeps it. The adapters also stop forwarding go-qrdb's holder label as an xkms CA profile name, which a real CA refused with `ca: profile not found`. Nil sign options are refused with `ErrNilSignOptions`.
- **go-qrdb v0.28.1-alpha.** Every module moves to go-qrdb and its `sdk/go` v0.28.1-alpha. go-qrdb v0.27 serves leases on a standalone node, so a clustered-config xkmsd advertises its API endpoints on a standalone qrdb node too, and the OIDC credential locker takes a real lease there (it keeps its in-process fallback for a backend that refuses leases). The init-ceremony and audit consequences of v0.28 have their own entries. xkms's object scope rule (`pkg/scope`) still lets a system-tenant identity, or a request with no identity, address every tenant's shared and service objects; go-qrdb v0.28 no longer grants that lift, and the decision for xkms is #1406.
- **The secure-analyzer gate classifies and fails go-qrdb v0.25's rules 4-7, and this repository carries no analyzer directives** -- `scripts/secure-analyzer-key.sh` recognises the v0.25 diagnostics (unborrowed `Buffer.Bytes`, a malformed `//secure:unborrowed` directive, a string conversion of protected bytes, an unwiped copy-out) as rules 4-7, which have no allowlist key and always fail the sweep; an unrecognised message is a hard failure rather than an unkeyed pass. The selftest plants a finding for each rule, proves each fails under its own classification, and now keeps its own assertion failures instead of resetting them. The analyzer fixtures reach `secure` through `sdk/go/secure`. The six remaining allowlist entries (four go-truststrap#60 imports, two `ssh.ParsePrivateKey` calls) are all still matched. Part of #1398.
- **`vaultkey.Sealed.Secret` becomes protected memory read through `TakeSecret`** -- the exported `Secret []byte` field is replaced by an atomically held `*secure.Buffer` that stays in locked memory until `TakeSecret` hands it to the caller exactly once (the caller wipes the returned slice) or `Destroy` discards it unread; a second `TakeSecret` returns `*SecretTakenError`, and a failed read returns `*ProtectError`. `staticpw` takes the secret this way. Every `Sealed` must end in one of the two calls. Part of #1398.
- **xkey and phone-backend secrets leave Go strings** -- the last string boundaries the securecheck v0.25 sweep found are now wipeable bytes or protected memory, with every JSON and archive wire format byte-identical (proved against records and archives written with string fields, including a backup whose checksum covers the encoded bytes). Go types change: `phone.Config.NoiseStaticKey` is `types.SecretBytes`; `oath.Credential`, `backup.OATHCredentialInfo`, `backup.PasswordInfo` and `cdp.StoredCredential` replace `SecretString()`, `PasswordString()` and `PrivateKeyString()` with `Secret()`, `Password()` and `PrivateKey()` returning a caller-owned `[]byte` copy the caller wipes, and `SetSecret`, `SetPassword` and `SetPrivateKey` take `[]byte` and copy it; `oath.Credential.ToURI` returns `(string, error)`; `OIDCStoredToken` token accessors return `[]byte`; and `backup.Archive`, `sync.OATHDelta` and `sync.PasswordDelta` and the pairing sync and OATH messages carry their secrets as the new `types.SecretText` (protected memory with `Destroy`), whose owner destroys it after use. `types.SecretText` and `types.SecretBytes` (now also a `TextMarshaler`, escaping like a string) are exported through `sdk/go` with `SecretTextError` and `SecretBytesError`. Part of #1398.

### Fixed

- **The `DeviceAttest` client sent its IP address as the order identifier, which the attested-identity check of #828 refuses** (#789, #1370 review). The order now names the device's own identity: `TPMModule` gains `DeviceIdentity` (the IAK certificate's RFC 4043 `permanentIdentifier`), read by the new exported `deviceattest01.DeviceIdentityFromCertificate`, the rule the server applies to the evidence (the `dice` form is the lowercase-hex `Ueid`). `sdk/go/acme` aliases it, with `ACMEAttestedKey`, `ACMEDeviceAttestObject`, the identity sentinel errors and the attestation formats. The simulator IAK certificate (`tpm2test.ProvisionIAKCertificate`) now carries a `permanentIdentifier`.
  - **Finalize binds the key of the device the request names.** The binding no longer depends on the order's first identifier (a `dns` identifier ahead of a `permanent-identifier` skipped it), and with several devices in one order it selects the attestation record of the `permanentIdentifier` the CSR names rather than the first recorded.
  - A TCG-CSR-IDEVID or endorse-01 finalize request for an order a `device-attest-01` challenge validated is refused (`badCSR`); it carries keys nothing attested and used to skip the key binding. A device identity that happens to decode as a public key is no longer taken for an endorse-01 order.
  - An `ip` identifier is declined (`rejectedIdentifier`) when no non-attestation challenge with a registered verifier remains, instead of being offered `device-attest-01` or failing with a 500.
  - A TPM leaf with two `permanentIdentifier` otherNames is refused as ambiguous.
  - The dial this client's identity would have broken is gone: see `security-device-attest-01-client-posts-attestation-737-789.md`.
- **A real arduino-generic device could not enroll through `device-attest-01`: its identity was invisible to the server, and nothing proved the path end to end** (#737). The AVR alias certificate has room for one extension, so it states the device's ueid as CWT claim 256 of its `tcg-dice-UCCS-evidence` and carries no `tcg-dice-Ueid` extension. `DeviceIdentity` and `dice.Verify` read only the extension, so the identity gate refused every genuine AVR device (and `RequireUeid` could never be met by one).
  - **`dice.DeviceUeid` reads both.** It returns the `tcg-dice-Ueid` extension when present and the UCCS claim 256 otherwise, and refuses a certificate stating two different values (`dice.ErrUeidConflict`) rather than choosing one. `dice.Verify`, `deviceattest01` (`DeviceIdentity`, `DeviceIdentityFromCertificate`) and the AVR backend (`Attestation.Ueid`) use it. SDK: `DICEDeviceUeid`, `DICEClaimUeid`, `ErrDICEUeidConflict`.
  - **End-to-end proof against the real firmware.** `TestDeviceAttestDICEEnrollsTheRealFirmware` and its refusals (`pkg/acme/client/device_attest_dice_e2e_test.go`) run arduino-generic's element-tier simulator (`agsim.StartElement`: the real firmware compiled for the host, with a model of the ATECC608A that does real P-256) through `Client.DeviceAttest` and the real ACME handlers, with the production `TrustAnchorVerifier` anchored on the DeviceID key. The device mints its alias certificate over `DICENonce(keyAuthorization)`; the order's identifier is the hex ueid; finalization binds the CSR to the alias key and the issued certificate carries the ueid as its `permanentIdentifier`. Refused: an order for another ueid (`unauthorized`), evidence over another challenge's nonce and untrusted roots (`incorrectResponse`, told apart by the reason the verifier recorded), and a CSR for another key (`badCSR`).
  - **The simulator is built, never skipped.** `make agsim` builds `agsim` and `agsim-atecc608a` from the arduino-generic module at the version `go.mod` pins into `AGSIM_DIR` (`scripts/build-agsim.sh`), refusing source whose module hash is not the one in `scripts/agsim.sum`; `make test`, `make race` and `make coverage-full` depend on it, and the `test-changed` and `race` CI jobs run it. A missing binary fails the test with the command to run.
  - Pins `github.com/jeremyhahn/arduino-generic/sdk/go` to v0.7.0-alpha (root and `sdk/go`), which returns the 164-byte `Device.Attest` frame with its fields in place and adds the `sdk/go/agsim` launcher.
  - **Open (arduino-generic):** a physical AVR cannot finish this enrollment. The alias key is the DeviceID key and `Client.DeviceAttest` must sign the CSR with the attested key, but the firmware has no command that signs a host-supplied digest or CSR (`Backend.Signer` returns `ErrSigningUnsupported`). The end-to-end test signs the CSR with the simulator's published test private key, which exists only for the simulator. Closing it takes either a signing command in the firmware or an alias key distinct from the DeviceID key, both arduino-generic decisions.
  - Closes #737.
- **The gRPC rate-limit interceptors and `Limiter.AllowConn` bucket IPv6 peers on their /64.** The HTTP middleware already folded a client address through `RateLimitKey`; the gRPC interceptors and the raw-connection check keyed on the full address, so an IPv6 client could escape the limit on those transports by rotating through addresses in its own delegation.
- **AES-KW, AES-KWP and RSA-AES wrap emit ciphertext as ordinary bytes** -- the last of the six RFC 3394 passes now writes its result into a plain slice instead of the wrapped key being copied out of the protected register buffer with `secure.CopyOut`, so callers of `WrapAESKW`, `WrapAESKWP` and `WrapRSAAES` no longer inherit a copy-out obligation on public data and `WrapRSAAES` no longer wipes the ciphertext it assembles. Output bytes are unchanged (RFC 3394 and RFC 5649 vectors pass). Part of #1398.

## [0.49.0-alpha] - 2026-10-01

### Added

- **`sdk/go/oidc`, `sdk/go/urlsafety` and `xkms.OpenTPMDevice`: the OIDC client core, the URL launch guard and the TPM device opener through the SDK.** v0.48.0-alpha moved the OIDC core to a shared `pkg/oidc` and wired `xkmsctl oidc`, xkey's OIDC commands and GUI services, xkey's AWS sign-in and xkey's TPM probes straight to `pkg/oidc`, `pkg/urlsafety`, `pkg/api/transport` and `pkg/tpm2/tpmdev` -- which the Architecture Gates job forbids (xkey and xkmsctl production code depend on `sdk/go` only). `sdk/go/oidc` re-exports the client side of `pkg/oidc` (templates and flows, `Provider`/`Client`, PKCE, state, DPoP, the loopback callback listener and the token stores) as aliases, `sdk/go/urlsafety` re-exports `ValidateLaunchURL`, and `xkms.OpenTPMDevice` re-exports `tpmdev.Open` with its refusal of the host's hardware TPM inside a test binary. xkey and xkmsctl now import these, and the OIDC credential client types from the existing `sdk/go/transport`; `xkmsctl`'s vault key factors use the existing `sdk/go` storage, key-type, service-backend and `sdk/go/localtpm`/`sdk/go/vaulttoken` re-exports. Exported-API growth, so this is a MINOR release.

### Changed

- **`vaultkey.Sealed.Secret` is a `*secure.Secret`, not a `[]byte`.** A freshly sealed key-factor secret is plaintext key material; v0.48.0-alpha returned it in an ordinary slice, which the secure-analyzer's rule 3 rejects. `vaultkey.Seal` now computes the key-check value and moves the secret straight into protected memory (`secure.NewSecret` wipes the drawn bytes), returning `*vaultkey.ProtectError` if that fails; the caller owns the Secret and must `Destroy` it. `pkg/staticpw`'s key-factor enrollment and `pkg/vaulttoken.SelfTest` hold it that way end to end. Breaking for any caller that read `Sealed.Secret` as bytes.

### Fixed

- **`main` is green again: gofmt, the secure-analyzer gate's rule table, and the sdk/go-only import gates.** v0.48.0-alpha was pushed to `main` without a CI run and left `Lint`, `Static Analysis` and `Architecture Gates` red (the last because `xkmsctl` and xkey's commands imported `pkg/*`; see the `sdk/go/oidc` entry). `make fmt-check`: eight files carried a stray blank line gofmt removes, and `pkg/pkcs11/module/module_keygen_quantum_test.go` returned two composite literals in one `return`, a shape Go 1.27's gofmt re-indents inconsistently -- it now builds both slices first. `make secure-analyzer`: go-qrdb v0.25 reworded rule 1 ("is forbidden; use ...") and added rule 4 (unborrowed `secure.Buffer.Bytes`) and the `securecopy` analyzer, so `scripts/secure-analyzer-key.sh`'s verbatim message table classified none of them -- every finding failed as an unknown message and the four go-truststrap#60 memguard entries read as stale while the imports they exempt were still there. `rule_for` now matches both rule-1 wordings, rule 4 and securecopy (the four memguard entries stay: go-truststrap's fix for #60 is on its main but not yet in a tag); rule 4 and securecopy findings are never allowlistable (their only exemption is the analyzer's own per-site directive). `make secure-analyzer-selftest` now plants a rule-4 and a securecopy violation and fails if any message the pinned analyzer emits does not classify, so the next go-qrdb bump that rewords a rule fails on its own pull request. `docs/release-engineering/user.md` now states that the CI-only gates must pass on a pull request before anything reaches `main`.
- **Every go-qrdb v0.25 secure-memory finding is fixed at its site.** go-qrdb v0.25's vet tool added rule 4 (a `secure.Buffer.Bytes` read with no borrow held across it) and `securecopy` (a copy of protected bytes that is never wiped, returned or consumed, and any `string(...)` of protected bytes); v0.48.0-alpha shipped 118 such findings across the root module, `sdk/go` and xkey. Reads now go through `Buffer.WithBytes` or `secure.CopyOut` (go-qrdb `sdk/go/secure`), copies are wiped with `defer secure.Wipe` right after they are made, buffers are filled through `WithBytes` rather than through `Bytes()`, and the AES key-wrap paths in `pkg/crypto/wrapping` run each wrap under a single borrow of one register buffer. The remaining sites carry the analyzer's own per-site directive with the reason it holds: `//secure:unwiped` where an interface or wire format requires a string (`types.Password.String`, backup and CDP serialization, OIDC token accessors) or hands the value to its caller by contract (PKCS#11 `C_GetAttributeValue` of `CKA_VALUE`), and `//secure:unborrowed allocates-protected` where the callee allocates protected memory of its own and so cannot run inside a borrow. Behaviour is unchanged except that a destroyed `pkg/password` buffer now makes `String()` return `ErrPasswordZeroed`, and a failed PIN borrow in `pkg/fido2` returns `ErrPINTokenFailed` instead of hashing nothing.

## [0.48.0-alpha] - 2026-10-01

### Added

- **Web console: manage your password-vault factors and recover a locked vault.** The Passwords view gains *Vault factors* (list your factors; add a passphrase, change one in place, remove a factor -- the server's refusal to remove the last one is shown) and *Use recovery code* on a locked vault (recovery code plus a new passphrase; the next code is shown once). The TS SDK types the vault status's `recovery` factor (`PasswordVaultFactorInfoType`). Covered by vitest component tests and a Playwright mock-API spec (`e2e/password-vault.spec.ts`).
- **Server-side OIDC credentials: `pkg/oidc/credential`, a service that holds named OAuth/OIDC logins on the tenant barrier and keeps them fresh.** A credential is tenant-shared or personal (`pkg/scope`: `{tenant}/oidc/shared/{name}`, `{tenant}/oidc/users/{subject}/{name}`); a personal credential is visible to its owner only, never to the system tenant. A login arrives by a device flow the server runs (`StartDeviceLogin`/`PollDeviceLogin`) or by importing tokens (`Create` with tokens, `ImportTokens`). `GetAccessToken` returns a current access token by reference, refreshing first inside the refresh margin (default five minutes) and still serving a valid token when the provider is briefly down. A rotating refresh token is redeemed under a per-credential lock -- an in-process mutex plus, on a raft cluster, a qrdb lease -- and persisted with the barrier's compare-and-swap, so concurrent consumers cause exactly one refresh. A rejected refresh (`invalid_grant`, `refresh_token_reused`, ...) moves the credential to `relogin_required` and emits `oidc_credential.relogin_required` (subscribers and the audit log); a non-refreshable token (the `anthropic` template) is tracked to its expiry and moves to `expired`. A scheduler started with `Start` refreshes every due credential in every unsealed tenant, on the node holding the `xkms/oidc/scheduler` qrdb lease; a standalone node, whose qrdb refuses the raft-only lease family, is its own leader.
- **OIDC credentials on every xkmsd surface, `xkmsctl oidc`, xkey's server mode, the SDKs and the web console.** REST `/api/v1/oidc/credentials` (list, create, and per credential `{scope}/{name}`: get, delete, `import`, `refresh`, `token`, `device`, `device/poll`); gRPC/Unix `OIDCCredential{Create,Import,Get,List,Delete,Refresh,GetAccessToken,DeviceStart,DevicePoll}`; MCP `oidc.credential.*`; the QUIC, MCP, REST, gRPC, Unix and embedded client transports (USB: not served by the phone). Permissions `oidc_credentials:{create,get,list,update,delete,token}`, xkms-owned and ScopeSelf; Admin and Owner hold all, the built-in User role `get`, `list` and `token`. Errors classify through `apierrors.OIDCCredentialClassOf`. xkmsd builds the service (and its scheduler) whenever it has a barrier registry and its qrdb node; an embedding host's module composes it from `Deps.Leases` (the host qrdb client's `Coordination()`), feature `oidc-credentials`. `xkmsctl oidc templates|create|login|import|list|get|token|refresh|delete` (`import --codex-auth`, `token --codex-auth-out`). xkey: with an xkmsd configured the existing `xkey oidc` commands act on server credentials (`providers add/list/remove`, `login --provider`, `token`, `refresh`, new `import`), `providers list` shows both backends, and `--local` keeps the local backend; without an xkmsd, xkey's local OIDC is unchanged. Go SDK: the transport types, `CodexAuthFile`, `ParseCodexAuth`, `BuildOIDCCredentialService`; TS SDK: `client.oidcCredentials` with `waitForDeviceLogin`; the web console's OIDC Credentials view (`#/oidc/credentials`, capability `oidc_credentials`). Docs: `docs/oidc-credentials/`.
- **`pkg/oidc` gains the device flow, token-only providers, rotating-refresh handling, re-login classification and the OpenAI and Anthropic templates.** `Client.StartDeviceAuthorization`/`PollDeviceToken` implement RFC 8628 (`authorization_pending`, `slow_down`, `access_denied`, `expired_token` as typed errors) and OpenAI's own device login (`DeviceStyleOpenAI`: `/api/accounts/deviceauth/usercode` and `/token`, the returned code exchanged form-encoded at `/oauth/token`), both taken from openai/codex `codex-rs/login/src/device_code_auth.rs`. `NewEndpointProvider` builds a provider from explicit endpoints with no discovery; exchange and refresh need only a token endpoint. `TokenResponse.InheritFrom` keeps a refresh response's rotated refresh token and inherits an omitted one (RFC 6749 §6); `ExpiresAt`/`JWTExpiry` read an access token's `exp` when the endpoint reported no expiry. `ReloginReason`/`ReloginRequired` classify `invalid_grant`, `refresh_token_expired`, `refresh_token_reused`, `refresh_token_invalidated` and HTTP 401 as needing a new login, and token error bodies are now read in OpenAI's nested `{"error":{"code","message"}}` and top-level `code` shapes too. `ParseCodexAuth` imports a codex `auth.json`; `CodexAuthTokensFile` renders one in the `chatgptAuthTokens` mode, in which codex never refreshes (verified against codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs), with the refresh token left empty. New templates: `openai` (issuer `https://auth.openai.com`, public client `app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann`, token endpoint `https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token`, JSON refresh body, device + import) and `anthropic` (the one-year `claude setup-token` token: import only, never refreshed). xkey's local provider picker lists only browser-login templates, so it is unchanged.
- **Password vault integration suite.** `make integration-test-password-vault` (replacing `integration-test-xkey-password`, whose local-store tests it folds in and brings up to date) runs every vault factor on its real token against a real xkmsd in the devcontainer -- passphrase, passkey on xkey's virtual authenticator, certificate key, TPM on swtpm under `platform` and a named policy, PIV on SoftHSM -- with recovery, two-user isolation and the browser bridge through the real native host. Shared harnesses: `test/integration/xkmsdtest` (a real xkmsd) and `test/integration/xkeytest` (the virtual authenticator, now also used by the logins suite). Fixes it found: xkmsctl's passkey verbs take `--device` to name the security key; `xkey password vault|unlock --key` log in to a PIV card or PKCS#11 token named by `--pkcs11-token`/`--pkcs11-library` (or the config's `piv` section) with `XKEY_PIV_PKCS11_PIN`; xkmsctl, xkey and `pkg/localtpm` open a TPM over TCP as `--tpm-device tcp://host:port`.
- **Storage: fenced create.** go-qrdb v0.25.0's tenant service creates a tenant only when its metadata store can write the record while it and the tenant's tombstone are absent, in one atomic step (`kvstore.FencedCreator`). xkms's storage stack gains that optional capability, `storage.FencedCreator` (`PutIfAllAbsent`): the engine backends decide it under their guarded-write lock, `qrdb.Backend` as one consensus transaction, and the prefix, file, LUKS, sealed and barrier wrappers forward it or report `storage.ErrFencedCreateUnsupported` -- never a check followed by a write. xkms's own tenant composition (`seal.NewHardwareTenantService`, used when the qrdb node's barrier is not engaged) creates tenants again. Held to a shared contract suite (`storagetest.RunFencedCreateContract`).
- **Password vault key factors on every client: xkmsctl, the xkey CLI and GUI, and the web console through the xKey extension.** `pkg/vaulttoken` (`sdk/go/vaulttoken`) is the one client implementation: it finds a key factor's token in an xkms key backend (a PIV backend's slot 9d key, a PKCS#11 token, a TPM 2.0 key, a software key), self-tests it before enrollment (`SelfTest`: a token that cannot open a secret sealed to its own key is refused), builds the enrollment, and recovers a vault factor's secret (`Find`, `UnlockCredential`). xkmsctl: `password vault enroll|recover --key-factor piv|certificate|tpm` and `password unlock --key`, with a PEM key (`--key-file`, `--cert-file`), a PKCS#11 token (`--key-pkcs11-module`, `--key-pkcs11-token`, `--key-pin`; needs a `-tags pkcs11` build, the CGO-free release answers `ErrVaultPKCS11Unavailable`) or a TPM (`--tpm-keystore`, `--tpm-create` under the built-in platform policy). xkey CLI: the same `--key-factor` / `--key` over xKey's local key store (barrier password flags); xkey GUI: *Add key*, *Unlock with key*, recovery with a key. **Browser bridge:** the console's *Unlock with xKey* asks the xKey extension (window.postMessage), whose worker forwards the browser-attributed origin of the top frame over encrypted native messaging to xKey (new IPC `vault` message); xKey refuses any origin that is not the connected server's console (https on its WebAuthn relying party domain), refuses factors that are not in the vault it reads itself, asks the user to approve (`vault:browser_unlock_request`, two-minute timeout), and unlocks the vault itself over its own connection -- the page receives only `{unlocked: true}`, never a key or secret. Without the extension the console says the factor needs it (`XkeyExtensionUnavailableError`). xKey's local key-store backend configuration is shared between the GUI and the CLI (`config.KeyBackendConfigs`).
- **Password vault key factors on the server: PIV (slot 9d), certificate and TPM keys.** A key factor is enrolled with the key's public key or certificate; the server draws a fresh 32-byte secret sealed to it (`pkg/vaultkey`: ECDH-ES with an HKDF-SHA256 KDF for EC P-256/P-384/P-521, RSA-OAEP-256 for RSA of 2048 bits or more), wraps the DEK under a key derived from the secret, and keeps only the sealed challenge, a key-check value and the key's SPKI SHA-256 fingerprint. To unlock, the private key's holder recovers the secret (`vaultkey.Open`, through any xkms key backend: `NewBackendToken`) and sends it with the fingerprint. The server cannot unlock alone and the DEK never leaves it. New wire fields on every transport (`public_key`, `certificate`, `key_fingerprint`, `key_ref`; factor `key_algorithm`, `key_challenge`, `key_check`, `certificate_subject`), new factor types `piv`, `certificate`, `tpm`, and `ErrVaultKeyExists` (409). The last-factor refusal now reads "cannot remove the last unlock factor".

### Changed

- **go-qrdb v0.25.1-alpha.** Every module moves to go-qrdb and its `sdk/go` v0.25.1-alpha, go-quicraft v0.15.0-alpha and go-enclave v0.6.1-alpha. Consumer-visible changes: `sdk/go/secure` drops the memguard-era `CatchInterrupt`, `EnablePurge`, `Purge`, `PurgeOrPanic` and `NotInitializedError` for `WipeAll` (a binary defers it at startup; xkmsd's teardown is now the single `enclave.WipeAll`); `types.NewLiteralSecretValue` returns `(*SecretValue, error)`, failing when the value cannot be sealed; `xkmsctl cluster add` takes `--identity` (the replica's `spki:` Raft member identity); the `sdk/go/dek` re-export and `QRDBTenantKeyManager` alias are removed, as go-qrdb removed what they aliased. In xkmsd, go-qrdb now owns `GET /health` (its node health) and `GET /v1/ca/bootstrap`, which it serves from xkmsd's CA bundle (`WithBootstrapCABundle`); the xkms module no longer registers either, and the bootstrap route no longer takes the `store_type`/`algorithm` filters. go-qrdb v0.25.1 changes the Raft WAL format: an existing data directory does not open, so upgrade from an empty one.
- **The password vault and its session moved off the entries namespace, to `/api/v1/password-vault`.** `GET /api/v1/password-vault` (vault status), `GET /api/v1/password-vault/session` (was `GET /api/v1/passwords/status`), `POST /api/v1/password-vault/unlock` and `/lock`, `POST /api/v1/password-vault/factors`, `PUT|DELETE /api/v1/password-vault/factors/{id}` and `POST /api/v1/password-vault/recover` replace the `/api/v1/passwords/vault...`, `/unlock`, `/lock` and `/status` routes. `/api/v1/passwords/{id}` now holds entries only, so an entry named `vault` or `status` is fetched by name like any other. The REST and QUIC client transports, the MCP path map, the TypeScript SDK (`passwords.unlock/lock/status/vault*`, unchanged method names) and the web console follow; gRPC, MCP method names and permissions are unchanged. No compatibility aliases: the stack is pre-v1 with one wire format.
- **Personal password entries no longer reveal names or folders to the tenant key.** A personal entry's ID is now `HMAC-SHA-256(K, lower(folder/name))` (128 bits, 32 hex characters) with `K = HKDF-SHA256(DEK, "xkms/staticpw/personal/v1/names")`, keyed per user, instead of the public xxhash of the name and folder; personal folder markers and aliases are stored under the same MAC of their text, with the folder path in the DEK-sealed value. Holding the tenant barrier key now shows only that a user has a vault, how many personal objects it holds, their sizes and when they change (documented in `docs/password-vault/architecture.md`). Shared, system and xkey-local stores keep the public `GenerateID` scheme. **No migration:** personal vaults written before this change are not read back under the new keys; the only deployment holding them (the burn-in node) is being rebuilt from zero.
- **The OIDC core is one shared package, `pkg/oidc`, used by xkey and xkmsd alike.** The client (authorization code + PKCE, refresh, DPoP, userinfo, revocation), discovery, provider templates, the loopback callback and the token-store abstraction (`TokenStore`, `MemoryTokenStore`, the barrier-backed `BackendTokenStore`, the DAO store) moved from `xkey/pkg/oidc` to `pkg/oidc`, and the URL-safety helpers it depends on from `xkey/pkg/urlsafety` to `pkg/urlsafety`. xkey's local OIDC is unchanged: same providers, flows, refresh loops and storage; only its imports moved. The AWS-specific login and the output handlers stay in `xkey/pkg/oidc/aws` and `xkey/pkg/oidc/handlers`.
- **The User role stores passwords.** The password manager is a store for users, so the built-in User role now holds `passwords:write` and `passwords:delete`: users create, change and delete their personal entries and share entries with their tenant (without `passwords:delete` an owner could not delete even their own entry). Updating or deleting a shared entry stays with its owner or an Admin/SO, as the service already enforced.
- **Password-vault passkeys are created for the server's WebAuthn relying party, and the web console enrolls and unlocks with them.** The fixed relying party `xkms-password-vault` is gone: a browser refuses a non-domain ID, so a passkey from the CLI could never open in the console. The vault status now advertises `passkey_rp_id` (the configured `webauthn.rp_id`; a host module passes `WithServiceModulePasswordVaultRelyingParty` or its WebAuthn config), every passkey factor records the `rp_id` it was created for, and every client -- `pkg/vaultpasskey` (xkmsctl, the xkey CLI and GUI) and the new `sdk/ts` `enrollVaultPasskey`/`unlockVaultPasskey` (WebAuthn PRF, `userVerification: "required"`, `prf.evalByCredential`) -- creates for the advertised ID and evaluates with the recorded one. With no relying party configured, passkey enrollment answers `ErrVaultPasskeyUnavailable` (REST 412, gRPC FailedPrecondition); another relying party is `ErrVaultRelyingPartyMismatch` (400). A browser or key without PRF is the typed `VaultPasskeyPrfUnsupportedError`, never a fallback. The console creates a vault with a passkey, unlocks with one, recovers with a new one and adds one from *Vault factors*. Cross-surface secret vectors (`pkg/fido2/testdata/vault_passkey_secret_vectors.json`) are checked by `pkg/vaultpasskey` and `sdk/ts`; a Playwright spec runs enroll and unlock through Chrome's WebAuthn stack with a CDP virtual authenticator with PRF. **No migration:** passkeys enrolled for `xkms-password-vault` are not carried forward (the burn-in node is being rebuilt).
- **One `xkey auth login` serves every transport to that server.** A stored login is now bound to the server's identity, not to the URL it was made through.
  - The identity is qrdb's SPKI SHA-256 thumbprint (`ComputeSPKIThumbprint`) of the TLS leaf certificate the server presents. It is read with the same trust as the call, from a TCP handshake for `https`/`grpcs`/`mcps` and a QUIC handshake for `quic`. New package: `xkey/pkg/serverid`.
  - A login made over `https://` therefore serves `grpcs://`, `quic://` and `mcps://` to the same server on any port, while a different certificate on the same host is a different server and never receives it. A reissued server key needs a fresh login.
  - On a Unix socket, the new `XKMSD_SERVER_NAME` / `xkmsd.server_name` selects the login by the host it was made to; a name matching two servers is refused (`AmbiguousServerNameError`).
  - `TokenEntry` gains `ServerID` and `ServerName`. `tokenstore.LoginToken` takes a `ServerRef` and picks the newest login of that server.
  - The CLI (endpoint, share, SSH) and the GUI connection resolve logins this way. The GUI reads the server name from `xkmsd.server_name`.
  - `xkey auth login --piv` no longer requires a WebAuthn `auth register` first: an unregistered server is reached by its URL and verified by the auth root pool.
  - The OIDC credentials integration suite logs in once with `xkey auth login --piv` (key on a SoftHSM token) over REST and uses that login on unix, REST, gRPC, QUIC and MCP. It also checks that a decoy server on the same host with another certificate receives no Authorization header.
- **xkey SSH is server-backed when connected and local when offline, CLI and GUI.** The same switch `xkey oidc` makes:
  - CLI: a configured xkmsd (the full `resolveXKMSdEndpoint` chain, any scheme; previously only `XKMSD_URL`/`xkmsd_url`, always as REST) makes every `xkey ssh` command server-backed unless `--local` is given (new flag). Server calls present `XKMSD_TOKEN` or the stored login, the CA bundle and the `XKMSD_TLS_CERT`/`XKMSD_TLS_KEY` client credential.
  - GUI: `SSHService.SetServerClient` replaces the never-wired `SetRemoteClientFunc`. While a server is connected the SSH key view runs on it (an explicitly chosen local backend is refused with `SSHLocalBackendConnectedError`); a server whose SSH API cannot be dialed fails closed with `SSHServerUnavailableError` instead of quietly using local keys; on disconnect it returns to the local store. `ConnectionService.SSHClient` dials the connected server's SSH API with the connection's trust and login.
  - SDK: `client/ssh.NewClientForServerWith(server, ServerOptions{TLSConfig, Token})` takes a full `tls.Config` (client certificate, SPKI pin) and presents the token on every transport. gRPC (`GRPCOptions.TLSConfig`, `AuthToken`), gRPC over a Unix socket (local credentials) and MCP (`MCPOptions.AuthToken`) carried no token before. `NewClientForServer` delegates to it.
- **xkey presents the stored login on its server calls, CLI and GUI.** `xkey auth login` stored a session token that only the GUI's API explorer read (from an always-empty in-memory store). Now:
  - `pkg/tokenstore` gains `Open` (the file-backed store `xkey auth login` writes, shared by the CLI and GUI) and `LoginToken` (no login is no token; an expired login is a `*LoginExpiredError` naming `xkey auth refresh`);
  - every CLI server call (`resolveXKMSdEndpoint`, the share client) presents `XKMSD_TOKEN` when set, otherwise the login stored for that server URL. The lookup never creates the xKey home or the store;
  - the GUI opens the same store (`xhome.Home.AuthDir`): a server connection presents the login stored for its URL and refuses an expired one, and the API explorer reads the real store instead of an empty one.
