- **xkmsctl: TPM vault keys under named policies; PIV/PKCS#11 are xkey's.** xKey's local TPM policy service (registry, policy authority, NV indexes, approval counter) moved to the shared `pkg/localtpm` (`sdk/go/localtpm`), which xkey and xkmsctl both run. `xkmsctl password vault enroll --key-factor tpm --tpm-create --tpm-policy <name>` now creates the key under a named policy in `--tpm-data-dir` (which replaces `--tpm-keystore` and shares xkey's data-directory layout); `ErrVaultTPMNamedPolicy` and `ErrVaultTPMUnavailable` are gone. xkmsctl stays CGO-free with no PKCS#11 build: `--key-factor piv` and the `--key-pkcs11-*`/`--key-pin` flags are removed, and PIV/PKCS#11 factors answer `ErrVaultKeyNeedsXkey` ("use xkey for PIV/PKCS#11 factors"). `make test` now runs the pkcs11 vault tests (`test-pkcs11`) and xkey's TPM simulator tests.

### Fixed

- **A barrier over an xkms storage backend now performs its guarded compare-and-swap.** go-qrdb's `StorageBarrier.CompareAndSwap` asserts its base for the two-value `CompareAndSwap(...) (bool, error)`; `pkg/seal`'s `guardedStorageBackend` forwarded only xkms's three-value shape, so every swap on a barrier over an xkms backend -- xkmsd's system barrier among them -- failed with "storage backend has no guarded swap". The wrapper now adapts the backend's `storage.CompareAndSwapper` to the barrier's shape (a base without the capability is still refused, never approximated by read-then-write). The OIDC credential service persists rotating refresh tokens with it. Tests: `pkg/seal/barrier_adapter_compareanddelete_test.go`.
- **A multi-node xkmsd cluster forms again on go-qrdb v0.25.x.** go-quicraft admits a Raft member by its identity and nothing else, and xkms had no way to pass one, so every multi-node boot failed with "no node identity in Config.MemberIdentities". `cluster.member_identities` (`XKMS_CLUSTER_MEMBER_IDENTITIES`, "nodeID=spki:<hex>" pairs) is mapped onto qrdb's `raft.member_identities`. Test: `pkg/server` `TestBuildXKMSQRDBConfig_ClusterFields`.
- **The cluster integration suite runs green against passphrase-barrier nodes.** The nodes boot sealed; the harness now initializes each node's barrier through its sealed window (allowed off loopback only on the private compose network), unseals a node it restarts, reads the first-boot admin credential from the datastore, finds node containers by compose project and service rather than a container name that never existed, sends `key_type` as the purpose with an explicit `algorithm`, and gives the standalone node a SAN for the name the suite reaches it by. The sealed-window client and the initialize/unseal calls are exported from `test/integration/xkmsdtest` (`SealedWindowClient`, `ReadBarrierState`, `InitializeBarrier`, `UnsealBarrier`, `OpenBarrier`) so the cluster harness reuses them rather than copying them.
- **The gRPC and MCP client transports now carry the authentication material a caller configures, and xkey can present an mTLS client credential to xkmsd.** The gRPC transport ignored a caller-built `tls.Config` (`transport.WithTLSConfig`, which `sdk/go`'s `WithTLS` and xkey use), so a CA bundle supplied in memory was never the trust anchor and every TLS connection fell back to the system pool; it now uses the given configuration (TLS 1.3 minimum). Neither gRPC nor MCP sent `transport.WithJWTToken`: gRPC now presents it as `authorization: Bearer` per-RPC metadata (TLS only -- a bearer token never crosses plaintext, so a token on a plaintext `grpc://` connection is refused at dial), MCP as an `Authorization` header. xkey reads `XKMSD_TLS_CERT` / `XKMSD_TLS_KEY` for an mTLS client credential, which the unified server's gRPC and MCP transports require for module calls. Found by the OIDC credentials integration suite driving xkey over every transport. Tests: `pkg/api/transport/grpc/transport_bearer_test.go`, `pkg/mcptool/client_bearer_test.go`, `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/xkmsd_client_test.go`.
- **PKCS#11: ECDH finds a PIV slot's key.** `Backend.DeriveKeyECDH` looked its private key up by `CKA_LABEL` built from the common name and algorithm, while `Signer` and `Decrypter` resolve the `CKA_ID` (a PIV slot's own ID for a slot key). A slot 9d key generated by `xkey piv generate` was therefore found for its public half but not for the agreement, so a PIV vault factor on a PKCS#11 token could not unlock. The agreement now resolves the key exactly as the other operations do.
- **The offline PKCS#11 module initializes again after `C_Finalize`, and raw `CKM_ECDSA` signs on in-process keys** — `libxkms_pkcs11.so` in offline mode (`XKMS_PKCS11_MODE=local`) answered `CKR_DEVICE_ERROR` to a `C_Initialize` that followed `C_Finalize`: `Module.Finalize` drops the embedded client the library injected, and `C_Initialize` rebuilt the offline module only when no global module existed, so the finalized module fell back to dialing the default remote target. PKCS#11 v3.2 §5.4 allows re-initialization, and `p11-kit server` always performs it (a probe initialize/finalize, then the RPC client's initialize), so no p11-kit-hosted deployment could come up. `cmd/pkcs11-module` now records the module it built and rebuilds it under one lock when that module has been finalized; a module a Go caller installed (xkey) is still initialized as it is and never replaced. Separately, a raw ECDSA signature (hash `NONE`, PKCS#11's `CKM_ECDSA`, which strongSwan's pkcs11 plugin uses) failed on every in-process key with `ecdsa: Sign must be called with a hash, not with crypto.Hash(0)`, because Go 1.27's `ecdsa.PrivateKey.Sign` refuses a zero hash identity; `signWith` now signs a raw digest on an `*ecdsa.PrivateKey` through `ecdsa.SignASN1`, which accepts a digest of any length and truncates it to the curve order as PKCS#11 v3.2 §6.3.4 requires. The other signers were audited: the PKCS#11 signer issues raw `CKM_ECDSA` itself; the TPM2 signer infers the scheme hash from a 32/48/64-byte digest and refuses any other length with the typed `ErrSchemeHashUnresolved`/`ErrUnsupportedOperation`; AWS KMS and GCP KMS refuse a zero hash with their typed `ErrInvalidAlgorithm`. Azure Key Vault's signer ignored the zero hash and always sent ES256, so a raw digest on a P-384 key failed remotely. It now takes the algorithm from the key's curve (P-256/ES256, P-384/ES384, P-521/ES512) and refuses a digest of another length with the new typed `ErrRawECDSADigestUnsupported` before any request is sent. Tests: `TestCInitialize_OfflineReinitializesAfterFinalize` (both seal strategies: initialize, generate a P-256 token key, sign and verify, finalize, initialize, find the key, sign and verify), `TestCInitialize_OfflineLeavesInjectedModuleInPlace`, `TestCInitialize_OfflineBuildFailureIsDeviceError`, `TestSignDigest_*`, `TestSign_RawECDSA_ThroughService` (32/48/64-byte digests through the service), `TestOffline_RawCKMECDSA` (raw `CKM_ECDSA` sign and verify on P-256 and P-384 with 32/48/64-byte digests in offline mode; a changed digest fails), `TestRawECDSAAlgorithm` and `TestSigner_RawECDSA` (azurekv). (#1386)
- **xkmsd with a `passphrase` (or `shamir`) barrier and network transports starts again.** The pre-boot sealed-window listener serves the node's pending-boot transports, which are TLS-only, but `serveSealedWindow` passed it no TLS material, so start-up failed with "cannot start REST transport: no TLS configured and no CeremonyCA available". xkmsd now hands the window the same unified TLS configuration the full server serves (`Server.sealedWindowTLS`, set where `buildUnifiedTLSConfig` runs). Tests: `pkg/server/sealed_window_test.go` (`TestServeSealedWindow_NetworkServingUsesUnifiedTLS`: the window serves the unified certificate over TLS and the boot completes after unseal); the OIDC credentials integration suite now runs xkmsd with a passphrase barrier initialized through the window.
- **TCG CA calls use one canonical path on every transport.** The server serves the TCG CA at `POST /api/v1/ca/tcg/{ek,ak,sign-csr,enroll}`, and the REST and QUIC transports call it there, but the Unix transport posted to a nonexistent `/api/v1/tcg-ca/{issue-ek-cert,issue-ak-cert,sign-tcg-csr,enroll-device}`, so EK/AK issuance, TCG CSR signing and device enrollment over the Unix socket always failed. The MCP transport's path-to-tool table carried the same stale spelling. Both now use `/api/v1/ca/tcg/*`, and the stale spelling is gone from the tree.
- **No test can reach the host's hardware TPM without an explicit opt-in.**
  - **Runtime guard:** opening a TPM character device now goes through one leaf package, `pkg/tpm2/tpmdev`. In a test binary (`testing.Testing()`), or in any process run with `XKMS_DENY_HARDWARE_TPM=1`, it refuses `/dev/tpm*` and `/dev/tpmrm*`, symlinks resolved, unless `XKMS_TEST_HARDWARE_TPM=1` is set (`ErrHardwareTPMInTest`). `make test` exports the deny flag, so a binary a test runs as a subprocess is held to it too.
  - **Openers routed through it:** every opener goes through `tpmdev`:
    - `pkg/tpm2` (`NewTPM2`, `Open`, `OpenDeviceTransport`), where a refusal is still `ErrOpeningDevice`, joined with the cause;
    - `pkg/luks`'s default opener;
    - `pkg/crypto/rand`'s TPM resolver;
    - xkey's enroller probe and EK probe;
    - the TPM integration test's hardware fallback;
    - the `tpm2` certificates example.
  - **Static guard:** `TestNoTPMDeviceOpensOutsideTpmdev` parses every Go file in the repository (all modules, test files included). It fails on any go-tpm path opener (`linuxtpm.Open`, `transport.OpenTPM`, `tpmutil.OpenTPM`), or any `os.Open`/`os.OpenFile` of a TPM or device argument, outside `tpmdev`. A short allowlist covers non-TPM devices (uhid).
  - This follows the provision tests, which sealed their barrier to a host's real TPM through auto-detection.
- **TPM 2.0 backend: RSA keys decrypt.** `Backend.Decrypter` used to refuse every key ("does not implement crypto.Decrypter") and its unreachable decrypter loaded the key without authorizing it. An RSA key now returns a decrypter that runs `TPM2_RSA_Decrypt` (RSA-OAEP, SHA-256, empty label) authorized by the key's own policy session through `TrustedPlatformModule.RSADecrypt`, which now takes the key's attributes and loads it itself, so it works for keys under a named TPM policy; other schemes are refused with `ErrDecryptionNotSupported` rather than answered with a different one, and EC keys report that they agree (`DeriveKeyECDH`) instead.
- **TPM 2.0: closing a TPM reached over TCP or a Unix socket releases the connection.** `TPM2.Close` closed device files and the simulator but never the network transport `NewTPM2` opened for a `CommandAddress` (swtpm) or a `.sock` device, so a long-running process held its connection until it exited -- and swtpm, which serves one client at a time, blocked every other client meanwhile (for about two minutes per call in the vault integration suite). `NewTPM2` also closes the connection when it fails after dialling.
- **The Unix-socket transport presents the login JWT.** `transport.WithJWTToken` reached the server on REST, QUIC, gRPC and MCP, but the Unix transport's gRPC channel carried no call credentials, so a token-authenticated caller lost its identity over the socket. The bearer credentials now live in one shared package, `pkg/api/transport/grpcauth`, used by both the gRPC and Unix transports. The Unix transport dials with gRPC local credentials instead of insecure ones, which states what the socket is (no network path) and lets the bearer token ride it.
- **The xKey GUI frontend type-checks clean, and `make test` keeps it that way.**
  - `svelte-check` reported 15 errors and 2 warnings; all are fixed.
    - Type drift: `pin_max_attempts` on `SetupChoices`, `sealer_backend` on `GUIConfig`, and a stale `backend_id` on the password add/update params, which the Go service never had.
    - The `clickOutside` action now declares its `on:clickoutside` event through Svelte's `ActionReturn`.
    - Smaller fixes: an async function typed `void`, a `size="small"` button, nullable backend capabilities, dead CSS, and a documented-but-unrendered console title.
    - One was a real bug: the Admin view dropped each backend's `metadata`, so YubiKey detection by library path and the slot re-probe on connect never ran.
  - `make test` (`test-web`) now runs the xKey frontend's `svelte-check --fail-on-warnings` and its vitest suite, neither of which `make test` ran before.
- **A Wails bindings drift guard.** `make check-wailsjs` (run by `make test`) regenerates the bindings with the wails CLI at the version `xkey/go.mod` pins (as `pkg@version`, so its dependencies stay out of xkey's module) and the tags `wails.json` names, then fails on any difference from the committed `xkey/frontend/wailsjs`. `make generate-wailsjs` regenerates them. Five binding files are committed as 0755, the mode the generator writes, so regeneration leaves the tree clean.
- **xkey: `TestApp_RegisterPKCS11XKMSBackend_FactoryNotRegistered` no longer fails in a `pkcs11` build.** The test assumed its binary was built without the `pkcs11` tag, but xkey's Makefile builds tests with it by default (`WITH_PKCS11=1`), so the factory existed and the precondition failed. The case now lives in `app_pkcs11_absent_test.go` (`!pkcs11`), and a `pkcs11` build runs `app_pkcs11_present_test.go` instead, which proves registration fails closed when the PKCS#11 module cannot be loaded.
- **xkey's software PIV keys persist, encrypted at rest.** The software PIV backend kept keys in the generating process's memory only, so `xkey piv generate --backend software` made a key no later `piv csr`, `cert request` or `auth login --piv` could use.
  - Software PIV keys now live in xKey's key store: the barrier's `keys/` namespace, the store the GUI and the vault key factors use. It is opened by the existing `localKeyBackends` and handed to the PIV manager through `InitPIVBackendResolver`, as PKCS#11 does. No new crypto.
  - Without a barrier the backend refuses (`ErrPIVSoftwareKeyStoreRequiresBarrier`).
  - The `piv` group, `auth login` and `cert request` take the barrier password flags.
  - Generating into a slot now replaces the slot's previous key in a key-persisting backend, instead of failing with "key already exists" (`PIVRekeyError` if it cannot).
  - Tests cover generate in one process and use in another, both in-process and with the real xkey binary in the OIDC credentials suite, and check that no private key is stored in plaintext.
  - The provision tests no longer reach the host's real TPM: they pointed TPM auto-detection at the default device, so on a host with a TPM they sealed to it.
- **The xKey GUI's Wails bindings are regenerated in full.** Earlier changes had edited them by hand, one service at a time, and they had drifted from the Go services across 41 files: missing methods on `OIDCService`, `PINService`, `PhoneService`, `TrustService`, `StorageService` and `FIDO2Service`; stale signatures on `StaticPasswordService`, `SealService` and others; and the `SSHService` server switch (`Connected`, `SetServerClient` and `SetServerUnavailable` replace `SetRemoteClientFunc`). `wails generate module` was run over the committed tree. `svelte-check` reports the same errors before and after, so the regeneration introduced no frontend type errors, and the frontend's vitest suite passes.
- **xkmsd's session tokens authenticate on every unified-server transport.** The embedded qrdb node's own auth chain (gRPC, MCP) knew only mTLS, so a token xkmsd minted, accepted on REST, was refused there with `no_peer_cert`.
  - xkmsd now registers a bearer authenticator on the node through qrdb's `WithAuthenticators` seam (`pkg/server/qrdb_bearer.go`). It reads the request's Authorization through qrdb's `HTTPAuthorizationFromContext`, which every transport feeds (go-qrdb v0.25.0). It declines with `ErrUnauthenticated` when there is no bearer token, verifies with the live xkms authenticator (reloads apply), and never admits a request through the no-op authenticator.
  - It reports its method as unobservable (`UnobservableMethodAuthenticator`): a session token says who, not how. Its issuers therefore enforce the account's permitted-method policy when they mint. WebAuthn already did; the PIV/mTLS login now does too (`CheckAuthMethod` for `mtls`), so an account that may not use a certificate gets no token.

## [0.47.0-alpha] - 2026-10-01

### Security

- **Remote PKCS#11 tokens no longer lose keys on file storage.** System-scope token records were keyed under an empty path segment (`pkcs11state//<token>/`) that file storage collapses, so a remote-mode module loaded none of its objects and its next key reused handle 1, overwriting an existing key. The system scope is now stored under `pkcs11state/system/<token>/`; existing system-scope remote tokens must be re-provisioned (pre-release, no migration). The service also refuses a token label of `.` or `..` (`ErrPKCS11StateTokenDotSegment`) and a key or list prefix with `.`/`..`, empty interior or leading-`/` segments (`ErrPKCS11StateKeyPath`), which a path-normalizing store would resolve outside the token's namespace.
- **`pkg/staticpw`: `VaultCredential.Secret` is now `*secure.Secret`, and `pkg/testutil/vaulttest`'s `SimulatedKey.PIN` test double follows the same rule.** The passphrase, hmac-secret output, and recovery code a vault factor wraps a DEK under were held as a plain `[]byte` struct field; they are now sealed in protected memory at the servicer boundary (`vaultCredential` in `pkg/xkms`) and opened only to derive a factor's key-encryption key (`vaultFactor.kek`) or check its length (`VaultCredential.validate`), each time destroying the opened buffer immediately after use. Wire and transport types (`transport.PasswordVaultCredential`, the REST/gRPC/MCP request types) are unchanged — they remain the plaintext boundary the analyzer does not flag. Closes the secure-analyzer rule-3 findings on `pkg/staticpw/vault.go` and `pkg/testutil/vaulttest/simkey.go` (go-xkms#1384).
- **A TPM2 object or NV index bound to the platform policy could be used without satisfying it.** Every keyed-hash object `pkg/tpm2` sealed, and every RSA, ECDSA and AES key it created, kept `userWithAuth` SET. Under TPM 2.0 the object's USER role then also answered its `authValue`. That value was empty when the object had no password, so a plain empty-password `TPM2_Unseal`, `TPM2_Sign`, `TPM2_RSA_Decrypt` or `TPM2_EncryptDecrypt2` worked on any platform state, never evaluating the PCR policy. An object with a password answered that password alone, outside the policy. Platform-policy NV indices had the same flaw through `TPMA_NV_AUTHREAD`/`AUTHWRITE` and their always-empty auth value. Passwordless objects and indices had a second open path: the platform policy was `PolicyOR(PolicyPCR, PolicyAuthValue)`, and its `PolicyAuthValue` branch is satisfied by an empty `authValue`.
  - **Affected:** the platform store's sealed PKCS#11 PIN (`credential://`), `tpmpolicy` scope secrets, `xkmsctl seal --tpm-policy platform` without `--password`, every platform-policy TPM2 key, and every platform-policy NV index. The barrier's `TPM2Strategy` root key sealed without credentials, and FROST TPM2 shares, were sealed with neither a policy nor a password; their only protection was the Platform SRK's authorization at `TPM2_Load`. Objects bound to a named policy already had `userWithAuth` cleared and were not affected.
  - **Proof:** every path was proven on the simulator, before and after the fix (`pkg/tpm2/seal_policy_bypass_simulator_test.go`, `pkg/tpm2/object_policy_simulator_test.go`).
  - **One shared fix (`pkg/tpm2/object_policy.go`).**
    - `bindObjectPolicy` binds every child object at creation: `sealKeyInternal`, `CreateRSA`, `CreateECDSA` and `CreateSecretKey`. An object with an `authPolicy` gets `userWithAuth` CLEAR, so its password counts only through `PolicyAuthValue` inside the policy. A passwordless platform-policy object gets the `PolicyPCR` branch alone (`platformPCRPolicyDigestFromPin`). An object with a password keeps the `PolicyOR`, so the recovery PIN still works after a platform change.
    - `objectSession` answers the USER role at every use: unseal, `Sign`, `ECDHZGen` and `RSADecrypt`. It reads the policy from the object: the named-policy binding record, else the loaded object's `authPolicy` read back with `TPM2_ReadPublic`. A passwordless platform object gets a `PolicyPCR` session (`platformPCRSession`), so it is used correctly even when the caller's attributes name no policy, as xkey's `LocalTPMPolicies.UnsealObject` does.
    - Platform-policy NV indices (`NVWrite`, `NVDefineCounter`, `NVDefineExtend`) are defined with the `PolicyPCR` branch alone and without `TPMA_NV_AUTHREAD`/`AUTHWRITE`. Reads go through `TPMA_NV_POLICYREAD`, chosen from the index's own attributes, or through the owner.
  - **`RSADecrypt` signature change.** `TPM2.RSADecrypt` now takes `(keyAttrs, backend, ciphertext)`; it was `(handle, name, ciphertext)`. It loads the key and authorizes it through `objectSession`. Before, it presented no authorization at all, so a key with a password or a policy could not decrypt through `pkg/backend/tpm2`.
  - **`SealKey` refuses unprotected seals.** `SealKey`, and therefore `Seal` and every sealing caller, refuses a seal with neither a policy nor a non-empty password. It returns the new typed `tpm2.ErrSealUnprotected` (`sdk/go`: `ErrTPMSealUnprotected`); previously that seal created an object anyone able to load it could unseal.
    - `Seal` with no `KeyAttributes` and no password now binds the object to the Platform SRK's own policy, and FROST's `TPM2SecretSealKeyAttributes` does the same for its shares.
    - Keys and symmetric key objects are not refused: their use stays gated by the Platform SRK at `TPM2_Load`.
    - `xkmsctl seal --backend tpm2` now needs `--tpm-policy`, `--password` or both. The `tpm_policy` and `password` fields of `SealRequest` are described the same way on the REST, MCP, gRPC, transport, `sdk/ts` and `xkmsctl` surfaces.
  - **`types.SealOptions.TPMPolicy` / `types.TPMSealPolicy` replaced by `types.SealOptions.AuthPolicy`** (`sdk/go`: the `TPMSealPolicy` alias is gone). Its `PCRSelection` and `HashAlg` were copied onto the key attributes and never enforced, so they were dropped; the caller keeps its own PCR list. The one enforced part, a caller-computed policy digest, stays as `SealOptions.AuthPolicy`. `Seal` checks that it is the size of the object's name-algorithm digest (`ErrSealAuthPolicySize`) and that the seal does not also name a TPM policy (`ErrSealAuthPolicyConflict`). It counts as a policy, so the seal is not refused, and the object gets `userWithAuth` CLEAR. xkms builds no session for such a digest and does not unseal the object; whoever computed the digest does. `pkg/luks`'s `systemd-tpm2` token under the Shared SRK uses it, and only systemd-cryptsetup unseals that token. `pkg/luks` no longer sets its random, discarded "guard" password on either seal path: the cleared attribute now refuses the empty-password `TPM2_Unseal` that the guard used to block, and `TestTPMSealer_SSRK_SealedObjectEnforcesPCRPolicy` proves both the refusal and systemd's PolicyPCR unseal on the simulator.
  - **Existing objects keep their old attributes.** Objects and NV indices created before this change keep `userWithAuth` (or `TPMA_NV_AUTHREAD`) SET and, when passwordless and platform-bound, their open `PolicyAuthValue` branch, so they can still be opened the old way. Nothing is migrated (pre-release, no migration path). Re-create them to protect them: re-enroll the platform-store credential, the `tpmpolicy` secrets and the barrier's TPM2 root key, and regenerate platform-policy keys and NV indices.
  - Docs: `docs/tpm2/engineering.md` ("Object authorization").
- **`pkg/tpm2/vtpm`: `Config.Binary` is validated once, at `NewManager`, instead of trusted at every `Start`.** A bare name (no path separator) is resolved through `exec.LookPath`; a path is confirmed to exist and be a regular, executable file with `os.Stat`. Either way the resolved path is fixed for the Manager's lifetime, not re-searched on `PATH` per vTPM start. A node whose `backends.tpm2.vtpm.binary` is missing or not executable now fails closed at startup with the typed `vtpm.BinaryError`, instead of at the first tenant's `Start` (gosec G204).

### Added

- **Attestation evidence primitives are one exported package.** The new `pkg/attestation/evidence`, re-exported with `pkg/tpm2`'s `VerifyCertify*` and `pkg/attestation/peer`'s IAK/IDevID checks in `sdk/go/evidence`, verifies TPM2_Quote signatures, qualifying data and PCR digests, AK certificates (tcg-cap-verifiedTPMRestricted) and EK certificates (tcg-kp-EKCertificate), and parses and replays TCG PC Client crypto-agile event logs from bytes with digest sizes taken only from the Spec ID header. Every failure is classified forged or absent. The attested-peer verifier and the CA's EK check now run these primitives instead of private copies.
- **Whole-node backup/restore, over the embedded go-qrdb node's shard-snapshot capability, and per-key export/import now share one API model** (#728, closing #1326 item 4, and the backup half of #690). `XKMSService` gained a `BackupServicer` (`CreateBackup`/`ListBackups`/`GetBackup`/`DeleteBackup`/`RestoreBackup`/`VerifyBackup`), wired to the host's qrdb node exactly as custodian/share already are (`SetBackupClient`, `compose.Deps.Backup`/`Stores.Backup`, unconditional on `ServeBarrier`), and reachable identically on REST (`/api/v1/backups*`), gRPC (`xkmsv1.XKMSService`), MCP (`xkms.*Backup*`), the embedded SDK transport, and a new `xkmsctl backup create|list|show|delete|restore|verify`. xkms performs no shard capture, checksum, compression or encryption of its own -- every byte of that logic stays in go-qrdb; a standalone (non-raft) node reports go-qrdb's own typed unsupported-operation error unmodified. The six verbs carry go-qrdb's canonical `backup:create/list/read/delete/restore/verify` permissions verbatim, cross-checked against REST, gRPC and MCP's existing wire-contract goldens so the three transports cannot drift apart. Per-key export/import (`keys:export`/`keys:import`) was already complete end to end and is unchanged; this closes the remaining gap the owner ruling (2026-09-30) identified.
  - The dead `pkg/backup` package (`BackupAdapter`/`BackupData`/`FileBackupAdapter`, zero importers, an unimplemented `KeyRestorer`) is deleted: its JSON archive form (`BackupFormatJSON`) serialized a key's private material in the clear, which is exactly the plaintext-key-material defect #1326 item 4 flagged, and nothing in the tree used it. `xkey/pkg/backup` (the desktop app's own local-data backup of its trust store, OATH credentials and passwords) is a distinct, already-correct feature and is untouched.
  - Files: `pkg/xkms/service.go`, `pkg/xkms/servicer_backup.go`, `pkg/api/transport/{servicer,client,types_backup}.go`, `pkg/api/{rest,grpc,mcp}/*backup*.go`, `pkg/api/grpc/proto/xkmsv1/xkms.proto`, `pkg/api/transport/{embedded,grpc,unix,quic,mcp,rest}/transport.go`, `cmd/xkmsctl/backup.go`, `pkg/compose/compose.go`, `pkg/server/server.go`, `pkg/apimodule/module_host.go`, `pkg/auth/permissions.go`, `internal/authzscan/authzscan.go`, `pkg/testutil/qrdb_fake.go`, `docs/backup/`.
  - Verified by `pkg/xkms/servicer_backup_test.go` (success/failure, a tampered-checksum verify failure, and a validated restore refusing a tampered backup), the REST/gRPC/MCP authorization golden tests and `pkg/api/authz_consistency_test`, `pkg/compose`/`pkg/apimodule` composition tests, and `pkg/api/rest/server_route_authz_test.go`'s RBAC-denial/grant table.
- **Signed reference values (CoRIM) are verified as an attestation evidence primitive.** The new `pkg/attestation/refvalue`, re-exported as `VerifySignedCoRIM` and its types in `sdk/go/evidence`, verifies a COSE_Sign1-signed CoRIM against a pinned key or an x5chain certificate chain, enforces the corim-meta and RIM validity windows, and returns each CoMID's reference-value triples in a flat form, with `PCRDigests` for TPM PCR reference values. It adds the dependencies `github.com/veraison/corim` v1.1.2, `github.com/veraison/go-cose` v1.3.0 and `github.com/veraison/swid`, with `github.com/lestrrat-go/jwx/v2` raised to v2.1.7 over corim's v2.0.8.
- **`ipsec-vtep` and `x509-svid` certificate profiles under name-constrained subordinate CAs.** `pkg/ca`, re-exported from `sdk/go`, adds two caller-named profiles. `ipsec-vtep` issues IKEv2 endpoint certificates (`id-kp-ipsecIKE`, IP SANs, 30-day default and 90-day maximum lifetime). `x509-svid` issues SPIFFE X.509-SVID leaves (one SPIFFE ID URI SAN, serverAuth and clientAuth, 1-hour default and 24-hour maximum). Both take their subject and names only from the issuing caller, never from the CSR. `(*CA).IssueSubordinateCA` certifies a caller-held key as an RFC 5280 name-constrained subordinate. `SignOptions.Validity` sets a lifetime shorter than a day. A pre-sign check, applied to every profile, refuses a leaf whose names violate the issuer's name constraints. The `tp-attestationEvidence` extension (OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.29377.101.23) carries the verdict ID, PCR digest and attestation time.
- **CGO-free PKCS#11 key provisioning.** `module.ProvisionECKeyPair` creates a P-256 or P-384 key pair on a remote-mode token with exactly the `CKA_LABEL` and `CKA_ID` the loaded module will find it by, by driving the module in process rather than writing token records by hand; it initializes a new token with the SO PIN and is idempotent. `module.NewRemoteStorage` exposes the token store a remote-mode module reads. Both are re-exported in `sdk/go/signserver`.
- **An embeddable, node-local, sign-only xkms server.** The new `pkg/signserver`, re-exported as `sdk/go/signserver` and buildable with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, serves a remote-mode PKCS#11 module on a unix socket behind three gates: an exclusive SO_PEERCRED uid/gid allowlist, an RPC allowlist (Health, Sign, token-record reads and PIN-lockout counter writes), and `Sign` only for the keys a slot names by `CKA_LABEL`. `CreateKey` creates those keys idempotently through the module itself. `pkg/api/unix` gains `GRPCConfig.ExclusivePeers` (`NewExclusivePeerCredentialPolicy`, `ErrNoAdmittedPeers`) and caller-supplied unary and stream interceptors.
- **A general SPIFFE ID builder and validator.** `pkg/spiffe` adds `TrustDomain`, `WorkloadID`, `ParseTrustDomain`, `ParseWorkloadID`, `WorkloadIDFromURL`, `ValidatePath`, `ValidatePathPrefix` and `HasPathPrefix`, enforcing the SPIFFE-ID specification for any trust domain and path, with `InvalidIDError` wrapping a sentinel per rule. The new `sdk/go/spiffe` re-exports it together with the existing tenant-scoped identity helpers.
- **`pkg/staticpw`: `NewTenantPasswordStoreManager` takes functional options, starting with `WithPassphraseKDFParams`.** The Argon2id cost a new passphrase vault factor wraps its DEK with was a package-private variable only `pkg/staticpw`'s own tests could override; every other package that builds a `TenantPasswordStoreManager` ran passphrase enrollment and unlock at the production cost (`kdf.DefaultParams`: 64 MiB, t=3, p=4), and running that many times over in parallel (`pkg/api/mcp`'s password-vault tests) exhausted a CI job's memory. Production callers are unaffected -- the manager defaults to `kdf.DefaultParams(kdf.AlgorithmArgon2id)` exactly as before; `pkg/testutil/kdftest.CheapPassphraseParams` is the cheap cost every package's test fixtures now pass explicitly.
- **`xkms.NewService` builds a key service instance without the process singleton.** An embedder can now run its own, separately scoped `XKMSService` beside whatever else the process composes; `Initialize` is built on it. Servicer methods resolve backends from their own instance instead of the package singleton, so an instance built this way sees only, and exactly, its own backends.

### Changed

- **One LUKS implementation, built on `go-luks2`, with a configurable TPM seal parent.** `pkg/luks` is now the single LUKS implementation in the stack: `LibExecutor`, a new production `Executor` on `github.com/jeremyhahn/go-luks2` (now a direct root-module dependency), attaches a loop device to a file-backed container on `Unlock`/`Create` and detaches it on `Lock`, formats, mounts and unmounts, and runs the kernel-keyring preflight (`EnsureKeyringAvailable`) before every operation that needs it. `xkey/pkg/luks.Volume` no longer drives `go-luks2` itself; it is a thin wrapper over `sdk/go/luks`'s `Executor`, keeping only what is genuinely xkey-specific (privilege-drop chown after mount, secure container wipe). `TPMSealer`'s storage parent is now an explicit, validated config (`TPMSealerConfig{Parent SealParent, PCRBank string}`): `SealParentPSRK` (default) binds the sealed passphrase to go-xkms's Platform SRK and platform PCR policy, written as an `xkms-tpm2` token, consistent with go-xkms#681's PSRK-only rule; `SealParentSSRK` binds it to a plain PolicyPCR digest under the TCG Shared SRK with empty parent auth, written as a `systemd-tpm2` token for `systemd-cryptenroll`/crypttab boot-time unlock -- a documented, narrow exception to #681, which go-xkms seals but deliberately never unseals (`ErrTPMSSRKUnsealUnsupported`), since `pkg/tpm2`'s `Unseal` has no session path for an ad hoc PolicyPCR policy. Neither seal path sets a password on the sealed object: `pkg/tpm2` clears `UserWithAuth` on every sealed object with a policy, so an empty-password `TPM2_Unseal` is refused and only a policy session unseals it (verified against the TPM simulator; see the `security-tpm2-sealed-object-userwithauth` entry). All actual sealing/unsealing is delegated to `pkg/tpm2.TPM2`; `pkg/luks` drives no TPM command of its own beyond the SSRK path's PolicyPCR digest computation. Tokens are now go-luks2's own `*luks2.Token` type instead of a parallel struct. See `docs/luks/` and `xkey/docs/luks/` (go-xkms#917).

### Fixed

- **`CKM_ECDSA` and every ECDSA sign under hash `"NONE"` work on Go 1.27.** Go 1.27's `ecdsa.PrivateKey.Sign` refuses `crypto.Hash(0)`, so signing a caller-supplied ECDSA digest failed. The service now names the SHA-2 function the digest length implies (28, 32, 48 or 64 bytes) and refuses any other length, SHA-1's included, with `ErrInvalidHashFunction`.
- **`pkg/tpm2/vtpm`: a restarted vTPM is no longer reported `Running` before its command socket exists.** The supervisor's restart path spawned the replacement `swtpm` process and marked it running immediately, without the readiness wait `Start` already performs for the first process; a `Transport` dial landing in that window got a raw `dial unix: ... no such file or directory` instead of the documented `ErrConnectionLost` retry-once contract. `Manager.supervise` now awaits the replacement's socket exactly as `Start` does before marking it running, bounded by the same `readyTimeout` and ended early if `Stop` is called while the wait is outstanding.

## [0.46.0-alpha] - 2026-09-30

### Added

- **Personal password vault: personal entries are sealed with each user's own key.**
  - Each user's personal entries are encrypted with a random per-user DEK. The DEK is wrapped under factors the user controls:
    - a passphrase (Argon2id, 64 MiB, t=3, p=4);
    - a passkey (FIDO2 hmac-secret / WebAuthn PRF output, HKDF-SHA256);
    - a one-time recovery code, shown once on first enrollment and replaced on every recovery.
  - The tenant barrier key alone reads none of it.
  - Rotating a factor re-wraps the DEK; the DEK never changes.
  - Every surface carries it:
    - gRPC `PasswordVault{Status,Enroll,Rotate,RemoveFactor,Recover}`;
    - REST `/api/v1/passwords/vault[...]`;
    - MCP `password.vault.*`;
    - every client transport and the Go and TS SDKs;
    - `xkmsctl password vault ...` and `xkey password vault ...`;
    - the xkey GUI vault panel.
  - Passkeys work on every client: `--passkey` on `xkmsctl` / `xkey password unlock|vault enroll|vault recover`, and "Use security key" in the xkey GUI. Every client goes through `pkg/vaultpasskey`:
    - RP ID `xkms-password-vault`;
    - the WebAuthn prf salt transform `SHA-256("WebAuthn PRF" || 0x00 || salt)`, so a passkey enrolled on any surface (or in a browser) unlocks on every other;
    - user verification by PIN, always.
  - `pkg/fido2` adds `FIDO2Handler.DeriveHMACSecret` (the raw hmac-secret), `EnrollmentConfig.PIN` / `AuthenticationConfig.PIN`, and `WebAuthnPRFSalt`, all re-exported in `sdk/go/fido2`.
- **`pkg/scope`: one ownership model for every feature.**
  - Scopes: `tenant` (shared: every user of the tenant), `user` (personal: the owner only) and `service` (workload-owned: explicit permission).
  - Keyspace: `{tenant}/{feature}/shared/`, `{tenant}/{feature}/users/{subject}/` and `{tenant}/{feature}/services/{owner}/`.
  - `Principal.Authorize` is the single access rule. It refuses cross-tenant, cross-user and unpermitted service access with typed errors that match `scope.ErrRefused`.
  - The system tenant is an ordinary tenant named `system`.
  - The password vault, TPM policies (`tpmpolicy.ScopeName` is replaced by `scope.TenantName`) and SSH all use it.
- **`ssh:service`**: the explicit permission a `scope=service` SSH address requires.
  - It is xkms-owned and `ScopeSelf`, and is granted to Admin and Owner.
  - It is checked below the transport gate through `XKMSService.AuthorizeCaller`.

### Changed

- **The password transport DTOs carry `Title`.**
- **The password service layer:**
  - `PasswordUpdate` returns the updated entry, so gRPC answers a rename with the new ID;
  - REST and MCP `generate` go through it, with a `Charset` field.
- **Password vault sessions are per user.**
  - Unlocking or locking opens or closes only the caller's personal session (`TenantPasswordStoreManager.UnlockUser` / `LockUser` / `IsUserLocked` / `UserStoreStatus`, replacing the tenant-wide `UnlockTenant` / `LockTenant` / `IsLocked` / `TenantStoreStatus` / `StoreForTenant` / `ResolveStore`).
  - Shared entries are usable whenever the tenant barrier is unsealed.
  - Personal operations on a locked session return `ErrStoreLocked`.
  - Sealing the tenant barrier ends its sessions.
- **SSH scope binding follows `pkg/scope`.**
  - `scope=user` assets are reachable only by their owner, now including system-tenant callers.
  - `scope=service` assets are reachable only with `ssh:service`, in the caller's own tenant, for any workload owner.
  - `OwnerBindingError` gains a diagnostic `Cause`.
  - `compose.BuildSSHClient` takes the permission checker.
- **SSH storage uses the scope layout:** `{tenant}/ssh/shared/`, `{tenant}/ssh/users/{subject}/`, `{tenant}/ssh/services/{owner}/`. The platform partition is `system/`. No migration.

### Removed

- **Dead ACME rate-limiter helper constructors removed, including the
  spoofable `TenantRateLimiterFromHeader` (#742).** The RFC 8555 §6.6
  regression they were left over from is already fixed: xkmsd
  (`cmd/xkmsd/acme.go`) and the standalone TrustedCA
  (`pkg/acme/client/trustedca.go`) both wire their per-client, per-tenant and
  per-category limiters through `pkg/acme/server.NewClientRateLimiterMiddleware`,
  `NewAccountRateLimiter`, and the tenant-aware `NewTenant{Order,Certificate,
  FailedValidation}RateLimiter` + `TenantRateLimiterFromRequestContext`, which
  resolves the tenant only from a verified JWS "kid". Deleted for having zero
  production callers: `pkg/acme/server.NewOrderRateLimiter`,
  `CertificateRateLimiter`, `OverallRateLimiter`, `FailedValidationRateLimiter`,
  `NewTenantAccountRateLimiter`, `NewTenantOverallRateLimiter`,
  `TenantRateLimiterFromHeader` (took the tenant from a client-supplied HTTP
  header) and `TenantRateLimiterFromContext` (a generic, unused
  context-value extractor), plus their tests.
- **`xkey/pkg/ca`, an unwired local-CA bridge, is deleted (#729).** It
  duplicated the canonical `pkg/xkms/servicer_ca*` CA implementation behind
  an `xkms.TCGCA`-backed `Service`, but had zero importers anywhere in the
  xkey module: `xkey`'s CLI (`cmd/xkey/cmd/ca.go`) and its `getSDKClient`
  are remote-mode only by design — "xkey never runs an in-process CA" — and
  reach the canonical servicer over the SDK transport against a running
  xkmsd. A local-CA mode for xkey is not built as part of this cleanup and
  awaits a separate owner ruling.
- **The deployment-wide user PIN no longer unlocks the password store.** `PasswordStoreUnlockRequest` carries a vault credential instead of `UserPIN`, and `ErrPasswordStoreUserPINRequired` / `ErrPasswordStoreUserPINNotProvisioned` are removed. The PIN remains for the features that use it.
- **The unwired team-sharing code:** REST team handlers and DTOs, `TenantDAOMiddleware`, `staticpw.TenantDAOFactory`, the password `DAOStore`/`PasswordEntity` and `TeamScopedStore`. xkey's local team list is kept.
- **The xkey GUI's `TryAutoUnlock`.**

### Fixed

- **A system-tenant identity no longer gets "Tenant not found" from the password routes.** The system tenant has its own shared and personal store under the system barrier.
- **Two xkey AES-GCM call sites and the PKCS#11 test token work under
  `GODEBUG=fips140=only` (go-xkms#23).** The password-vault backup envelope
  (`xkey/pkg/gui/services/staticpw_backup.go`) and the in-process key wrapper
  (`xkey/pkg/authenticator/key_wrapper.go`) now use
  `cipher.NewGCMWithRandomNonce`; FIPS mode refuses a caller-chosen GCM nonce
  even when it is random. `pkg/testing/pkcs11test`'s mock token selects its
  CKM_AES_GCM AEAD through `pkg/crypto/aead`, so a token-generated IV works
  in FIPS mode as it does on the real backends.
  - **Breaking:** the password backup envelope is now version 2, with the
    nonce folded into `ciphertext`. A version 1 backup is refused with
    `ErrRestoreUnsupportedVersion`. The key wrapper's format is unchanged.

## [0.45.0-alpha] - 2026-09-30

### Added

- **Named TPM policies can be composite (an OR of branches, each an AND of `pcr`, `auth_value` and `locality` conditions), and carry a description.**
  - The authority signs one approval per branch, all for the policy's `policyRef`, so `PolicyAuthorize` accepts whichever branch the session satisfies. Update, revoke and authority rotation work on every branch, still without re-keying.
  - The session tries the branches in order.
    - A branch with `auth_value` is tried only when a password was supplied.
    - A branch whose PCR or locality check fails moves on.
    - If every branch is refused, the result is `*PolicyBranchesRefusedError`, which unwraps to each branch's error.
    - A policy with an `auth_value` condition gives its objects no separate password branch, so a password alone cannot bypass a "PCR and password" policy.
    - An `auth_value` policy refuses objects without a password (`ErrPolicyAuthValueRequired`).
  - `TPM2_PolicyLocality`, which go-tpm v0.9.8 does not implement, is sent as a raw command.
  - The binding record is `XTPB` v2 with the auth-value flag; v1 records still decode.
  - `Service.SetDescription` updates the free-text description.
  - Verified on the simulator:
    - AND: signing needs both the password and the PCR;
    - OR: the PCR branch works without a password, and the password branch after the PCR changes;
    - locality: the allowed locality works, and the TPM refuses a disallowed one at use;
    - update, replay refusal, revoke and rotation across every branch;
    - per-branch verification and descriptions.
- **Key versions on every backend and every API surface.** Rotating a key no longer replaces its material in place: `RotateKey(K)` generates the next version as its own backend key `K--v<n>`, with the current version's algorithm, size or curve and attributes -- for a TPM2 key, in the same tenant scope and bound to the same TPM policy (`PolicyOf`) -- and records it as current in a version record (`pkg/keyversion`, stored under `{tenant}/key-versions/<backend>/<keyID>` in the new `key-versions` storage, built through the one construction path `compose.BuildKeyVersionStore` by xkmsd and embedding hosts alike). A key with no record is version 1; generating a key writes no record. Sign, encrypt and encrypt-asym use the current version and report `key_version` beside their standard-format output; verify, AEAD and RSA-OAEP decrypt, unseal and authenticated unwrap try every enabled version newest first unless `key_version` names one; AES-CBC and RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 decrypt (and unwrap) require `key_version` once a key has more than one enabled version (`*keyversion.KeyVersionRequiredError`, 400 / InvalidArgument). Derivation (`DeriveKey`, `DeriveKeyECDH`) takes and reports the base key's version. Versions are listed, enabled, disabled and retired (retiring deletes the version's key; the current version cannot be disabled or retired, 409 / FailedPrecondition), and `RotateScopeKeys` rotates every key of a tenant. `ListKeys` shows each key once with its current version; `DeleteKey` deletes every version. Key IDs ending in `--v<digits>` are reserved and refused. New surface on REST (`GET /api/v1/keys/{id}/versions`, `POST …/versions/{n}/enable|disable|retire`, `POST …/versions/enable-all|disable-all`, `POST /api/v1/keys/rotate-all`), gRPC/Unix (the declared `ListKeyVersions`/`Enable`/`Disable`/`EnableAll`/`DisableAllKeyVersions` RPCs are implemented and gated, plus `RetireKeyVersion` and `RotateScopeKeys`; `key_version` fields on `KeyInfo`, `Sign`, `Verify`, `Encrypt`, `Decrypt`, `EncryptAsym`, `RotateKey`, `Seal`/`Unseal`, `Wrap`/`UnwrapKeyByID`, `DeriveKey`, `DeriveKeyECDH`), MCP (`xkms.*KeyVersion*`, `xkms.rotateScopeKeys`), every client transport (`transport.KeyVersionService`), `sdk/go`, `sdk/ts` (`keys.versions.list/enable/disable/retire/enableAll/disableAll/rotateAll`) and `xkmsctl` (`key versions`, `key version enable|disable|retire|enable-all|disable-all`, `key rotate-all [--tenant]`, `--key-version` on `key verify` and `key decrypt`). Permissions reuse `keys:list`, `keys:rotate` and `keys:delete`. A tenant's symmetric key generated through the service is now stored in the tenant (it was stored as a system key). See `docs/tpm-policies/` ("Key versions").
- **`pkg/tpm2` can bind keys and sealed objects to named, authorized TPM policies that can be updated, revoked and re-signed by a new authority without re-keying.**
  - A key or sealed object whose `TPMPolicy` names a policy (anything but `""` or `platform`) is created with `authPolicy = PolicyOR(PolicyAuthorizeNV(the policy's NV index), PolicyAuthValue)`. It has only the first branch when it has no auth value, and `userWithAuth` is cleared.
  - A `.tpmpolicy` binding record (format `XTPB` v1) is saved beside its blobs.
  - At use, the session code reads that record and runs PolicyPCR → PolicyNV(counter == epoch) → VerifySignature → PolicyAuthorize → PolicyAuthorizeNV. The approval comes from a `PolicyBindingResolver`.
  - A PCR change fails as `PolicyPCRMismatchError`, and a superseded approval fails as `PolicyApprovalRevokedError`. Both wrap the TPM response code.
  - New primitives:
    - digests: `PolicyRef`, `AuthorizeDigest`, `ApprovedPolicyDigest`, `ApprovalDigest`, `AuthorizedObjectPolicy`;
    - NV indices: `FindFreeNVIndex`, `DefinePolicyIndex`, `WritePolicyIndex`, `ReadPolicyIndex`, `UndefineNVIndex`, `NVIndexName` (a full NV space is `ErrTPMNVExhausted`);
    - counters: `DefineCounterIndex`, `IncrementCounter`, `ReadCounter`;
    - keys: `CreateStorageKey` (a tenant's storage key under the Platform SRK), `SignApproval` and `AuthorityName`.
  - NV indices are `AUTHWRITE` with a random write secret, plus `POLICYREAD` restricted to the one command that needs the read, so using an object needs no secret.
  - Verified on the TPM simulator:
    - `TestAuthorizedPolicy_DigestsMatchLiveSession`: every trial digest equals the live session digest;
    - `..._KeysSignUnderApproval`: two keys, with and without a password;
    - `..._PCRChangeRefusesApprovedBranch`;
    - `..._UpdateReapprovesWithoutRekey`: byte-identical blobs;
    - `..._ReplayOfSupersededApprovalRefused`;
    - `..._AuthorityRotation`: the old authority is refused;
    - `..._SealedObject`, the binding-record and refusal tests, and the NV index and counter tests.
- **Named TPM policies on every API surface.** The TPM policy service (`pkg/tpmpolicy`) is built by xkmsd whenever `backends.tpm2` is enabled (and by an embedding host whose XKMSService has a `tpm2` backend) through the one construction path `compose.BuildTPMPolicyService`, and installed as the TPM2 backend's scope provider: every TPM2 key and seal now runs in the TPM scope of its tenant (`KeyAttributes.TenantID`), is bound to a named policy (`tpm_policy`, default `platform`), and is recorded in the policy registry. New surface on REST (`/api/v1/tpm/policies*`, `/api/v1/tpm/authority/rotate`, `/api/v1/keys/{id}/tpm-policy`, `/api/v1/tenants/{id}/tpm*`), gRPC/Unix (`TPMPolicy*`, `TPMObjectPolicy`, `Get/SetTenantTPMMode`, `TenantVTPM*`), MCP (`tpm.policy.*`, `tpm.object.policy`, `tpm.authority.rotate`, `xkms.*TenantTPMMode`, `xkms.tenantVTPM*`), the SDK (`transport.TPMPolicyService`, plus `TPMPolicyService`/`NewTPMPolicyService` for an in-process service) and `xkmsctl` (`tpm policy …`, `tpm authority rotate`, `key policy`, `key generate --tpm-policy`, `seal --tpm-policy/--password`, `tenant tpm-mode`, `tenant vtpm …`). Permissions `tpm_policy:{create,get,list,update,revoke,verify,delete,rotate}` (ScopeSelf) and `tenants:set_tpm_mode` (ScopeCross). New config `backends.tpm2.vtpm` (off unless enabled). See `docs/tpm-policies/`.
- gRPC `Seal`/`Unseal` carry a TPM2 sealed object's areas, the TPM policy and the password (`SealRequest` 5–6, `SealResponse` 6–9, `UnsealRequest` 7–11); REST and MCP carry them too.
- **`pkg/tpmpolicy`: named TPM policies, the key↔policy registry, and per-tenant TPM scopes.**
  - `Service` creates, lists, updates, revokes, verifies and deletes named policies. The PCR values are captured live from the TPM, never supplied by the caller.
  - `UpdatePolicy` re-captures a policy's PCRs, bumps the tenant's NV counter and re-signs every approval in the scope, so bound keys keep working without a re-key and superseded approvals are refused by the TPM. `RevokePolicy` bumps the counter and leaves the revoked policy unapproved. `RotateAuthority` rewrites every policy index and re-signs under a new authority, and is crash-recoverable.
  - The registry answers "which policy does this object use" and "which objects use this policy". `DeletePolicy` refuses with `*PolicyInUseError`, listing the objects.
  - Tenant scopes follow `tpm.mode` (default `shared`):
    - `shared`: the physical TPM, under a per-tenant storage key and a tenant-prefixed key store;
    - `vtpm`: a supervised swtpm, provisioned on first start, whose state key is sealed under the system scope's `vtpm-state` policy;
    - `none`: `ErrTPMModeNone`.
  - A mode change is refused while the tenant has TPM objects or policies.
  - Scope secrets are sealed by the physical TPM.
  - Verified on the TPM simulator and on real swtpm:
    - two keys under one policy, both listed by the registry;
    - a PCR change refuses them;
    - update restores them with byte-identical blobs;
    - replaying an old approval is refused;
    - deleting a policy while it's assigned is refused;
    - revoke and restore;
    - authority rotation, with no re-key and the old authority refused;
    - shared-mode tenant isolation: the other tenant's key cannot be loaded (`TPM_RC_INTEGRITY`);
    - mode-change refusal;
    - crash reconciliation;
    - a vTPM that survives stop/start and a service restart with the same state key.
  - A go-tpm v0.9.8 defect (`hmacKeyFromAuthValue` truncates an auth value at any 0x00 byte, not just trailing ones) makes HMAC authorization fail for about 12% of random 32-byte secrets. The generated scope secrets therefore contain no zero byte.
- **`pkg/tpm2/vtpm` runs a per-tenant virtual TPM for `tpm.mode: vtpm`.** `Manager` starts one `swtpm socket --tpm2` child process per tenant. Each has its own state directory and a private unix command socket. The process is supervised and restarted with backoff if it dies. `Transport(tenant)` hands out a `go-tpm` transport that frames TPM responses and reconnects to a restarted process. A command lost mid-flight is reported as `ErrConnectionLost` and never replayed, because TPM commands are not idempotent.
  - A vTPM's state is always encrypted with an AES-256 key from a `StateKeyProvider`. The key reaches swtpm through an inherited pipe (`--key fd=3`) and is never written to disk. xkms seals the key under the system scope's `vtpm-state` policy.
  - swtpm is now a dependency of `make test`. It was already installed in the CI and devcontainer images.
  - Verified against real swtpm 0.7.3 by `TestManager_StartServesAVTPMAndStopEndsIt`, `..._StatePersistsAcrossRestartUnderItsKey` (state survives a restart, and a vTPM refuses to start over state encrypted under another key), `..._RestartsACrashedVTPMAndTheTransportFollows` (SIGKILL, supervised restart, same transport reconnects), `..._TenantsAreSeparateTPMs`, `..._RefusesBadInputs` and `..._MissingBinaryIsAStartError`, stable over `-race -count=5`.
- **xkmsd can keep the user PIN in the TPM (`pin.strategy: tpm2`), and it chooses the PIN store exactly the way xKey does.** Before this change, `initializePINManager` accepted only `software`. PIN selection now runs through one resolver shared by xkmsd, the xKey GUI, `xkey pin` and `xkey extension serve`. That resolver is `pkg/pinselect.Resolve`, moved from `xkey/pkg/pinstrategy`, which is deleted; xKey reaches it through `xkmssdk.ResolvePINBackend`. The governing strategy is recorded in `<storage.path>/pin/strategy`.
  - `tpm2` puts the PIN on the Platform SRK of xkmsd's TPM2 backend as its auth value, verified in hardware with the TPM's lockout. The store comes from the new `pkg/tpm2.AttachPlatformKeyStore`, which xKey's GUI now uses too.
  - `auto` is now the default. It never adopts an SRK whose auth nobody has confirmed, so an existing software deployment keeps software.
  - An explicit strategy that differs from the recorded one is refused with `*pinselect.StrategyMismatchError`, because switching would orphan every PIN in the old store.
  - `tpm2` without `backends.tpm2.enabled` refuses to start with `*pinselect.ProviderUnavailableError` and records nothing.
  - Files: `pkg/pinselect/{resolve,strategy,strategy_errors,tpmprovider}.go`, `pkg/tpm2/platform_keystore.go`, `pkg/server/pin_manager.go`, `pkg/server/server.go`, `pkg/server/errors.go`, `sdk/go/pin.go`, `sdk/go/tpm.go`, `xkey/pkg/gui/app.go`, `xkey/pkg/gui/services/pin_strategy.go`, `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/{pin,pin_tpm,extension_serve}.go`, `docs/pin-management/{engineering,user}.md`.
  - Verified with the TPM simulator by `TestInitializePINManager_TPM2StrategyGovernsWithThePlatformSRK` (the PIN is set and verified in the TPM, and a wrong PIN is refused), `..._TPM2StrategyWithoutATPMIsRefused`, `..._AutoNeverAdoptsAnUnconfirmedSRK` and `..._StrategyChangeAgainstRecordIsRefused`. Also by the `TestResolve_Explicit*` resolver tests and the `TestAttachPlatformKeyStore_*` tests.

### Changed

- **Composite TPM policies and descriptions reach every surface, the single-branch shims are gone, and `rotate-all` skips keys a rotation would not serve.**
  - The API speaks branches only. `TPMPolicy` carries `description` and `branches` (each with its `conditions` -- `type`, `bank`, `pcrs`, hex `pcr_values`/`pcr_digest`, `localities` -- and `approved`). `TPMPolicyCreateRequest` carries `description` and `branches`, and a request that supplies PCR values is refused. `TPMPolicyVerifyResponse` reports every branch.
  - The top-level `bank`/`pcrs`/`pcr_values`/`pcr_digest`/`mismatched` fields are removed from the API and the proto; their field numbers are reserved. The deprecated `tpmpolicy.CreatePolicyRequest.Bank`/`PCRs`, `Policy.Bank`/`PCRs`/`PCRValues`/`PCRDigest`/`Approval`, `Verification.Mismatched` and `ErrAmbiguousPolicyRequest` are also removed. `tpmpolicy.PCRBranch` and `transport.TPMPolicyPCRBranch` build the one-branch policy.
  - New operation to set a description: `POST /api/v1/tpm/policies/{name}/description`, gRPC `TPMPolicySetDescription` (`tpm_policy:update`), MCP `tpm.policy.setDescription`. It is available on every client transport (the USB transport answers not supported) and in `sdk/go` and `sdk/ts` (`setDescription`, `pcrBranch`).
  - CLIs. `xkmsctl` and `xkey` `tpm policy create` take `--description`, and either `--pcrs`/`--bank` for one pcr branch or a repeatable `--branch 'pcr=sha256:0,7;auth_value;locality=0'`. Both commands parse through the shared `transport.TPMPolicyBranches`. `tpm policy describe NAME TEXT` sets a description, and `get`/`list`/`verify` show branches.
  - The web console and xKey TPM policy panels create policies in a simple mode (one PCR selection) or an advanced mode (branches of PCR, password and locality conditions). They show and edit descriptions, and verify each branch.
  - New typed errors from policy validation are classified as invalid argument on every transport: `*InvalidLocalityError`, `*UnknownConditionTypeError`, `*DuplicateConditionError`, `*ConditionOperandError`, `*DescriptionTooLongError`, `ErrNoBranches`, `ErrEmptyBranch`, `ErrEmptyLocalitySelection`, `ErrPCRValuesSupplied` and `tpm2.ErrPolicyAuthValueRequired`.
  - `RotateScopeKeys` gives each key a `state` (`rotated`, `skipped` with a `reason`, or `failed`) and counts `skipped`.
    - It skips keys that other subsystems name exactly: TPM2 PIV slot keys (`piv-<slot>`), the TPM2 sealed objects `Seal` names, and the barrier's seal wrapping key (`xkms-barrier-seal`). A new version of these would never be used.
    - It skips keys with a certificate, because the certificate would stay on the old version.
    - Single-key `RotateKey` still rotates a certified key, and reports `certificate_reissue_required` (gRPC field 7). `xkmsctl key rotate` and the web console warn when it is set.
  - Verified by `pkg/tpmpolicy`, `pkg/xkms` (`TestRotateScopeKeys_SkipsPinnedAndCertifiedKeys`, `TestPinnedKeyReason`, `TestRotateKey_ReportsCertificateReissue`) and `pkg/api/...` (route, authz-golden and error-class parity for the new operation). CLI tests cover both CLIs, and there are `sdk/ts`, web console and xKey frontend vitest suites.
- **A TPM key names its policy instead of flipping a `PlatformPolicy` switch, and `platform` is the default.** `types.KeyAttributes.PlatformPolicy bool` is now `TPMPolicy string`. The value is empty for no policy (the TCG primaries such as the EK and Shared SRK), `types.TPMPolicyPlatform` (`"platform"`) for today's PCR-16-or-password policy, or the name of an authorized TPM policy (added next, in `pkg/tpmpolicy`). `KeyConfig.platform-policy` is now `tpm-policy`. `pkg/backend/tpm2` binds every key and symmetric key its caller leaves unnamed to `platform`. The xkmsd platform store's sealed objects always use `platform`.
  - Removed: `backends.tpm2.platform_policy`, `pkg/backend/tpm2.Config.PlatformPolicy`, `seal.TPM2ProbeConfig.PlatformPolicy`, and the dead `platform-policy` fields on the CA software and TPM2 keystore configs and the PKCS#11 backend config. None of the removed fields reached key creation. The TCG provisioning switches (`idevid`/`iak`/`platform-srk` `platform-policy`) stay, because they configure the primaries.
  - Verified by `TestGenerateKey_DefaultsToThePlatformPolicy` (a key created with no policy is bound to `platform` and signs on the simulator), `TestGenerateKey_KeepsAnExplicitPolicyReference`, and the existing `pkg/tpm2`, `pkg/backend/tpm2`, `pkg/seal`, `pkg/server`, `pkg/xkms` and `pkg/ca` suites.
- **The web console and the TypeScript SDK use TPM policies.**
  - `@go-xkms/sdk` drops the PCR-snapshot `policies` client.
  - It adds `tpmPolicies` (create, list, get, update, revoke, verify, delete, objects, setAutoUnseal, keyPolicy, rotateAuthority) and tenant TPM-mode and vTPM methods on `tenants`.
  - It adds `tpm_policy` on key generation and `tpm_policy`/`password` on seal.
  - The console's "PCR Policies" view is replaced by "TPM Policies" (`/tpm/policies`, shown when the server reports the `tpm_policies` capability). The view covers:
    - approval state, object counts and the auto-unseal toggle;
    - create with bank and PCR selection;
    - update, revoke and verify (which shows mismatched PCRs);
    - delete, which surfaces the server's "assigned to …" refusal;
    - rotate authority.
  - The key-generation dialog gains a TPM policy picker, defaulting to `platform`.
  - Verified by 169 SDK and 414 console vitest cases, plus `npm run check`/`build`.
- **xKey uses the shared TPM policy service; its own PCR-policy stores are gone.**
  - Deleted: `xkey/pkg/pcr_policy`, `PlatformPolicyService` (and its `platform.policy` file), the composite PCR/password policies, policy export/import, manual policy-to-handle assignment, the `custom_pcr` seal type (which silently ignored its PCRs) and `xkey policy`.
  - In local mode xKey runs `pkg/tpmpolicy` over its own TPM, with its registry in `<dataDir>/tpm-policies`. Connected to xkmsd, it runs the same operations through the `TPMPolicy*` client methods, and `TPMPolicyService.SetClient` is now wired on connect.
  - CLI: `xkey tpm policy create|list|get|update|revoke|verify|delete|objects|key|auto-unseal` and `xkey tpm authority rotate`. They run against the server when an xkmsd URL is configured.
  - GUI: the TPM view gains a Policies panel (create with bank and PCR picker, update, revoke, verify, delete, objects, auto-unseal, rotate). The Seal view picks none, `platform` or a named policy plus an optional password. Settings gains a barrier auto-unseal panel.
  - Barrier auto-unseal is now an attribute of a named policy. Enabling it seals the barrier password in the TPM under that policy, and startup unseals it through a real policy session. A PCR change or a revoke makes the TPM refuse (`ErrBarrierAutoUnsealRefused`), and the user unlocks by hand. The previous software PCR comparison and its unchecked TPM fallback are removed.
  - The setup wizard seals the barrier password under an `auto-unseal` policy (PCRs 0, 7 and 9) and the LUKS passphrase under `platform`. Its "Creating platform policy" step is gone.
  - Verified by the service tests on the simulator (two keys under one policy, delete refused listing them, update, verify, auto-unseal refused after a PCR change), remote-mode and connection-wiring tests, CLI tests, and frontend vitest.

### Removed

- The PCR snapshot store `pkg/seal/policy` and everything built on it: `/api/v1/policies/*`, the `Policy*` RPCs, the `policy.*` MCP tools, `transport.PolicyService`, `xkmsctl policy`, `apimodule.WithPCRReader` / `WithServiceModulePCRReader`, `compose.BuildPolicyManager`, `pkg/tpm2.BankPCRReader`, the `policy:*` permissions. `SealRequest.PCRs`/`PCRHashAlg` were removed: they were copied into a PCR selection that never became an authPolicy, so a "PCR-bound" sealed object was bound to nothing.

### Fixed

- **xkmsd's TPM platform PCR defaults to 16, as it does in xKey and the library, instead of PCR 0.** `pkg/backend/tpm2.Config.Validate` left an unset `platform_pcr` at zero, so xkmsd's `backends.tpm2` path (the key backend, node-seal autodetect and platform-store opens) extended the golden measurement into PCR 0, the firmware PCR, and computed platform policies over it. The library default (`pkg/tpm2.DefaultConfig`) and xKey used PCR 16, so a TPM enrolled by one computed a different Platform SRK policy from the other. `Validate` now resolves an unset PCR to the new `pkg/tpm2.DefaultPlatformPCR` (16) and an unset bank to `PCRBankSHA256`. `DefaultConfig`, the SDK (`xkmssdk.DefaultPlatformPCR`) and xKey's CLI all use the same constant instead of their own literals. **Upgrade note:** an xkmsd that relied on the old implicit PCR 0 computes a different platform policy after this change and must re-enrol its Platform SRK; zero is "unset", so PCR 0 can no longer be selected.
  - Files: `pkg/tpm2/config.go`, `pkg/backend/tpm2/config.go`, `pkg/config/config.go`, `sdk/go/tpm.go`, `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/tpm.go`, `docs/tpm2/engineering.md`.
  - Verified by `TestConfig_Validate_PlatformPCRDefault` and `TestConfig_Validate_PlatformPCRExplicit` (`pkg/backend/tpm2`).
- **A shared-mode tenant can hold TPM symmetric keys, and unsealing in-memory blobs honours the object's named policy.**
  - `pkg/tpm2` symmetric keys accepted only the Platform SRK as parent, and only the TPM's default key store. They now accept any storage key beneath the Platform SRK (never the Shared SRK, and never a non-storage key) through the store-aware `GenerateSymmetricKeyIn`, `GetSymmetricKeyIn`, `SymmetricEncrypterIn` and `DeriveFromSymmetricKeyIn`.
  - The TPM2 backend routes every scope's symmetric keys through these variants. The encrypter it returns opens its key's scope for each operation, because a shared tenant's storage key is flushed when the operation ends.
  - `Unseal` of caller-supplied blobs read a named policy's binding record from the TPM's default store only, so a tenant's sealed object failed its policy session. It now reads the record from `UnsealOptions.Backend`, and the backend's copy-from-store workaround is removed.
  - Verified on the simulator:
    - `TestSymmetricKey_UnderATenantStorageKey`: a tenant key encrypts and decrypts, and Shared SRK and non-storage parents are refused;
    - `TestScopedBackend_SymmetricKeysInEveryScope`: the system and tenant scopes, the registry assignments, and cross-tenant invisibility;
    - `TestAuthorizedPolicy_SealedObjectFromBlobsInCallerStore`: proven to fail without the fix.
- **A TPM2 seal without a key ID no longer overwrites the previous one, and the TPM policy API has one conversion for xkmsd and xKey.**
  - Fixed: every TPM2 seal without a `key_id` reused the object name `xkms-sealing-key-tpm2`, so each seal replaced the previous object's blobs, policy binding and registry assignment, and the earlier object no longer unsealed (`TPM_RC_POLICY_FAIL`). Each such seal now creates its own object named `xkms-sealing-key-tpm2-<uuid>`, returned in `SealResponse.KeyID` (REST/MCP `key_id`, gRPC `key_id` = 9), and its assignment is per object. A TPM2 unseal must pass that key ID back; without one it is refused with `xkms.ErrTPMSealedObjectKeyIDRequired` (invalid argument). Other backends are unchanged. `pkg/xkms/servicer_seal.go`; `xkmsctl seal`/`unseal-data` `--key-id` help updated.
  - Changed: `xkms.TenantTPMPolicies` (`NewTenantTPMPolicies(svc, tenant)`, re-exported by `sdk/go`) serves the tenant-level `TPMPolicy*` operations for one fixed tenant and holds the single `*tpmpolicy.Service` to API-type conversion. `XKMSService` binds the caller's tenant and delegates to it; xKey's `LocalTPMPolicies` delegates to it for the system scope under the TPM accessor, and its duplicate converter (`localPolicyToTransport`, `formatPolicyTime`, `localObjectKinds`) and `ErrTPMObjectKindInvalid` are deleted in favour of `xkms.ParseTPMObjectKind` / `*xkms.InvalidTPMObjectKindError`.
  - Verified by `TestTPMPolicy_SealsWithoutKeyIDAreDistinctObjects` (simulator, xkmsd: the first of two seals still unseals to its plaintext and keeps its `boot` assignment; failed before the fix), `TestSeal_TPM2Backend_NoAutoGenerate`, `TestUnseal_TPM2Backend_RequiresKeyID`, `TestNewTPMSealedObjectName`, the `TenantTPMPolicies` tests, and the unchanged `pkg/xkms` TPM policy servicer and xKey local-mode simulator suites.

## [0.44.0-alpha] - 2026-09-29

### Security

- **The ACME `http-01` and `dns-01` circuit breakers were global, so one account's always-failing validation target could stall validation for every other account** (#1189, #1190). `WrapChallengeVerifiers` wrapped each challenge type with a single breaker shared by every account (`http01`, `dns01`); an account naming a target that never responded, or a `dns-01` zone whose authoritative name server was slow, tripped that one breaker and made `ErrCircuitOpen` fail every other account's validation of the same challenge type, healthy targets included.
  - `circuitbreaker.Manager` now supports **per-target breaker groups** (`pkg/acme/server/circuitbreaker/target.go`, `Manager.TargetBreaker`/`RegisterTargetGroup`/`TargetGroupStatuses`): one breaker per validation target — the domain http-01 dials, or the zone dns-01 queries (the only attribution the verifier's signature actually gives the wrapper; there is no visibility into which authoritative name server `net.Resolver.LookupTXT` contacted) — created lazily and looked up by `circuitbreaker.WrapChallengeVerifierPerTarget`, which `WrapChallengeVerifiers` (`pkg/acme/server/resilience.go`) now uses in place of the single-breaker `WrapChallengeVerifier` for `http-01`/`dns-01`. A failing or slow target now only ever affects its own breaker.
  - Each group's table is bounded: an LRU-ordered `container/list` under one mutex evicts the least recently used target once the group's capacity is exceeded, and independently evicts a target idle past its TTL (the same list order serves both, since the least recently used entry is also the longest idle). New `ACMECircuitBreakerConfig` fields `target_capacity` / `target_idle_timeout_seconds` (on the `http01`/`dns01` resilience sections; meaningless elsewhere) configure the bound, defaulting to 1000 targets / 10 minutes idle (`DefaultACMEBreakerTargetCapacity`, `DefaultACMEBreakerTargetIdleTimeoutSeconds`). A refused target (invalid or reserved address) still does not count toward its breaker, per #1181.
  - `GET /acme/health`'s `HealthStatus` gains `target_groups`, a bounded per-group summary (`capacity`, `tracked`, `closed`, `half_open`, `open`, and up to 10 `top_open` target names) alongside the existing named-breaker `breakers` map; `healthy` is unaffected by `target_groups`, since one account's failing target is now expected, isolated behavior rather than a server-wide health signal.
  - Files: `pkg/acme/server/circuitbreaker/{circuitbreaker,decorators,target}.go`, `pkg/acme/server/resilience.go`, `pkg/acme/server/handlers/resilience.go`, `pkg/config/acme_resilience.go`, `cmd/xkmsd/acme.go` (test wiring), `docs/acme-issuance/{architecture,engineering,api}.md`.
  - Verified by new tests in `pkg/acme/server/circuitbreaker/target_test.go` (isolation between targets, capacity/idle-TTL eviction, bounded `/acme/health` summary, a `-race` concurrency stress test) and updated tests in `pkg/acme/server/resilience_test.go`, `pkg/acme/client/trustedca_resilience_test.go` and `cmd/xkmsd/acme_test.go` proving a failing target no longer blocks a healthy one. `go build`, `go vet` and `go test -race` clean for `pkg/acme/...`, `pkg/config/...` and `cmd/xkmsd/...` under `codec_cbor codec_json codec_msgpack tpm_simulator frost`; `golangci-lint` clean on every touched package.
- **File-backed guarded writes (`PutIfAbsent`, `CompareAndSwap`, `CompareAndDelete`) are now atomic across processes sharing one store directory, not only within a single process** (#1157). `pkg/storage/file.FileStorage` — the constructor the PKCS#11 module's `StorageTypeFile` opens directly — previously relied solely on `pkg/storage/engine.go`'s `engineBackend`, whose guard is a Go `sync.Mutex` invisible to a second process. Two module instances sharing one file-token directory could interleave a guarded read-compare-write on the PIN failed-attempt counter (#1144) and both report success, undercounting the shared lockout budget — a bypass reachable by running two processes against the same token instead of one.
  - `pkg/storage/file` now holds an advisory `flock` (`golang.org/x/sys/unix`) on a `.lock` file in the store root across every write this package performs — `Put`, `Delete`, `PutIfAbsent`, `CompareAndSwap`, `CompareAndDelete` — not only the guarded verbs, for the same reason `writeMu` covers unconditional writes in-process: an unguarded write from another process landing inside a guarded operation's critical section would defeat the guard exactly as it would locally. A fresh file description is opened and locked per call rather than held for the store's lifetime, since `flock(2)` locks are scoped to the open file description; this single mechanism serializes concurrent goroutines in one process and every other process with no separate in-process mutex to keep paired with it.
  - The lock file never collides with a stored key: `encodeKeyToPath` already percent-escapes a segment's leading `.`, and the go-qrdb file engine's own `List`/`Scan` already skip dot-prefixed entries.
  - Verified with `TestFileStorage_CompareAndSwap_ConcurrentAccumulates` (single-process, many goroutines) and `TestFileStorage_CompareAndSwap_CrossProcessAccumulates` (re-execs the test binary as several real OS processes racing a compare-and-swap retry loop against one shared counter) in `pkg/storage/file/crosslock_test.go`, and `TestModuleStorage_FailedAttemptCounter_CrossProcessAccumulates` in `pkg/pkcs11/module/storage_crossprocess_test.go`, which exercises the actual #1144 PIN attempt counter across real processes sharing a `StorageTypeFile` token and asserts the durable count is exact. All three fail deterministically when the lock is removed.
  - Files: `pkg/storage/file/lock.go` (new), `pkg/storage/file/storage.go`, `storage_putifabsent.go`, `storage_compareandswap.go`, `storage_compareanddelete.go`, `keypath_test.go`, `coverage_gaps_test.go`, `crosslock_test.go` (new); `pkg/pkcs11/module/storage_crossprocess_test.go` (new).
  - Verified by `go test -race` on `pkg/storage/...` and `pkg/pkcs11/module/...`, `go vet`, and `golangci-lint run` (0 issues) on both packages and `cmd/pkcs11-module`.
- **A provisioned account's first passkey could be enrolled by anyone who knew its email, with no proof of possession; account creation now issues a single-use activation invitation instead, and enrollment of the first credential is authorized by redeeming it** (#1294 part B).
  - `pkg/webauthn.Service.BeginRegistration` — the public, unauthenticated WebAuthn registration entry point — previously enrolled the first passkey of ANY existing account that held zero credentials, including one an administrator had just provisioned through `CreateUser`. It now refuses every account that existed before the call, whatever its credential count; the only account it may still enroll a passkey for is one it creates itself in the same call, under open self-registration (`AllowPublicRegistration`).
  - `XKMSService.CreateUser` (`pkg/xkms/servicer_user.go`) now creates an email-login-key account `LifecyclePending`, not active, and mints a single-use activation invitation through go-qrdb's canonical `invite.TenantStore` in the same call — the plaintext token is returned exactly once (`transport.GetUserResponse.Invite`), never recoverable afterward. A mint failure rolls the account back. The certificate-only/bootstrap path (`WithoutEmailLoginKey`) is unchanged: created active, no invitation.
  - New invite-redemption entry points: `pkg/webauthn.Service.BeginInviteRegistration`/`FinishInviteRegistration` (require `LifecyclePending`, zero credentials) and `pkg/xkms.XKMSService.{GetInvite,BeginInviteRegistration,FinishInviteRegistration,ActivateInvitePIV}`, which bind the credential to the still-pending account, activate it, and redeem the invitation — in that order, so a failure at any step never leaves a redeemed invite pointing at an unactivated account or a live token on an already-active one. Every unusable token (absent, expired, already redeemed, malformed) answers with the one opaque `invite_unusable`/`ErrInviteUnusable` response.
  - These four are composed surface (`transport.InviteServicer`/`InviteService`, embedded into `transport.XKMSServicer`/`transport.Client`), so they are public/unauthenticated on **every** transport, not REST alone: REST (`/api/v1/invites/{tenant_id}/{token}`, `.../fido2/begin`, `.../fido2/finish`, `.../piv/activate`), gRPC and Unix (`KeystoreService.{GetInvite,BeginInviteRegistration,FinishInviteRegistration,ActivateInvitePIV}`, new deliberately-unannotated RPCs in `pkg/api/grpc/proto/xkmsv1/xkms.proto`, regenerated), QUIC (reuses the REST handlers over HTTP/3), and the embedded transport. MCP exposes `invite.get`/`invite.pivActivate` as ordinary public methods but excludes the FIDO2 Begin/Finish pair (`ErrIdentityCeremonyExcluded`), the same go-xkms#193 ruling already applied to `BeginRegistration`/`FinishRegistration`: MCP holds no state to correlate a Begin call with its Finish, and an agent-facing tool surface must not mint sessions or enroll credentials. `pkg/api/grpc/authz_proto_option_test.go`'s ungated-RPC golden register was updated for the four new RPCs.
  - New `xkmsctl user invite redeem <invite-link-or-token>` (`cmd/xkmsctl/user_invite.go`) redeems an invitation over `xkmsctl`'s default transport: FIDO2 (default) drives the local CTAP2 security key through the registration ceremony; `--method piv` activates with a presented PIV certificate. Replaces the REST-curl workaround previously documented in `docs/user-onboarding/cli.md`.
  - `transport.CreateUserRequest` gains `InviteTTLSeconds`; `transport.GetUserResponse` gains `Invite *InviteInfo` — propagated on every transport's `CreateUser` (REST, gRPC, Unix, QUIC, MCP, embedded); the gRPC/Unix wire gained `CreateUserRequest.invite_ttl_seconds` and `UserResponse.invite` (`pkg/api/grpc/proto/xkmsv1/xkms.proto`, regenerated).
  - New operator config section `invite:` (`public_base_url`, `default_ttl`, `max_ttl`) controls the invitation link and TTL bounds. The invite store works in xkmsd's **default** configuration through exactly ONE storage path, with no fallback (per the owner's standing "never use fallbacks without approval" rule): `pkg/server/server.go` wires `pkg/server.tenantPrefixedInviteStore` (`invite_store.go`, new; renamed from an earlier `fileInviteStore` once the fallback it existed to feed was removed) unconditionally, built on the same `createStorage` seam every other xkmsd subsystem's persistent metadata uses (the `pkcs11state` precedent), namespaced per tenant with `storage.NewPrefixBackend` over the existing `pkg/storage/kvadapter` bridge, using the qrdb SDK's own `qrdbsdk.NewInviteStore`/`InviteDAOStore` for every single-use/redemption semantic. An earlier revision tried `qrdbsdk.TenantInviteStore` over the embedded qrdb node's `StoreResolver` (available only with a configured barrier registry) first and fell back to a `createStorage`-backed store otherwise; that two-path design was removed as an unapproved fallback. `createStorage` itself becomes a prefixed, barrier-protected, replicated view over one shared qrdb datastore under go-xkms#1363, and this store moves with that change automatically. `CreateUser` fails closed (`xkms.ErrNotConfigured`) only if this one store's construction fails; that failure is not fatal to server startup.
  - `xkmsctl user register` and `xkmsctl admin create --method fido2` no longer drive a local FIDO2 ceremony inline (an administrator cannot enroll a passkey on an invitee's behalf); they create the account and print the activation invitation, redeemable with the new `xkmsctl user invite redeem`. The `--device`/`--timeout`/`--user-verification`/`--pin*`/`--origin`/`--rp-id`/`--rp-name` flags were removed from both verbs. `xkmsctl admin create --method mtls` is unaffected.
