- **`xkey device relay` pinned nothing, `xkey device listen`/`relay` served the full xkmsd bridge on Noise static-key possession alone with no liveness proof, and `remote.syncPasswords`/`syncOATH`/`syncAll` exported the password vault and OATH secrets to any paired phone with no desktop approval** (#1306). Four gaps found auditing the phone-pairing protocol against its own docs, closed by reusing the existing Noise/attestation/bridge primitives rather than a new mechanism.
  - `xkey device relay` generated a fresh, unpinned Noise static key every invocation and bound `:8444` on every interface; a phone holding *any* Noise key could complete the handshake, and it never served the xkmsd bridge at all (no `RequestHandler`). It now pins to a specific already-paired device (required `--device` resolution shared with `listen`), reuses that device's own persistent local/remote static keys, binds `127.0.0.1:8444` by default (an explicit non-loopback `--listen` opts into network exposure), and wires the identical request handler and xkmsd bridge `xkey device listen` uses. `phone.TCPPairingConfig` gained `ExpectedRemoteStatic` (mirroring `BLEPeripheralConfig`'s existing pin, refused at construction if set to anything but a full-length key: `ErrTCPServerInvalidPin`) so the pin is enforced by the Noise handshake itself, not merely by configuration intent.
  - A phone-initiated session (`xkey device listen`'s BLE peripheral and, now, `xkey device relay`'s TCP responder) served every `remote.*` method immediately after the Noise handshake, with no re-attestation — unlike a laptop-initiated connection, which `PhoneKeyBackend.Connect` already proves liveness on via the #129 challenge-response protocol. Both `phone.TCPPairingConfig` and `phone.BLEPeripheralConfig` now carry a required `LiveAttest pairing.LiveAttestFunc`: immediately after the handshake and before any request reaches the handler, the responder sends `local.attestDevice` to the phone over the same connection (`pairing.InlineExchange`, a minimal single-exchange request/response built from each transport's raw send/receive primitives) and requires a verified answer. A `nil` `LiveAttest` refuses every connection (`ErrLiveAttestationUnavailable`) rather than silently skipping the check; both CLI commands wire `newLiveAttestor`, the same verifier constructor the initiator path already used.
  - `pairing.Bridge` now requires a `SyncApproval pairing.SyncApprovalFunc` to serve `remote.syncPasswords`, `remote.syncOATH` or `remote.syncAll` — the three methods that export the local password vault or OATH credentials to the phone (`remote.syncTrustStore` and `remote.syncStatus` are unaffected; they carry no secrets). A `nil` approver refuses all three (`ErrSyncApprovalRequired`); a configured approver that declines refuses with `ErrSyncNotApproved`. `xkey device listen`/`relay` wire a new session-level approver (`newSessionSyncApproval`) gated by a new `--allow-sync` flag, one decision made at session start rather than a per-request prompt (both commands run as a foreground daemon with no UI thread to interrupt per request); `xkey fido2`'s phone bridge wires `nil`, since it has no equivalent opt-in flag. A new enterprise policy pair, `policy.phone_sync_allow_secret_export` / `policy.lock_phone_sync_policy` (`PhoneSyncAllowSecretExport`/`LockPhoneSyncPolicy` in `pkg/config.PolicySection`), can lock the decision either way under the existing SO-PIN-sealed policy mechanism, mirroring `PairingAllowUnattestableDevices`/`LockPairingAttestationPolicy`'s precedent exactly (`allowPhoneSyncExport`).
  - `xkey device pair` now derives a short authentication string (SAS) from the #129 attestation channel binding (`pairing.ShortAuthString`, three four-digit groups) and prints it after the handshake, for the operator to compare against what the phone shows — informational only today, since the Android app does not yet display a matching code; see the docs below for exactly what it must compute and show.
  - Several helpers that had no Bluetooth dependency of their own were moved out of `ble`-tagged files into shared, untagged ones so `xkey device relay` (which needs none of them) compiles and works without `-tags ble`: barrier open/seal (`device_barrier_shared.go`), the enterprise-policy resolver and attestation-trust loader (`device_pairing_policy_shared.go`), the local-key unseal/live-attestor constructor (`device_session_shared.go`), the sync-service opener (`device_sync_shared.go`), and the phone-initiated request handler/bridge wiring, now shared by `listen`, `relay`, and `xkey fido2`'s phone bridge (`device_listen_handler.go`).

### Changed

- **`storage.backend`'s "file"/"pebble"/"memory" values, which each built their own private, unreplicated storage engine per xkms subsystem, are removed; xkms now has exactly one global, always-qrdb-backed datastore, configured under the new `datastore:` section (#1345).** Before this change, `Server.createStorage`/`createStorageAt` (`pkg/server/storage_factory.go`) switched on `storage.backend`: `"qrdb"` shared one embedded or remote qrdb node across every subsystem, but `"file"`, `"pebble"` (the default) and `"memory"` each opened a *separate* storage engine per subdirectory — unreplicated, outside the barrier's reach as a single unit, and outside RBAC's identity plane. That was backwards for a library whose whole premise is that go-qrdb owns storage and xkms only composes it (`CLAUDE.md` "Layer Ownership"). `createStorage`/`createStorageAt` now unconditionally return a key-prefixed view over the one shared datastore; they can no longer fail on an unrecognized backend name, because there is nothing left to switch on.
  - **New `config.DatastoreConfig`** (yaml `datastore:`) replaces `config.StorageConfig` (yaml `storage:`): `engine` (`memory`/`file`/`pebble`, default `pebble`) selects the local qrdb database engine — mapped straight onto `qrdbsdk.DaemonDatabaseConfig.Backend`, never a parallel enum — and is only meaningful when `mode` (`standalone`, default, or `remote`) is `standalone`; `path` is the on-disk root, **required for `standalone` regardless of `engine`, `"memory"` included** (go-qrdb roots the node's on-disk state, its vector-storage subsystem in particular, under this directory regardless of the primary KV engine — adopted exactly as go-qrdb's own contract, not worked around; see the "Known go-qrdb SDK constraint" bullet below); `remote` (`config.DatastoreRemoteConfig`, replacing `config.QRDBConfig`) configures dialing an already-running external qrdb cluster (`address`, `transport: rest|grpc`, `tls`) when `mode: remote`.
  - `config.Validate` now fully enumerates the datastore configuration space at config-parse time — invalid `engine`/`mode` values and mode-specific requirements (path, remote address/transport) are refused with a typed `*errs.Message` — instead of the old scheme, where `storage.backend` accepted any non-empty string as long as `storage.path` was set and only failed later, at server construction, in `createStorage`'s `default` case.
  - Network protocols (REST/gRPC/QUIC/MCP) now require `datastore.mode: "standalone"` (previously `storage.backend: "qrdb"`); `cluster.enabled` likewise. RBAC's identity plane is now available in every configuration (standalone or remote) — `config.ComplianceGaps`'s old "RBAC enabled without an identity plane" gap no longer exists, because there is no longer a datastore configuration without one.
  - Barrier encryption-at-rest is unaffected in shape (`config.BarrierConfig`) but now applies uniformly: there is no longer a `storage.backend` choice that silently bypasses it for an entire class of deployments.
  - **Breaking, no compatibility shim (pre-release alpha):** `storage:`/`XKMS_STORAGE_*` config keys are gone; `storage.backend: "file"`/`"pebble"`/`"memory"` deployments must move to `datastore.engine` (same values, same meaning, now shared through the one qrdb-backed store) and drop `storage.backend: "qrdb"` entirely (its behavior is now the unconditional default). `storage.qrdb.*` moves to `datastore.remote.*` when `datastore.mode: "remote"`. Nothing migrates existing on-disk data between the old private per-subsystem stores and the new shared datastore; this is a fresh-deployment change, not an in-place upgrade.

Docs: `docs/datastore/` (renamed and rewritten from `docs/storage-engines/`), `docs/rbac/{architecture,engineering}.md`, `docs/clustering/architecture.md`.

### Fixed

- **`acme/client.EnrollDevice` now installs the IAK certificate it receives during enrollment, so device-attest-01 works on real TPMs without a manual install step** (#1100). Enrollment parsed the issued IAK certificate out of the finalized chain and returned it to the caller, but never called `TPM2.ProvisionIAKCert` — `pkg/acme/challenges/device-attest-01.Setup` reads the certificate back later, via `IAKCertificate()`, to build a device-attest-01 statement's `x5c[0]`, so a device that enrolled and then attested in a separate process (the normal case on real hardware) had no certificate to answer with even though enrollment had succeeded. #1059 fixed only the in-process TPM simulator path, which re-mints a throwaway certificate on every open regardless of what enrollment issued.
  - `client.TPMModule` gained `ProvisionIAKCert(cert *x509.Certificate) error`, implemented by `XKMSTPMAdapter` as a thin delegate to the underlying `TrustedPlatformModule.ProvisionIAKCert`. `EnrollDevice` calls it immediately after parsing the IAK certificate from the finalized chain, before returning; a provisioning failure is a typed `*caerrors.TrustedCAError` naming the cause.
  - The hardware device path (`pkg/acme/client/service.openDeviceTPM`) previously opened without any certificate store at all — `TPM2.ProvisionIAKCert`/`IAKCertificate` refuse with `ErrCertStoreNotConfigured` unless the device configures an NV index for its IAK certificate. It is now given `store.FileCertStore`, a new `CertificateStorer` implementation backed by the same `storage.Backend` the device's key blobs already persist to (`pkg/tpm2/store`), so a hardware device's IAK certificate survives a process restart without a new, separately configured store. The in-process TPM simulator keeps `MemoryCertStore`: it re-provisions a fresh throwaway certificate every time it opens, so nothing needs to persist across restarts for it.
  - Files: `pkg/acme/client/tpm.go`, `pkg/acme/client/enrollment.go`, `pkg/acme/client/service/device_tpm.go`, `pkg/tpm2/store/file_cert_store.go` (new), `pkg/tpm2/store/interfaces.go`.
  - `ProvisionIAKCert`'s public-key match check also caught three test fixtures across the tree that drove `EnrollDevice` against the real in-process TPM 2.0 simulator but returned a canned IAK certificate for an unrelated key, fixed with a new `testutil.FakeACMEDirectory.SetCertsFromCSR` hook that mints the certificate for the IAK public key the client's submitted TCG-CSR-IDEVID actually carries: `TestDeviceManager_Enroll_Success` (`pkg/acme/client/service`), `TestDeviceEnroll_Success` (`pkg/acme/gui/client/api`), `TestDeviceEnrollCmd_Success` (`cmd/acme-client`). Every other caller of `EnrollDevice`/`NewFakeACMEDirectory` in the repo (`pkg/acme/client`'s own suites, `sdk/go`, `xkey`, `test/integration`) either drives a mock `TPMModule` that performs no real key-material check or issues from a genuine CA, so none needed the same fix.
  - Verified by `TestEnrollDevice_InstallsIAKCertificate` / `TestEnrollDevice_ProvisionIAKCertFailure_ReturnsTypedError` (`pkg/acme/client`), `TestXKMSTPMAdapter_ProvisionIAKCert` (`pkg/acme/client`), the `pkg/tpm2/store.FileCertStore` test suite, and the three fixed simulator-backed enrollment tests above. `go test -race` clean on every touched package (`pkg/acme/client/...`, `pkg/acme/server/...`, `pkg/acme/gui/client/api/...`, `cmd/acme-client/...`, `pkg/tpm2/store/...`, `pkg/testutil/...`); `golangci-lint run` clean; `make vet-integration` clean (33 build-tag combinations under `test/integration`, compile-only).
- **Fixed a race in ACME nonce epoch rotation that could install two epochs for one expiry** (#1371). `RestService` tracked the current signing epoch and the time it began as two separate atomics (`nonceEpoch atomic.Pointer[acmenonce.Service]`, `nonceEpochAt atomic.Int64`), updated with two consecutive, non-atomic stores in `rotateNonceEpoch`. A concurrent reader could observe the store to `nonceEpoch` (the fresh epoch) before the store to `nonceEpochAt` (still the retired epoch's start time), compute a stale age for the already-current epoch, and pass that current epoch back into `rotateNonceEpoch` as `stale`. Because the re-check there (`current != stale`) compared against that same already-current pointer, it passed trivially and let the reader perform a second, illegitimate rotation — defeating the single-rotation-per-epoch guarantee `nonceRotateMu` exists to provide. Under `-race -cpu=2,8` with the host CPU-saturated, this reproduced at roughly 1-in-200 concurrent-rotation runs (`TestRestService_NonceEpochRotation_NoConcurrentDoubleRotation`, `pkg/acme/server/handlers/nonce_wiring_test.go`); it did not reproduce with `GOMAXPROCS=1` or without external CPU contention, consistent with a narrow scheduling window between two independent atomic stores.
  - Fixed by collapsing the pair into one `nonceEpochRecord{epoch, at}` swapped through a single `atomic.Pointer[nonceEpochRecord]`, so a reader can never observe a fresh epoch paired with a stale start time. `rotateNonceEpoch`'s re-check now compares whole records, which is sound because a record is only ever replaced as a unit.
  - Files: `pkg/acme/server/handlers/service.go` (`nonceEpochRecord`, `RestService.nonceEpoch`, `currentNonceEpoch`, `rotateNonceEpoch`), `pkg/acme/server/handlers/nonce_wiring_test.go` (updated to the new record type; no test behavior changed).
  - Verified: 4000 runs of `TestRestService_NonceEpochRotation_NoConcurrentDoubleRotation` (`-race -count=1000 -cpu=1,2,4,8`) under artificial CPU oversubscription (32 busy-loop processes on a 24-core host) — 0 failures after the fix, versus 5 failures in 900 runs under the same stress before it. `go test -race` clean on `pkg/acme/server/handlers` and `pkg/acme/nonce`; `golangci-lint run` clean on both packages.
- **Removed the enroll-01 challenge type's dead per-client port parsing** (#1183). `pkg/acme/server/handlers/challenge.go` could parse a port suffix out of a challenge type (`"enroll-01-8880"`), but nothing on the offering side (`createChallenges`, `new_order.go`) ever produced one — every enroll-01/endorse-01/device-attest-01 challenge this server offers is the bare registered type string, which always validates against the type's fixed default port (8080 for the enrollment family, 80 for http-01). The parser made the port-suffixed form look supported when it never routed a challenge anywhere; two devices behind one NAT, or two concurrent enrollments on one host, could never both be served, and the earlier investigation into this exact symptom (documented in `CHANGELOG.md`'s `TestEnrollment_ConcurrentRequests`/`TestEnroll01_CompleteWorkflow` entry) had already established the protocol does not let a client choose its callback port. Actually offering a client-chosen port is a protocol change and needs an explicit design decision; this change only removes the parsing that falsely implied it already worked.
  - `parseChallengeAsDynamicPortAssignment` is deleted. `ChallengeHandler` now looks up the verifier and selects the default port directly from the exact, unsuffixed challenge type. `isEnrollXChallenge` and `IsEndorseChallengeType` (`endorse_eab.go`) now match the literal challenge type instead of stripping a port suffix that is never present.
  - Files: `pkg/acme/server/handlers/challenge.go`, `pkg/acme/server/handlers/endorse_eab.go`, and their test files (dead port-suffix-parsing tests removed; a handful of tests that used a port-suffixed challenge *type string* as an arbitrary unique map key, without testing port parsing, are unaffected).
  - Verified by the existing `pkg/acme/server/handlers` suite (`go test -race` clean) and `golangci-lint run` clean.
- **`xkmsd init` now reaches the process's protected-memory teardown on every exit path, and `run()`'s live-server graceful-shutdown path is now covered by tests that never touch the test process's own signal handling** (#1141). #1153 first split `runProcess()` (which arms go-qrdb's `secure.CatchInterrupt()` and, on return, purges `secure.Purge()`/`enclave.WipeAll()`) from `run()`. This finishes that split for the `init` subcommand: `runInit` and its internal `exitInit` helper used to call `os.Exit` directly on every failure path, which — like any `os.Exit` — terminated the process immediately and skipped `runProcess`'s deferred purge, so a failed (or even a successful) `xkmsd init` never actually wiped the protected-memory buffers `runProcess` exists to guarantee are wiped. Both now return an exit code instead; `subcommands` (the `os.Args[1]` dispatch table `run()` uses) changed from `map[string]func([]string)` to `map[string]func([]string) int` so the code flows back through `run()` → `runProcess()` → `main()`'s single `os.Exit(runProcess())`, and the purge now runs unconditionally.
  - `run()`'s own live-server section — `srv.Start()` through the ACME/server graceful shutdown — is extracted into `serve(shutdownCtx context.Context, srv *server.Server, cfg *config.Config, logger *slog.Logger) int`, which takes its shutdown trigger as an ordinary context parameter. A test drives it with a context it cancels itself, instead of a real SIGTERM racing `secure.CatchInterrupt`'s process-wide `os.Exit` handler (which is what made this path untestable before: `run()` no longer arms that handler, only `runProcess` does).
  - No externally observable behavior changes for a real deployment: exit codes are unchanged, and the purge now runs where it always should have.
  - Files: `cmd/xkmsd/main.go`, `cmd/xkmsd/init.go`, and new tests in `cmd/xkmsd/serve_test.go`, `cmd/xkmsd/runinit_test.go`, `cmd/xkmsd/run_lifecycle_test.go`.
  - Verified by `go test -race ./cmd/xkmsd/...` and `golangci-lint run ./cmd/xkmsd/...`; `cmd/xkmsd` package statement coverage went from ~76.8% to ~90.3%.

## [0.43.0-alpha] - 2026-09-29

### Security

- **The Encrypt RPC's and the AES-GCM key wrap's caller-supplied-nonce reuse guard was in-memory only, so a restart forgot every claim it had made.** `pkg/xkms/servicer_crypto.go`'s `Encrypt` and `pkg/xkms/servicer_wrapkey.go`'s `wrapAESGCM` both already claimed a caller-supplied or provider-generated AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce through the shared, atomic `aead.SharedAEADNonceGuard` before sealing (closing the check-then-record race the per-key-provider `types.AEADSafetyTracker` cannot), but the guard's tracker was process memory: a restart, or a second `xkmsd` node in a cluster, had no way to see a claim another process had already made. PKCS#11 v3.2 §6.13.1–§6.13.2 (`CK_GCM_PARAMS` always takes a caller-supplied `pIv`; `CK_GCM_MESSAGE_PARAMS`'s `ivGenerator` makes the caller-supplied `CKG_NO_GENERATE` an explicitly supported alternative to the mandatory `CKG_GENERATE`) and KMIP v1.4 §3.6/§4.29 (`Random IV` is an opt-in server-generation request; the IV/Counter/Nonce otherwise travels in the client's request, and "the server does not store or otherwise manage" it) both permit a caller-supplied nonce as the default case, so the fix is a durable, atomic guard over that case, not removing caller-supplied nonces.
  - `aead.KeyNonceGuard` gained `PersistentNonceStore`, an optional durable backing consulted from a new `UseContext(ctx, keyMaterial, nonce)` method in addition to the existing in-memory tracker `Use` alone still checks. The persisted identity (`persistentEntry`) is deliberately NOT salted with the guard's own per-process random salt (used only for the in-memory tracker's `entry`): the same (key, nonce) pair has to derive the identical identity after a restart or on a different node, and a per-process salt would defeat that. `claimAEADNonceIn` (`pkg/xkms/aead_nonce_guard.go`, shared by `Encrypt` and the AES-GCM wrap) now calls `UseContext` instead of `Use`.
  - New package `pkg/aeadnonce` implements `aead.PersistentNonceStore` over a `storage.Backend`, mirroring `pkg/pkcs11state`'s and `pkg/staticpw`'s existing thin-namespacing-wrapper pattern rather than adding a new storage mechanism: the claim is `storage.Backend.PutIfAbsent`, so it inherits whatever durability and, with `Storage.Backend: qrdb`, cluster-wide replication the configured backend already provides. `pkg/crypto/aead` itself still takes no dependency on `pkg/storage` or qrdb, so the PKCS#11 module — a cgo-loaded client library with no reason to carry either — is unaffected; its own in-process claim (`guardGCMNonce`) still calls the unchanged `Use`.
  - `pkg/server`'s new `initializeAEADNonceStore` builds the store (via the same `createStorage` seam every other durable subsystem uses) and attaches it to the process-wide `aead.SharedAEADNonceGuard` at startup; the new `detachAEADNonceStore`, called from `shutdown()`, removes it again so the package-singleton guard is never left pointing at storage a stopped server has closed.
  - Files: `pkg/crypto/aead/key_nonce_guard.go`, `pkg/aeadnonce/store.go` (new), `pkg/server/server.go`; tests in `pkg/crypto/aead/key_nonce_guard_persistent_test.go` (new), `pkg/aeadnonce/store_test.go` (new), `pkg/server/server_aeadnonce_test.go` (new); docs in `docs/symmetric-aead/architecture.md`, `docs/symmetric-aead/engineering.md`.
- **A second, non-atomic nonce guard still existed alongside the one above, and it was the only one protecting a caller that never went through `XKMSService`.** The per-backend `types.AEADSafetyTracker` (`CheckNonce`/`RecordNonce`, one instance per `symmetric.Backend`/`azurekv.Backend`/`pkcs11.Backend`/`tpm2.TPM2`/`quantum.QuantumBackend`) checked and recorded in two separate steps under an `RWMutex` — a TOCTOU race two concurrent callers could both win — and knew nothing about a key generated by an earlier process or reachable under a second name, backend instance, or an `sdk/go`/`xkey` caller that constructs a backend directly rather than through the service: that caller never reached the durable guard above at all.
  - `types.AEADSafetyTracker` (`pkg/types/types.go`) lost `CheckNonce`/`RecordNonce` entirely; it now covers only the NIST SP 800-38D bytes-encrypted budget, which is a genuinely separate, per-backend-instance concern the durable guard does not and should not replace. `backend.NewMemoryAEADTracker` (`pkg/backend/aead_tracker.go`) lost its nonce map accordingly.
  - New `pkg/backend/aead_nonce.go` adds `ClaimAEADNonce`/`ClaimGeneratedAEADNonce` (plus `...In` variants taking an explicit guard, for tests): the single point every backend's `Encrypt` now calls, atomically, immediately before `Seal` — the software symmetric backend, Azure Key Vault, PKCS#11, TPM2, and the quantum KEM hybrid encrypter alike. This is the lowest layer common to a request reached through `XKMSService` and one reached by a caller holding a `Backend` directly, so both are now covered by the one shared, optionally-persistent `aead.SharedAEADNonceGuard`. The key identity (`aeadNonceIdentity`) prefers a key's own material wherever the backend already has it in hand for the encryption itself (software symmetric, Azure Key Vault, and TPM2's software AES-GCM path, which unseals the key into process memory for exactly this call) — so the same physical key reached under two names or two instances collides on one guard entry — and falls back to `sealedAEADKeyDomain + attrs.ID()` only for PKCS#11, whose key material never leaves the token at all. `ClaimGeneratedAEADNonce` preserves the one policy difference the old service-layer code had: it tolerates a full guard (a provider-generated nonce is fresh by construction and cannot itself be a repeat), while `ClaimAEADNonce` does not.
  - `pkg/xkms/servicer_crypto.go`'s `Encrypt` and `pkg/xkms/servicer_wrapkey.go`'s `wrapAESGCM` no longer claim anything themselves — `pkg/xkms/aead_nonce_guard.go` (`claimAEADNonce`, `claimGeneratedAEADNonce`, `aeadKeyIdentity`) is deleted. Keeping it alongside the new backend-layer claim would have claimed the same pair twice for every request reached through the service, refusing the first, legitimate call as a false reuse.
  - `backend.ErrNonceReused` is now an alias for `aead.ErrNonceReuse` (was a distinct `errors.New`), so `errors.Is(err, backend.ErrNonceReused)` keeps matching what the guard actually returns.
  - AWS KMS, GCP KMS and Vault Transit were investigated and found out of scope: none of the three ever called `CheckNonce`/`RecordNonce` — each refuses a caller-supplied nonce outright (`ErrCallerNonceNotSupported`) because their remote encryption service manages nonce generation itself, so there is no local (key, nonce) pair for this guard to claim.
  - Files: `pkg/types/types.go`, `pkg/backend/aead_tracker.go`, `pkg/backend/aead_nonce.go` (new), `pkg/backend/errors.go`, `pkg/keyprovider/symmetric/backend.go`, `pkg/backend/azurekv/azurekv_symmetric.go`, `pkg/backend/pkcs11/pkcs11_symmetric.go`, `pkg/tpm2/symmetric.go`, `pkg/keyprovider/quantum/signer.go`, `pkg/xkms/servicer_crypto.go`, `pkg/xkms/servicer_wrapkey.go` (`pkg/xkms/aead_nonce_guard.go` deleted); tests in `pkg/backend/aead_nonce_test.go` (new), plus updates to `pkg/backend/aead_tracker_test.go`, `pkg/backend/pkcs11/pkcs11_symmetric_test.go`, `pkg/backend/awskms/awskms_backend_gaps_test.go`, `pkg/backend/software/software_test.go`, `pkg/keyprovider/symmetric/backend_tracking_test.go`, `pkg/xkms/servicer_crypto_nonce_test.go`, `pkg/xkms/servicer_wrapkey_nonce_test.go`; docs in `docs/symmetric-aead/architecture.md`, `docs/symmetric-aead/engineering.md`.

- **CA certificate revoke had no ownership check; any authenticated caller holding `certs:revoke` could revoke another tenant's certificate, or the server's** (#1229).
  - `pkg/ca`'s `signCSR` — the single issuance site shared by `SignCSR`/`SignCSRWithSPIFFE` and `IssueCertificate`/`IssueCertificateWithProfile` — now records the tenant a certificate was issued for (`""` for the system/platform scope) against its serial via the new `recordCertTenant`, persisted alongside the existing revocation and issued-key records under `cert-tenant/<serial-decimal>.json` in the same replicated `revocationStore`.
  - `XKMSService.RevokeCertificate` (`pkg/xkms/servicer_ca.go`) reads the recorded tenant back with the new `CertificateTenant` and runs it through the same `bindTenantTarget` every other tenant-scoped operation in this service uses: a tenant-scoped caller may revoke only its own tenant's certificates, and any other certificate — including a foreign tenant's or the server's own — is refused with the same not-found-shaped `*TenantBindingError` used elsewhere, before `CA.Revoke` is ever reached. A cross-tenant (system) caller may still revoke any certificate. `IssueCertificate` now binds `req.TenantID` against the caller's own tenant before forwarding it, exactly as `SignCSR` already did, so a tenant-scoped caller cannot mint a certificate attributed to a different tenant either.

  - A certificate issued through a path that never calls `signCSR` (TCG EK/AK/IDevID device-identity certificates, the CA's own root/intermediate chain) carries no tenant record and so resolves to the system/platform scope, reachable only by a cross-tenant caller — strictly more restrictive than before, never a regression.

- **BREAKING: `PKCS11State*`/`SealStore*` permission names changed on gRPC and MCP; `EnableUser`/`DisableUser` permission names changed on all three transports and REST's enable/disable route shape changed.** go-xkms#1249's audit of the "single verb/api model" ruling found two families gated on different, internally-consistent permission models across transports. The PKCS#11 remote-state and platform-sealed-store families: REST's `/api/v1/pkcs11state/*` and `/api/v1/platform/secrets*` routes already carried per-verb CRUD actions (`keys:create`/`get`/`list`/`update`/`delete`), while gRPC's seven `PKCS11State*` RPCs and all six `SealStore*` RPCs (plus MCP's `sealStore.*` methods) collapsed every mutation to a coarse `keys:write` and every read to `keys:read`. Every transport now carries the identical per-verb action: `Put`/`PutIfAbsent`/`SealStorePut` → `keys:create`, `CAS`/`SealStoreReseal` → `keys:update` (a compare-and-swap and a reseal-in-place are both mutations of an existing record, not the creation of a new one), `CAD`/`Delete`/`SealStoreDelete` → `keys:delete`, `Get`/`SealStoreGet`/`SealStoreStatus` → `keys:get`, `List`/`SealStoreList` → `keys:list`. A role granted only `keys:create`/`keys:delete`/`keys:get`/`keys:list` can no longer reach the PKCS#11-state or seal-store CAS/reseal routes over gRPC or MCP (it needs `keys:update` too, same as REST already required); a role granted only `keys:write`/`keys:read` on gRPC or MCP for these operations must be re-granted the per-verb equivalents. REST's own routes are unchanged.
  User enable/disable: gRPC's `EnableUser`/`DisableUser` RPCs and MCP's `user.enable`/`user.disable` methods required the coarse `users:update`, and REST served both directions from a single `PUT /api/v1/users/{username}` route with an `{"enabled": bool}` body — which could also only carry `users:update`, since the static permission gate runs before the body is decoded and so cannot see which direction a request means. All three transports now require go-qrdb's own `users:enable`/`users:disable` (`permission.UsersEnable`/`UsersDisable`): REST serves `POST /api/v1/users/{username}/enable` and `.../disable` as their own routes (no body), matching gRPC and MCP exactly. `PUT /api/v1/users/{username}` is gone entirely — it had no purpose beyond the enable/disable toggle, and pre-release carries no compat shim. A role granted only `users:update` can no longer enable or disable a user on any transport; it needs `users:enable`/`users:disable`.
  - Retired the xkms-minted `keys:read`/`keys:write` permission names entirely (`pkg/apimodule/module_scopes.go`'s `selfScopedPermissions`): nothing gates on them anymore now that the PKCS#11-state and seal-store families use qrdb's own per-verb `keys:*` actions, which qrdb already declares tenancy scope for. `keys:update` remains xkms-owned (qrdb's `keys:*` vocabulary has no `update` member) and keeps its `ScopeSelf` declaration.
  - `pkg/api/authz_consistency_test`'s cross-transport golden gained seven `pkcs11state.*` entries (one per RPC/route) and `users.enable`/`users.disable` entries covering all three transports, and dropped the `pkcs11state.*` and `users.update` carve-outs it used to allowlist.
  - `sdk/ts/src/clients/users.ts`: `update(username, {enabled})` replaced by `enable(username)`/`disable(username)`; `UpdateUserRequest` removed from `sdk/ts/src/types/users.ts` (nothing else used it). `web/app/src/views/UsersView.svelte`'s toggle button now calls `users.enable`/`users.disable` directly and gates on `can("users","enable")`/`can("users","disable")` instead of `can("users","update")`. `xkmsctl user update` (`cmd/xkmsctl/user.go`) is unchanged at the CLI surface — it already went through the SDK's `EnableUser`/`DisableUser` transport methods, not a raw HTTP call, so only its doc comment needed updating.
- **BREAKING: `POST /api/v1/passwords/access-mode` now requires `passwords:write` on REST, closing the last #1249 exception.** The owner ruled (2026-09-29) that the password vault is not a login feature, so this route drops its `RouteAuthSession` tier (any authenticated caller, no RBAC check) and joins its `passwords:*` siblings on the qrdb-native coarse read/write model gRPC's `PasswordStoreSetAccessMode` and MCP's `password.setAccessMode` already required — the passwords family is deliberately coarse (qrdb declares no per-verb CRUD for it), so `passwords:write` is the correct grant, not a new per-verb action. A caller without `passwords:write` who previously could still change the access-control strategy over REST alone now gets the same `403` gRPC and MCP already gave. No SDK or web-app change was needed: neither `sdk/ts` nor `web/app`/`xkey` gate a `can("passwords", ...)` UI control on this route (there is no such call site in either app), and `xkey`'s CLI/GUI already called this operation through the gRPC/Unix transport clients, which already required `passwords:write`.

### Added

- **The Azure Key Vault backend now uses Azure's native BYOK (bring-your-own-key) flow instead of unwrapping key material locally** (#1342). `pkg/backend/azurekv.Backend.ImportKey` used to unwrap the caller's wrapped key material inside this process -- with a locally generated ephemeral RSA wrapping keypair -- and send the resulting plaintext private key to Azure Key Vault's `ImportKey` API as a standard JWK. That meant the target key's plaintext existed inside xkms, briefly, on every import.
  - `GetImportParameters` now provisions (once, and reuses on every later call) a vault-scoped RSA-HSM key-encryption key (KEK) with Azure Key Vault's `import` key operation, and returns its public half. `WrapKey` wraps the caller's key material client-side against that public key using `CKM_RSA_AES_KEY_WRAP` (RSA-OAEP-256 wraps an ephemeral AES-256 key, which wraps the target key material with AES-KWP) -- the wire format Azure Key Vault's `key_hsm` transfer field requires. `ImportKey` sends the wrapped blob to Azure Key Vault as the JWK `key_hsm` (`T`) field with `HSM: true`; Azure's own HSM performs the unwrap, using the KEK's private half, which never leaves the HSM boundary. `UnwrapKey` is now unconditionally `backend.ErrNotSupported` -- there is no local unwrap step left to perform.
  - The single-use import token from #1340/#1342's `pkg/backend/importtoken.Store` now binds each ceremony to the KEK's `kid` and the wrapping algorithm (a `kekBinding`, not a sealed local wrapping key): `ImportKey` refuses a token whose algorithm does not match `WrappedKeyMaterial.Algorithm`, and refuses one whose KEK has since been rotated or recreated, before ever presenting a doomed blob to Azure.
  - Plain RSA-OAEP wrapping (with no AES-KWP layer) is no longer accepted by `GetImportParameters`/`WrapKey`: it is not a valid Azure Key Vault `key_hsm` encoding on its own.
  - Files: `pkg/backend/azurekv/{azurekv,azurekv_importexport,mock_client}.go`, `pkg/backend/azurekv/{azurekv_importexport_test,import_token_handle_test,import_token_bounds_test,azurekv_test}.go`, `test/integration/azurekv/{azurekv_importexport_integration_test,azurekv_cloud_integration_test}.go`, `docs/backends/azurekv.md`.
  - Verified by: `pkg/backend/azurekv` unit tests against the mock Key Vault client (KEK created once and reused across ceremonies and algorithms; `ImportKey` sends `key_hsm` carrying the wrapped blob and never a plaintext key component under `HSM: true`; a wrapping-algorithm mismatch between the token and `WrappedKeyMaterial` is refused with `*importtoken.AlgorithmMismatchError`; an unknown, expired, or already-consumed import token is refused with `backend.ErrKeyNotFound`); `go vet` and `go test -race` under `-tags azurekv`; `go build`/`go vet` under `-tags "codec_cbor codec_json codec_msgpack tpm_simulator frost azurekv"` and with `integration` added.
  - Fixes #1342 (item 1; items 2 and 3 shipped in #1349).

## [0.42.0-alpha] - 2026-09-29

### Security

- **CI workflows are hardened (#1335).**
  - Third-party actions are pinned to full commit SHAs.
  - `ci.yml` defaults to `permissions: contents: read`, with per-job overrides.
  - Every checkout sets `persist-credentials: false`.
  - Workflow outputs reach scripts through environment variables, not template interpolation.
  - Build and scan images are pinned by digest.
  - Release-process changes (#1334) are left out on the owner's instruction.
- **The `fido2` auth factor accepted an assertion that only proved user presence, and never checked the clientData `origin`** (#1289). `Verify` checked `authenticatorData`'s user-present flag but not its user-verified flag, and no enrollment recorded either a user-verification requirement or an expected origin, so `Verify` had nothing to check `clientDataJSON.origin` against. An assertion produced with a PIN/biometric bypass, or against a spoofed page that relayed a genuine authenticator's touch, still verified.
  - `Enroll` now records both at enrollment time: `"origins"` (a string or `[]string` MethodParam, defaulting to `["https://" + rp_id]`) and `"require_user_verification"` (a bool MethodParam, defaulting to **true** — the WebAuthn/CTAP2 best practice for a factor used to unseal or authenticate). `Challenge` carries both into `MethodData` (`origins` as `[]string`, `require_uv` as `bool`) alongside the existing enrolled key and rp id.
  - `Verify` now refuses when the enrollment requires verification and `authenticatorData`'s user-verified flag is clear, and refuses when `clientDataJSON.origin` is not exactly one of the enrolled origins — checked with go-webauthn's own `protocol.IsOriginInHaystack` comparator rather than a re-implemented string match. An enrollment missing either field (for example, one recorded before this change) leaves the corresponding `MethodData` key unset; `Verify` treats that the same as any other incomplete challenge and refuses — go-xkms is pre-release and carries no compatibility path for such enrollments.
  - The FIDO2 CTAP2 local enrollment ceremony (`LocalCeremony.Enroll`, used at init/administrator enrollment) now records the same origin (`"https://" + rp_id`) and user-verification requirement it actually presented to the authenticator, rather than relying on `Factor.Enroll`'s defaults to happen to agree.
  - Files: `pkg/factor/fido2/factor.go`, `pkg/factor/fido2/ctap2.go`, `pkg/factor/fido2/factor_test.go`, `docs/auth-factors/{architecture,engineering,api,user}.md`.
  - Verified by `TestFIDO2Factor_Verify_RejectsUserPresenceWithoutVerification`, `TestFIDO2Factor_Verify_AcceptsUserPresenceWhenVerificationNotRequired`, `TestFIDO2Factor_Verify_RejectsChallengeWithoutRequireUV`, `TestFIDO2Factor_Verify_RejectsWrongOrigin`, `TestFIDO2Factor_Verify_AcceptsAnyEnrolledOrigin`, `TestFIDO2Factor_Verify_RejectsChallengeWithoutOrigins`, `TestFIDO2Factor_Enroll_RecordsOriginAndUVRequirement`, `TestFIDO2Factor_Enroll_RecordsExplicitOriginsAndUVOverride`, `TestFIDO2Factor_Enroll_RejectsEmptyOrigins`, and `TestFIDO2Factor_Enroll_RejectsMalformedRequireUserVerification`. `go build`, `go vet` and `go test -race` clean for `pkg/factor/...` and `pkg/init/...` under `codec_cbor codec_json codec_msgpack tpm_simulator frost`.
  - Addresses #1289 (items 2 and 3; item 4 landed in #1329).

### Fixed

- **`make lint`/`make vet` now cover the pkcs11/awskms/azurekv/gcpkms/vault/raft-tagged root-module code, and every `//nolint` in the codebase now names its linter and carries a reason** (#1348). `LINT_TAGS_root` only ever carried `TEST_TAGS`, so every file behind the hardware/cloud KMS backend tags and the raft clustering tag compiled (via `go build`/`go test`) but was never linted — the same "a tag nobody passes is a directory the toolchain never opens" gap #650/#682 already closed for test/integration and for xkey.
  - Two new root-module passes, `LINT_TAGS_root_backends` (`pkcs8,tpm2,awskms,gcpkms,azurekv,pkcs11,vault` unioned with the default set) and `LINT_TAGS_root_raft` (the default set plus `raft`), wired into both `make vet` and `make lint`. Each tag combination is one CI already proves compiles (the ci.yml `build`/`race`/`build-raft` jobs), verified locally with `go build`/`go vet` before being added to the gate.
  - Fixing what the new passes found surfaced real defects, not just style: `awskms.Decrypt` ignored the caller's OAEP hash choice (both branches of an `if opts != nil` set the same algorithm) and now honors an explicit SHA-1 request; `azurekv`'s symmetric decrypt appended a GCM tag directly onto the caller's ciphertext slice, risking a silent write into its spare capacity, and now allocates its own backing array; `pkcs11.DeriveKeyECDH` accepted a `ctx` parameter it normalized but never consulted, and now checks `ctx.Err()` before doing HSM work, matching `Backend.AttestKey`; two `SA4023` "comparison never true" findings in `azurekv.Sign`/`Verify` were dead `opts == nil` checks against a `crypto.Hash` value that can never be a nil interface; two `SA9003` empty-branch findings (`vault.DeleteKey`, `gcpkms.DeleteKey`) silently discarded a config/metadata cleanup error with no code in the branch at all, and now log or explicitly discard with a reason.
  - `nolintlint` is enabled with `require-explanation: true` and `require-specific: true`. Enabling it surfaced 76 pre-existing `//nolint` directives repo-wide that were either missing a reason or no longer doing anything (the underlying linter never fires there — most commonly `//nolint:errcheck` in a `_test.go` file, which `.golangci.yml` already excludes from errcheck, or a `//nolint:staticcheck` written against `key.PublicKey.X`-style deprecated-field access that a later `QF1008` rewrite simplified to the promoted `key.X` form staticcheck's `SA1019` check does not follow through embedding). Genuine suppressions (raw ECDSA/RSA coordinates for wire-format compatibility, PKCS#1 v1.5 support gated behind a documented reason, etc.) kept their `//nolint` with an accurate reason added; directives with nothing left to suppress were removed, in some cases exposing dead code (`pkg/backend/pkcs11/pkcs11_mock_test.go`'s unused `mockSigner`, `pkg/backend/pkcs11/signer_rsa.go`'s unused `rsaOID`, four unused test helpers in `pkg/backend/pkcs11/pkcs11_importexport_test.go`, one in `pkg/backend/vault/transit_double_vault_test.go`) that was deleted rather than re-suppressed.
  - `errcheck` v1.9.0 at `/usr/local/bin/errcheck` crashes on Go 1.27 export data, but nothing in this repository pins or invokes that standalone binary — `make lint`/CI use golangci-lint's bundled errcheck exclusively — so no version pin needed changing.
  - Files: `Makefile`, `.golangci.yml`, and the fixes/nolint reasons above span `pkg/backend/{awskms,azurekv,gcpkms,pkcs11,vault}`, `pkg/crypto/rand`, `pkg/pivcert/pkcs11`, `pkg/auth/token`, `pkg/acme/client`, `pkg/ca`, `pkg/certstore`, `pkg/tpm2`, `pkg/ssh/session`, `pkg/api/grpc`, `pkg/trust/resolver`, `cmd/xkmsd`, `examples/certificates/hardware/hybrid`, and `xkey/pkg/{ipc,gui/services}`.
  - Verified by `make lint` (all six passes: root default/backends/raft, sdk/go, xkey, web/desktop) and the existing test suites for every touched package.
- **Fourteen discarded errors across xkey and go-xkms now fail closed instead of being silently swallowed** (#1346). In every case a `_ :=`/`_, _ :=` (or similarly ignored) error meant a caller proceeded as if an operation had succeeded — sealing without the requested password, importing a duplicate the store failed to report, skipping owner-hierarchy auth on an EK certificate NV write — when it had actually failed or its outcome was unknown.
  - `xkey/pkg/gui/services/seal_service.go`: `SealData` now returns the new `ErrSealPasswordUnavailable` before calling the SDK client if `opts.Password.String()` fails, instead of sealing with an empty password.
  - `xkey/pkg/oidc/aws/response.go`: `TokenResponse.ToTokenData` now propagates a `GetExpirationTime` failure instead of silently zeroing `Expiration`.
  - `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/seal.go`: a staging-directory cleanup failure during a failed migration copy is now joined into the returned `*SealError` and the staging path reported, instead of being discarded.
  - `xkey/pkg/luks/volume.go` and `detect.go`: `IsMounted` now returns `(bool, error)` instead of swallowing the underlying mount-check error to `false`. Propagated through every caller: `pkg/storage/luks` (`VolumeOperator` interface and `Backend.Attach`, with the new `VolumeMountCheckError`), `xkey/pkg/gui/services/storage_service.go` (`RequireUnlocked`, `GetStatus`), and the `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd` LUKS commands (`root.go`, `lock.go`, `unseal.go`, `seal.go`, `wipe.go`, `migrate.go`, `import_data.go`) — each now fails closed (never proceeds as if unmounted) when the mount state can't be determined.
  - `xkey/pkg/audit/store.go` and `dao_store.go`: a failure writing to the configured `slog.Logger` is now joined into the write-failure path (so a `SeveritySecurity` operation still surfaces `*ErrAuditWriteFailed`) instead of being dropped. The `slog` field is now the new package-internal `entryLogger` interface so tests can inject a failing logger.
  - `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/device_enroll_phone.go`: every `device enroll-phone` flag is now bound with `*Var` (e.g. `StringVar`, `DurationVar`) instead of read back with `f.GetString`/`GetDuration`/`GetBool`/`GetStringSlice`, which discarded lookup errors and could leave `enrollPhoneOptions` at its zero value.

  - `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/oidc.go`: the auto-refresh exec hook now skips its cycle and logs when `parseIDToken` fails, instead of running the hook with an empty `Subject`/`Email`/`Name`.

  - `xkey/pkg/pwimport/importer.go`: a `store.Get` failure other than `xkms.ErrStaticPasswordNotFound` now records the entry as a failed import, instead of being treated as "no existing entry" and imported anyway.
  - `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/tpm_idevid_cert.go`: `runIDevIDCSRExportPEM` now tolerates only "no OpenSSL config file found" (`LoadOpenSSLConfig` returning `(nil, nil)`); a config file that exists but fails to parse now fails the command. Extracted to the testable `buildCSRSubjectFromOpenSSLDefaults`.
  - `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/tpm_ek.go`: `runEKRestore` now calls `tpm.ProvisionEKCert(hierarchyAuth, ...)` (via the new `restoreEKCert`) instead of `tpm.WriteEKCert`, which always passed a nil hierarchy auth — an EK certificate NV index protected by owner/platform hierarchy auth could not previously be restored. `hierarchyAuth` is wiped via `enclave.Wipe` after the call.
  - `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/fido2.go`: the `/dev/urandom`-backed `cryptoRandRead` now uses `io.ReadFull` (via the new `readCryptoRandomFrom`) instead of a single `Read`, so a short read no longer silently yields fewer random bytes than requested for the FIDO2 serial number.

## [0.41.0-alpha] - 2026-09-29

### Security

- **The xkey agent server's mTLS revocation check was skipped on TLS session resumption** (#1285). `Server.buildTLSConfig` wired the agent-connection and revocation-status check (`EnrollmentService.VerifyAgentCertificate`) onto `tls.Config.VerifyPeerCertificate`, which Go does not call when a session resumes from a ticket — a revoked or removed agent holding a still-valid ticket kept access for up to the ticket's 7-day lifetime. The check now runs as `tls.Config.VerifyConnection`, which Go calls on every handshake including a resumed one, using the certificate chain Go restores into `ConnectionState.VerifiedChains` for the resumed session. The server also now sets `SessionTicketsDisabled: true` as defence in depth: this server's agent connections are long-lived and already reconnect with their own backoff, so there is no latency-sensitive case here that needs 0-RTT resumption, and disabling tickets means no connection can reach the wire without running the full handshake.
  - Files: `xkey/pkg/agent/server.go`, `xkey/pkg/agent/server_test.go`, `xkey/pkg/agent/server_resumption_test.go` (new).
  - Verified by `TestServer_TLSSessionResumption_RevokedAgentRefused`, a real TLS handshake test that captures a session ticket over a loopback connection, revokes the agent's certificate, then resumes the session and confirms the server refuses it (`ConnectionState.DidResume` is asserted true at the moment the check runs, so the test fails if it stops exercising the resumption path); `TestServer_TLSSessionResumption_NonRevokedAgentStillResumes` proves a still-enrolled, unrevoked agent's resumed session keeps working; `TestServer_BuildTLSConfig_SessionTicketsDisabled` proves the production config disables tickets. The xkey agent client (`xkey/pkg/agent/client.go`) and every other `tls.Config` in xkey (`grep -rn VerifyPeerCertificate xkey`) were audited and found not to rely on `VerifyPeerCertificate` for a security decision; `cmd/xkey/cmd/auth.go`'s SPKI-pinned client config already uses `VerifyConnection`.
  - `go vet -tags "codec_json tpm_simulator" ./pkg/agent/...` and `go test -race -tags "codec_json tpm_simulator" ./pkg/agent/...` clean.
- **The xkey API Explorer response preview rendered fetched HTML in a same-origin, scripted `srcdoc` iframe** (#1274). `APIExplorer.svelte`'s preview tab set `sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups"` by default, and that same default was writable via user config (`gui.api_explorer_sandbox_policy`) and enterprise policy (`policy.api_explorer_sandbox_policy`). A `srcdoc` frame with `allow-same-origin` shares the parent document's origin, so `allow-scripts` combined with it let script in *any* fetched HTML response reach `window.parent`, including every Wails service binding — `OIDCService.ExecuteScript` among them, which shells out. The default policy no longer includes `allow-same-origin` or `allow-scripts`: previewing rendered HTML needs neither, and without `allow-same-origin` the srcdoc document has a unique opaque origin, so `allow-scripts` alone (if a user re-enables it) can no longer reach the parent at all.
  - New shared validator, mirrored in TypeScript and Go: `xkey/frontend/src/lib/utils/sandboxPolicy.ts` (`validateSandboxPolicy`) and `xkey/pkg/config/sandbox_policy.go` (`ValidateAPIExplorerSandboxPolicy`). Both refuse `allow-scripts` + `allow-same-origin` together, and refuse `allow-top-navigation*`, `allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox`, and `allow-modals` outright, regardless of combination. `APIExplorer.svelte` and `Settings.svelte` validate every policy they load or build (user config, enterprise override, and the Settings toggles) and fall back to the safe default with a visible notification when a policy is refused.
  - Go is authoritative, not just advisory: `config.Config.Validate()` now rejects a `policy.api_explorer_sandbox_policy` (enterprise policy) that carries the dangerous combination or a forbidden directive, since that plane is opt-in and security-authoritative. `gui.GUIConfig.Validate()` normalizes (rather than rejects) an invalid `gui.api_explorer_sandbox_policy`, because every installation that has not touched Settings since before this fix already has the old dangerous string persisted on disk as its default, and rejecting it outright would lock every existing user out at next launch.
  - Added a `Content-Security-Policy` restricting frame sources to `frame-src 'self' about: data:` (plus `object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'`), applied via a Wails `AssetServer` middleware (`pkg/gui/csp.go`) for the built app and via a `<meta>` tag in `frontend/index.html` for the Vite dev server. This is deliberately narrower than a full CSP: `script-src`/`style-src`/`connect-src` are left unrestricted because the Svelte build's inline style attributes, xterm.js, and the Vite dev server could not be exercised against a running GUI to confirm a stricter policy would not break them.
  - Files: `xkey/frontend/src/lib/utils/sandboxPolicy.ts` (new), `xkey/frontend/src/views/APIExplorer.svelte`, `xkey/frontend/src/views/Settings.svelte`, `xkey/frontend/index.html`, `xkey/pkg/config/sandbox_policy.go` (new), `xkey/pkg/config/errors.go`, `xkey/pkg/config/config.go`, `xkey/pkg/gui/config.go`, `xkey/pkg/gui/csp.go` (new), `xkey/pkg/gui/app.go`.
  - Verified by: new vitest suites `sandboxPolicy.test.ts` (13 cases) and `APIExplorer.test.ts` (renders the component through the real `window.go` seam and asserts the rendered iframe's `sandbox` attribute), both passing under `make frontend-test`; new Go tests in `pkg/config/sandbox_policy_test.go`, `pkg/config/config_test.go`, and `pkg/gui/config_test.go`; `go build`/`go vet` clean under `codec_json tpm_simulator ble` for `pkg/config/...` and `pkg/gui/...`. The Wails CSP header and dev-server meta tag were not exercised against a running GUI; see the file-level comments in `pkg/gui/csp.go` and `frontend/index.html` for exactly what remains unverified.
  - Fixes #1274.
- **Four independent bearer/session-auth gaps closed: a JWT with no `exp` claim, an OIDC ID token that failed audience validation salvaged through the userinfo endpoint, the Unix socket gRPC listener trusting file mode alone with no kernel peer-credential check, and an xkey SSH console ticket that never expired** (#1299).
  - `pkg/auth.JWTAuthenticator.validateToken` now parses with `jwt.WithExpirationRequired()`, so a token that omits `exp` entirely — which jwt/v5 otherwise treats as never expiring — is refused rather than accepted as a permanent credential. Operator key-file mode (`auth.jwt.public_key_file`) now refuses to start with the new typed sentinel `server.ErrJWTKeyFileIssuerAudienceRequired` unless both `issuer` and `audience` are configured; without them `JWTAuthenticator` skips both checks and accepts a token from any issuer for any audience so long as it is signed by the configured key. The internally-issued-token path (`pkg/auth/token.Issuer`) was already stamping `exp`/`iss`/`aud` on every access and refresh token and needed no change.
  - `pkg/auth.OIDCAuthenticator.validateToken` no longer falls back to the userinfo endpoint whenever ID-token validation failed for any reason (bad signature, wrong issuer, or — most dangerously — a mismatched audience); it falls back only when the token does not parse as a JWT at all (`jwt.ParseUnverified` fails), which is the only case that legitimately belongs to the opaque-access-token flow. Both `validateIDToken` and `validateAccessToken` now also refuse an empty `sub` claim (the existing but previously unused `ErrOIDCMissingSubject` sentinel), so neither an ID token nor a userinfo response can mint an `Identity` for nobody. RFC 7662 token introspection was not added for opaque access tokens — this authenticator's `OIDCConfig` carries no client secret to authenticate an introspection call with, and adding one is config/discovery plumbing of its own, tracked as a follow-up; the userinfo endpoint remains the opaque-token verification path.
  - `pkg/api/unix.GRPCServer` registers its keystore service with `WithLocalTrust` (RBAC off), trusting only the Unix socket's file mode and directory permissions — but had no check on who was actually on the other end of an accepted connection, and no check that a pre-existing socket directory hadn't been left group- or world-writable. `Start` now validates the socket directory (new `validateSocketDir`, mirroring `pkg/ssh/agent`'s own work-directory check: not a symlink, not writable by group or other, owned by this process) before binding, and installs `grpc.Creds` with a new accept-time transport credential (`peerCredentialTransport`) that reads the kernel-verified peer UID/GID via `pkg/peercred` and refuses any peer that is not the daemon's own uid, root, or an entry in the new `GRPCConfig.AllowedUIDs`/`AllowedGIDs` allowlist. The kernel peer-credential syscalls (`SO_PEERCRED` on Linux, `LOCAL_PEERCRED`/`LOCAL_PEEREPID` on Darwin) were previously duplicated in `pkg/acme/api/server`; both listeners now share the one implementation in the new `pkg/peercred` package, and `Start` refuses to run at all on a platform `pkg/peercred.CheckSupport` has not verified one for.
  - `xkey/pkg/gui/services.SSHConsoleService.resolve` redeemed a stored console ticket regardless of its age. It now refuses (and deletes) a ticket older than `consoleTicketTTL`, closing the case of a browser tab left open long after the connect dialog it belonged to was abandoned redeeming a ticket whose signer(s) and host-key policy were captured under stale conditions. A new clock seam (`SSHConsoleService.now`, defaulting to `time.Now`) makes the expiry path hermetic to test without a real 2-minute sleep.
  - Files: `pkg/auth/jwt.go`, `pkg/auth/oidc.go`, `pkg/server/server.go`, `pkg/server/errors.go`, `pkg/peercred/*` (new), `pkg/api/unix/grpc_server.go`, `pkg/api/unix/peercred.go` (new), `pkg/api/unix/sockdir*.go` (new), `pkg/acme/api/server/peercred_{linux,darwin,unsupported}.go`, `xkey/pkg/gui/services/ssh_console_service.go`.
  - Verified by: `pkg/auth`'s existing JWT/OIDC suites plus new cases (`TestJWTAuthenticator_AuthenticateHTTP/missing_exp_claim`, `TestOIDCAuthenticator_AudienceMismatchNotSalvagedByUserinfo`, `TestOIDCAuthenticator_EmptySubjectRefused_{IDToken,AccessToken}`); `pkg/server`'s `TestServer_CreateJWTAuthenticator_KeyFileRequiresIssuerAndAudience`/`_KeyFileWithIssuerAndAudience`; `pkg/peercred`'s own suite plus `pkg/acme/api/server`'s existing peer-credential tests (unchanged, now exercising the shared implementation); `pkg/api/unix`'s new `TestPeerCredentialPolicy_Allowed`, `TestGRPCServer_PeerCredential_SameUIDAccepted`, `TestValidateSocketDir_*`, `TestGRPCServer_Start_RefusesGroupWritableSocketDir`; `xkey`'s new `TestSSHConsole_Resolve_ExpiredTicketRefused`/`_UnexpiredTicketAccepted`. `go vet` and `gofmt` clean under `codec_cbor codec_json codec_msgpack tpm_simulator frost` (root) and `codec_json tpm_simulator ble` (xkey).
  - **Breaking:** operator key-file JWT mode (`auth.jwt.public_key_file`) now requires both `auth.jwt.issuer` and `auth.jwt.audience` to be set; a deployment that configured only `public_key_file` refuses to start until both are added.
  - Fixes #1299.
- **REST's `/keys/wrap` and `/keys/unwrap` required the wrong permission, and `internal/authzscan` did not cover REST, `pkg/acme/admin`, or MCP's own permission table, so nothing would have caught it.** `pkg/api/rest/routes.go` gated `POST /api/v1/keys/wrap`/`unwrap` on `keys:encrypt`/`keys:decrypt` while the identical operation — the same request fields, same underlying `XKMSService.WrapKey`/`UnwrapKey` call — required `keys:wrap`/`keys:unwrap` on gRPC's `WrapKey`/`UnwrapKey` RPCs and MCP's `xkms.wrapKey`/`xkms.unwrapKey` methods (the by-id variants, `/keys/wrap-by-id`/`unwrap-by-id`, already used the correct pair). A caller granted only `keys:wrap` could not reach the plain route; a caller granted only `keys:encrypt` could reach a wrap operation gRPC and MCP both gate more narrowly. Both routes now carry `auth.ActionWrap`/`auth.ActionUnwrap`. Two of the same routes also carried the raw string literals `"derive"`, `"wrap"`, `"unwrap"` instead of `auth.ActionDerive`/`ActionWrap`/`ActionUnwrap` — a retyped literal is a silent authorization change, since it stops matching the qrdb grant with no compile error — with no test that would have caught it.
  - `internal/authzscan.Seam` gained `Bare` (match a plain identifier call, not just a method selector — REST's route-table helpers are local closures) and `LabelArgs`/`LabelPrefix` (key a `Site` by a call's own literal arguments, e.g. the HTTP method and path, instead of the enclosing function name — REST and `pkg/acme/admin` each register dozens of gates from a single function). A new `internal/authzscan.ScanMap` resolves a `map[string]T{"key": {resource, action}}` composite literal the same way `Scan` resolves a call's arguments, for MCP's `methodPermissions`, which is data rather than a sequence of gate calls.
  - New wire-contract goldens: `pkg/api/rest/authz_golden_test.go` (174 routes), `pkg/acme/admin/authz_golden_test.go` (51 `gate.Wrap` registrations), `pkg/api/mcp/authz_golden_test.go` (165 `methodPermissions` entries, reusing the package's existing `goldenMethodPermissions` table so the value-comparison and the literal-rejection tests cannot drift apart). Each fails if a gate is added, removed, repointed, or spelled as a literal — verified by temporarily reintroducing the literal and by deleting a gate, both while writing this fix.
  - New cross-transport consistency golden, `pkg/api/authz_consistency_test` (`TestCapabilities_RequireSamePermissionOnEveryTransport`): re-derives gRPC's, REST's, and MCP's tables from their own source and asserts every capability in a hand-built, audited 157-entry table requires the identical `resource:action` pair on every transport that exposes it. Two further mismatches the audit found are allowlisted (excluded from the checked table) pending a product decision, not fixed here: `POST /api/v1/passwords/access-mode` is REST session-only with no RBAC permission where gRPC/MCP require `passwords:write`; the `PKCS11State*`/`pkcs11state/*` family uses REST per-verb CRUD actions where gRPC collapses to a coarser write/read tiering. Both are two internally-consistent but different design choices, not a wrong-table typo.
  - Fixed the stale `pkg/api/quic` references in `internal/authzscan`'s package doc and `pkg/api/mcp/authz.go`'s `methodPermissions` doc comment (the legacy per-transport listeners, including `pkg/api/quic`, were removed wholesale in favor of HTTP/3 on the REST port) and a stale claim in the latter that REST served PIN/custodian/tenant routes session-only with no RBAC permission of their own — it has carried the matching `pin:*`/`ceremony:*`/`tenants:*`/`tenant_barrier:*` grants since go-xkms#773 and was verified to still agree.
  - Corrected `docs/frost-threshold-signing/architecture.md` and `api.md`, which said no supported `xkmsd` configuration path could register a FROST backend: `pkg/server/backend_frost.go`'s `(*Server).initFrostBackend` has registered one from `backends.frost` in `xkmsd.yaml` since it was added, and `pkg/config.BackendsConfig.Frost` is a real, validated config block. `cli.md` did not carry the stale claim and needed no change.

- **The Azure Key Vault backend no longer hands its import-wrapping private key to the caller** (#1340). `pkg/backend/azurekv.Backend.GetImportParameters` returned the ephemeral RSA wrapping key's PKCS#1 private key as `ImportParameters.ImportToken`, and `UnwrapKey`/`ImportKey` parsed the private key back out of the caller-supplied `WrappedKeyMaterial.ImportToken`. That broke the `ImportParameters` invariant that the unwrapping private key never leaves the backend: anyone who saw the token in transit (REST/gRPC/MCP response, logs) could decrypt the wrapped key material, and a caller could supply a private key of its own choosing. The backend-side store the fix for #1261 bounded was never read.
  - The wrapping private key is now sealed in an `importtoken.SealedRSAKey` held in the backend's `importtoken.Store`, keyed by a random UUID handle, and `ImportToken` is only that handle -- the same pattern the software and symmetric backends use. `UnwrapKey` (and `ImportKey` through it) resolves the handle with a single-use `Take` and refuses an unknown, expired or replayed handle with `backend.ErrKeyNotFound`; a failed unwrap also consumes the handle. The store is no longer keyed by CN, so two concurrent ceremonies for the same CN no longer overwrite each other's wrapping key, and `ImportKey`'s redundant "delete after import" step is gone.
  - Tokens issued before upgrade are refused; callers must request new import parameters. The backend still unwraps locally and imports the key as a JWK; Azure Key Vault's native key-exchange-key BYOK flow is not used.
  - Files: `pkg/backend/azurekv/{azurekv,azurekv_importexport}.go`, `docs/crypto-backends/engineering.md`.

- **Four surfaces not reachable from `xkmsd` today were still unbounded, so a future wiring or a standalone consumer of the affected packages would have inherited the gap** (#1263).
  - xkey's agent gRPC server (`xkey/pkg/agent/server.go`, binds `:9443`) took no `MaxConcurrentStreams`, keepalive enforcement policy, message-size cap, or connection timeout. It now builds its `[]grpc.ServerOption` through a new `grpcServerOptions` method carrying all four, with `Config` gaining `MaxRecvMsgSize`/`MaxSendMsgSize`/`ConnectionTimeout`/`MaxConcurrentStreams` (defaulted in `Validate`, mirroring `pkg/api/unix/grpc_server.go`'s option set) and a `KeepaliveEnforcementPolicy` (30s `MinTime`, `PermitWithoutStream: true` for the agent table's long-lived, bursty connections). The option-building code itself is not shared with `pkg/api/unix`: xkey's own `CLAUDE.md` requires it integrate only through `go-xkms/sdk/go`, never `pkg/*`, directly.
  - `pkg/acme/client/enrollment.go`'s enroll-01 and endorse-01 challenge-activation handlers (`startEnrollServer`, `startEndorseServer`) read `r.Body` with no size cap. Both now wrap the body in `http.MaxBytesReader` at `acmeserver.MaxRequestBodySize` (`pkg/acme/server`'s existing 256 KiB ACME request-body cap, already imported into this package by `trustedca.go`) before reading it, and answer 413 on an oversized body — the same pattern `pkg/acme/challenges/enroll-01/enroll01.go`'s `activateCredentialHandlerWithShutdown` already used.
  - `pkg/ca/ocsp.go`'s in-memory OCSP response cache was keyed on any requested serial number and never evicted, so a client probing distinct serials grew it without bound. `OCSPResponderConfig` gains `MaxCacheEntries` (default 10000, matching `pkg/acme/server/degradation`'s cache default); `cacheResponse` evicts expired entries first and then arbitrary ones (Go's randomized map iteration order) until back under the cap before inserting. Each entry's expiry is now `min(CacheTTL, the response's own NextUpdate)`, so a `CacheTTL` configured longer than `NextUpdate` can no longer keep serving a response RFC 6960 already tells relying parties to treat as stale.
  - `pkg/acme/api/server.MultiProtocolServer` was investigated, not changed, per instruction: nothing in the tree imports `go-xkms/pkg/acme/api/server` outside its own package. It is a `go-trusted-ca` migration artifact (`DefaultGRPCUnixPath`/`DefaultHTTPUnixPath` still name `trusted-ca` sockets) but is not abandoned — its constructor and `buildRouter` are wired against the *current* `pkg/acme/admin` interfaces (`admin.Service`, `admin.TenantService`, `admin.AuthHandler`, `admin.NewPermissionGate`, `admin.TenantAwareService.BarrierSvc()`), the same ones `cmd/xkmsd/admin.go`'s `finalizeAdminModule` already constructs for REST, and its gRPC authorization interceptor received a real fix under #743's own number. It is very likely the intended host for #743 (ACME admin over gRPC, QUIC and MCP); wiring it in still needs the `trusted-ca` socket-path defaults renamed and a decision on whether it gets its own dedicated listeners (as built) or mounts onto `xkmsd`'s existing unified mTLS listener the way REST does today.
