- **xkey's `tpm` FIDO2 attestation statement is now WebAuthn L2 §8.3 compliant,
  so a relying party no longer rejects it.** The TPM2 key backend now
  implements `keybackend.FIDO2AttestingKeyBackend` directly
  (`keybackend.TPM2AttestingBackend`), certifying each credential key with a
  real `TPM2_Certify` under the device's Initial Attestation Key (IAK) instead
  of leaving `certInfo` as the only populated field. The emitted `attStmt` now
  carries the full required set: `ver` ("2.0"), `alg` (the IAK signature's COSE
  algorithm — including the RSA/RSA-PSS families `EncodeCOSEPublicKey` did not
  previously encode), `x5c` (the IAK certificate), `sig` (the IAK's ordinary
  signature over `certInfo`), `certInfo` (the TPMS_ATTEST TPM2_Certify
  produced, with `extraData` set to the hash of `authData‖clientDataHash`
  using the IAK's own hash algorithm) and `pubArea` (the credential key's
  TPMT_PUBLIC, whose Name TPM2_Certify's `certInfo` attests to). A statement
  missing any required field now degrades to `"none"` rather than being sent
  incomplete. `keybackend.FIDO2AttestationStatement.TPMData` is removed —
  BREAKING for any direct caller — replaced by structured `Ver`, `CertInfo`
  and `PubArea` fields. Verified end to end against go-webauthn's own `tpm`
  format verifier (the library `pkg/webauthn`'s RP already embeds) using the
  TPM simulator: a real IAK-issued statement verifies, a tampered `pubArea`
  fails the Name binding check, and a `clientDataHash` the authenticator never
  signed for fails the `extraData` check. Files:
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/keybackend/tpm_attestation.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/keybackend/keybackend.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/keybackend/cose.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/keybackend/tpm_attestation_simulator_test.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/cmd_makecredential.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/cmd_makecredential_test.go`,
  `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/fido2.go`. Follow-up filed: xkms's IAK certificate
  issuance path (`xkey tpm iak csr` + CA countersign) does not yet emit a
  certificate conformant to WebAuthn L2 §8.3.1 / the TCG EK-Profile AIK
  requirements (empty Subject, TCG-manufacturer SAN, `tcg-kp-AIKCertificate`
  EKU) — until it does, a real device's `tpm` attestation is structurally
  correct but its AIK certificate will fail a strict relying party's
  certificate-profile check. Issue #695.

## [0.20.0-alpha] - 2026-09-23

### Security

- **xkey's agent server rejects revoked and removed agents at connect time,
  and removing an agent now revokes its certificate.** An audit found the
  master-side agent server (`xkey/pkg/agent/server.go`) accepted any client
  certificate that chained to the configured CA, with no check against the
  enrollment store or the CA's revocation state — a removed agent's
  certificate kept working indefinitely, because `RemoveAgent`
  (`xkey/pkg/gui/services/agent_service.go`) only deleted the store record and
  never called `CAService.RevokeCertificate`. Both are fixed. `Server`'s mTLS
  `tls.Config.VerifyPeerCertificate` now runs
  `EnrollmentService.VerifyAgentCertificate` on every connection: the leaf's
  public-key fingerprint must match an enrolled, still-present agent in the
  store, and its serial number must not be revoked (checked directly through
  the CA's existing `IsRevoked` RPC — no new CRL parser). Either check failing,
  or the revocation check itself failing, rejects the connection; enrollment
  now records each issued certificate's serial number
  (`AgentInfo.CertificateSerial`) so it can be revoked later.
  `EnrollmentService.RemoveAgent` revokes the certificate through the CA
  first and only then deletes the record; a revocation failure returns the
  error and leaves the record in place. The GUI's `AgentService.RemoveAgent`
  now calls it instead of deleting directly, and the CLI gained `xkey agent
  code`, `xkey agent pending`, `xkey agent approve <id>`, `xkey agent reject
  <id>`, and `xkey agent remove <id>` over the same shared service layer,
  closing a GUI/CLI parity gap. One-time codes and pending enrollment
  requests, previously held only in the enrollment service's memory, are now
  persisted through `EnrollmentStore` (`FileStore`'s `agents/`, `codes/`,
  `pending/` subdirectories; `DAOStore`'s matching DAO namespaces), so a code
  or request from one process is honored by another sharing the same store
  - the CLI and a running `agent start` daemon in particular. Codes are
  stored by their SHA-256 hash, never in plaintext; `EnrollmentStore.ConsumeCode`
  is single-use and atomic even across processes (`FileStore` relies on
  `os.Remove`'s atomicity; `DAOStore`'s is Get-then-Delete, a documented gap
  since go-qrdb's `GenericDAO` has no compare-and-delete primitive yet).
  Pending requests are deleted on approval or rejection, so `ErrEnrollmentRejected`
  - unreachable once rejection deletes the record - is removed. Files:
  `xkey/pkg/agent/{enrollment,entity,errors,server,store,dao_store}.go`,
  `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/{agent_ca,agent_verbs}.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/gui/services/agent_service.go`.
- **The device attestation key verifier now refuses an Android Key Attestation whose TEE-enforced key was not generated in secure hardware, or is not authorized to sign** (#132, follow-up to #129/#124). Everything `VerifyDeviceAttestation` checked before this — the chain, the security level, the verified boot state, the genesis challenge, the live challenge signature — was equally consistent with a device attestation key generated elsewhere and imported into the TEE; only the TEE's own `Origin` claim rules that out. `xkey/pkg/attestation.RequireAttestedKeyOrigin` now refuses unless the TEE-enforced authorization list claims `Origin == GENERATED` and its `Purpose` set includes `SIGN`, reading exclusively from `TeeEnforced` — a `SoftwareEnforced` claim is the calling application's word, not the secure hardware's. An authorization list that makes neither claim (an absent extension, or evidence from a device with no TEE) fails closed. Two typed errors name the two ways it can fail: `ErrAttestationKeyOriginNotGenerated`, `ErrAttestationKeyPurposeNotSign`. `pkg/attestation/android` gained the ASN.1 extraction this check depends on — `Origin` (tag 702) and `Purpose` (tag 1) were declared on `KeyDescription.TeeEnforced`/`SoftwareEnforced` but never parsed out of a real certificate; `parseAuthorizationList` now reads both, defaulting an unclaimed `Origin` to `OriginUnknown` rather than the zero value it shares with `OriginGenerated`, so an attestation that never asserts an origin cannot be misread as asserting `GENERATED`. `BuildAttestationExtensionWithOptions` is the additive sibling to `BuildAttestationExtension` that lets a fixture assert `Origin`/`Purpose` in `teeEnforced`, re-exported through the SDK as `BuildAndroidAttestationExtensionWithOptions`; `xkey/pkg/attestation/attesttest`'s shared device-key fixtures (`AttestedLeafDER`, `NewDAK`) now default to a TEE-enforced `GENERATED`+`SIGN` claim so every existing pairing/re-attestation test keeps exercising the stricter verifier, with `*WithClaims` siblings for tests that vary the claim. Files: `pkg/attestation/android/extension.go`, `sdk/go/attestation.go`, `xkey/pkg/attestation/device.go`, `xkey/pkg/attestation/errors.go`, `xkey/pkg/attestation/attesttest/fixtures.go`; docs in `xkey/docs/phone-hsm/engineering.md`. Verified by new tests covering the accept path, an imported origin, a purpose set without `SIGN`, an authorization list with neither claim, and — the mutation guard named in the issue — a claim present only in `SoftwareEnforced`, confirmed to turn red if the check is changed to read that list instead of `TeeEnforced`; `pkg/attestation/android` is additionally verified against a real (non-synthetic) Android attestation chain, which is the first evidence that the new ASN.1 parsing decodes genuine device output and not only fixtures this suite built itself. **Caveat carried forward from the issue and not yet closed:** the coordination note in #132 asks that this be confirmed against a real handset attestation before merging — the fixture proving the parser reads genuine device output is an emulator chain with no TEE, so it can confirm the parser but not that a real StrongBox/TEE attestation reports `Origin`/`Purpose` the way this check expects; that confirmation, and a filing against xkey-android if any device disagrees, is still open.
- **`pkg/crypto/mem`'s hand-rolled `GuardedBuffer` is retired; every caller
  moves to go-enclave's `MemoryEnclave` — BREAKING.** `GuardedBuffer`'s Linux
  mlock call discarded its own error (`_ = sysCallMlock(dataRegion)`) and
  proceeded unlocked with no signal when the kernel refused — key material
  then sat on swappable pages silently. go-enclave's constructors return
  `ErrLockedMemoryUnavailable` for the same failure instead of failing open,
  and it was already a direct dependency of this module
  (`pkg/storage/sealed`), so this removes a parallel implementation rather
  than adding one. `pkg/crypto/mem` is deleted outright (no deprecation
  period, no shim — this project carries no backward compatibility).
  `mem.Zero`/`mem.GuardedBuffer` callers move to `enclave.Wipe` /
  `enclave.MemoryEnclave`: `pkg/crypto/kdf/hasher.go`,
  `pkg/keyprovider/pkcs8/sealer.go`, `pkg/server/credentials/service.go`,
  and `pkg/pintpm2/backend.go`, whose FIDO2 PIN hash cache
  (`fido2Guard atomic.Pointer[mem.GuardedBuffer]`) is now
  `fido2Enclave atomic.Pointer[enclave.MemoryEnclave]`, with hash comparison
  via `MemoryEnclave.EqualTo` (constant-time, fail-closed on a nil or
  destroyed enclave) replacing a direct `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` over
  `Bytes()`. The SDK re-export `sdk/go/crypto.go` keeps `SecureMemZero` as a
  drop-in `enclave.Wipe` alias (an existing go-quicbaas caller depends on the
  exact signature) and drops the `GuardedBuffer`-only re-exports
  (`SecureMemGuardedBuffer`, `SecureMemNewGuardedBuffer`,
  `SecureMemZeroAndFree`, and their error types), since go-enclave is
  already a public dependency SDK consumers can import directly. The three
  remaining hand-rolled zero-loops flagged alongside this
  (`pkg/pkcs11/module`'s `zeroize`, and xkey's `luks.clearBytes` /
  `authenticator.clearBytes`) are also retired in favor of `enclave.Wipe`;
  `authenticator.clearBytes` was package-shared beyond the one call site
  named in the issue, so every call site in `xkey/pkg/authenticator`
  (`attestation.go`, `key_wrapper.go`, `key_manager.go`, `token.go`,
  `ext_hmac_secret.go`) moves with it. `cmd/xkmsd` now also calls
  `enclave.WipeAll()` in its orderly-shutdown defer, alongside the existing
  `secure.Purge()` (go-qrdb#'s memguard-backed `Secret`/`Buffer` remain a
  second, still-necessary protected-memory subsystem pending qrdb's own
  migration to go-enclave); libraries in this repository call neither.
  Deferred to follow-on issues, both blocked on upstream releases that have
  not shipped: moving `cmd/xkmsctl`'s and `pkg/server/bootstrap_suite.go`'s
  direct `*memguard.LockedBuffer` use onto go-truststrap's `MemoryEnclave`
  API once that wave lands (go-truststrap#60), and dropping
  `github.com/awnumar/memguard` from `go.mod` once go-qrdb's own `pkg/secure`
  delegates to go-enclave. go-xkms#623.

### Changed

- **`xkey/pkg/authenticator.ErrNotImplemented` renamed to
  `ErrCommandNotSupported` — BREAKING.** The sentinel is returned for three
  CTAP 2.1 commands this software authenticator declines:
  `authenticatorBioEnrollment` (no fingerprint sensor to enroll against),
  and `authenticatorClientPIN` / `authenticatorLargeBlobs` when disabled by
  `Config.EnablePIN` / `Config.EnableLargeBlobs`. All three are optional per
  CTAP 2.1, `authenticatorGetInfo` never advertises the corresponding
  capability (`bioEnroll`, `clientPin`/`pinUvAuthProtocols`, `largeBlobs`)
  when declined, and `Config.SetDefaults` forces `EnablePIN` whenever
  credential management is enabled — the only feature here that mints
  pinUvAuthTokens for UV without a PIN — so declining
  `authenticatorClientPIN` with `EnablePIN=false` never blocks a required
  capability. `CTAP1_ERR_INVALID_COMMAND` (`StatusInvalidCommand`) is the
  spec-correct response in all three cases; the rename only replaces the
  inaccurate "not implemented" name with one that says so. Files:
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/authenticator.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/cmd_clientpin.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/cmd_largeblobs.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/authenticator_test.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator/cmd_largeblobs_test.go`,
  `xkey/docs/fido2/authenticator-api.md`. Fixes go-xkms#663.
- **`frost.FrostBackend.Signer` refuses a threshold greater than 1 at
  construction instead of failing on the first `Sign` call — BREAKING.** A
  `crypto.Signer` performs one synchronous `Sign` call and cannot coordinate
  a multi-party FROST round, but `Signer` previously returned a working
  `*FrostSigner` for any threshold and only discovered the problem inside
  `Sign`, where it returned an untyped `"orchestrated multi-participant
  signing not implemented"` message. `Signer` now loads the key package
  first and returns the new typed `*frost.ThresholdSigningNotSupportedError`
  (wrapping the new `frost.ErrThresholdSigningNotSupported` sentinel) when
  the key's threshold requires coordinating more than one participant,
  naming the key ID and threshold and pointing callers at `GenerateNonces`,
  `SignRound`, and `Aggregate` for distributed signing. Since every FROST key
  in this codebase — and in the underlying `go-frost` trusted-dealer
  implementation itself — requires a threshold of at least 2,
  `FrostBackend.Signer` now always returns this error for real keys;
  `FrostSigner.Sign`'s single-participant round is kept for a threshold-1 key
  built directly (not reachable through any generator here today) rather
  than removed as dead code. Files: `pkg/keyprovider/frost/backend.go`,
  `pkg/keyprovider/frost/signer.go`, `pkg/keyprovider/frost/errors.go`,
  `pkg/keyprovider/frost/signer_test.go`,
  `pkg/keyprovider/frost/backend_test.go`,
  `test/integration/frost/backend_integration_test.go`,
  `docs/frost/api.md`, `docs/frost/architecture.md`. Fixes go-xkms#663.

### Removed

- **`BackupFormatProtobuf` deleted — BREAKING.** `pkg/backup`'s `CreateBackup`
  had a `BackupFormatProtobuf` case that unconditionally returned "protobuf
  format not yet implemented": API surface that could be selected but never
  worked. JSON and Encrypted are the only backup formats go-xkms ships, so
  the `BackupFormatProtobuf` constant is deleted along with its dead
  serialization branch. Selecting an unrecognized `BackupFormat` (including
  the string `"protobuf"`) now falls through to the existing typed
  `ErrInvalidBackupFormat`, exactly as any other unknown format already did.
  Files: `pkg/backup/backup.go`, `pkg/backup/file.go`,
  `pkg/backup/backup_test.go`. go-xkms#661.
- **Deleted two unreferenced `ErrNotImplemented` sentinels — BREAKING.**
  `frost.ErrNotImplemented` (`pkg/keyprovider/frost/errors.go`) and
  `escrow.ErrNotImplemented` (`pkg/escrow/errors.go`) had zero production
  call sites; the frost sentinel is superseded by the new
  `frost.ErrThresholdSigningNotSupported` (see the FROST signer entry
  above). Test doubles that referenced `frost.ErrNotImplemented` now use a
  package-local `errMockUnimplemented` in
  `pkg/keyprovider/frost/config_test.go`. Fixes go-xkms#663.

### Fixed

- **`GetTLSCertificate` returns one canonical response shape on every
  transport — BREAKING.** REST and QUIC previously failed to decode any
  certificate with a chain: the wire-level `pkg/api/rest.GetTLSCertificateResponse.ChainPEM`
  was `[]string` while `pkg/api/transport.GetTLSCertificateResponse.ChainPEM`,
  which the REST and QUIC client transports decode into, was a `string` under
  the same `chain_pem` JSON tag. MCP's server returned a locally-defined
  `GetTLSCertificateResult{CertPEM, ChainPEMs, PrivateKeyType}` whose field
  names never matched the MCP client transport's decode target
  (`transport.GetTLSCertificateResponse{CertificatePEM, ChainPEM}`), so every
  MCP call decoded to a zero-value response. Both REST- and MCP-local result
  types are deleted; every server handler (REST, gRPC, unix, QUIC, MCP,
  embedded) and every client transport now use the one canonical
  `pkg/api/transport.GetTLSCertificateResponse`, re-exported unchanged by the
  SDK. `ChainPEM` is now `[]string` everywhere — one PEM-encoded certificate
  per chain entry, leaf excluded — matching the shape the gRPC proto
  (`GetTLSCertificateResponse.cert_chain_pem`) already used. The gRPC and
  unix client transports (`pkg/api/transport/grpc/transport.go`,
  `pkg/api/transport/unix/transport.go`) had an additional latent bug fixed
  by this change: both silently discarded every chain entry past the first.
  `xkmsctl tls get` decodes each chain entry individually via
  `client.DecodeCertificatePEM` instead of concatenating a single string.
  The private key stays deleted from this response (go-xkms#627) and does
  not come back. Files: `pkg/api/transport/types.go`,
  `pkg/api/rest/types.go`, `pkg/api/rest/handlers.go`,
  `pkg/api/mcp/types.go`, `pkg/api/mcp/handlers.go`,
  `pkg/xkms/servicer_cert.go`, `pkg/api/transport/grpc/transport.go`,
  `pkg/api/transport/unix/transport.go`, `cmd/xkmsctl/tls.go`.
- **Fixed six Makefile per-package targets that pointed at nonexistent
  packages.** `test-backup`/`coverage-backup`/`bench-backup` targeted
  `./pkg/adapters/backup/...`, which does not exist, instead of
  `./pkg/backup/...`. The same audit, run by matching every `test-*`,
  `coverage-*`, and `bench-*` per-package target's path against `go list`
  in each module, found five more: `test-auth`/`coverage-auth` and
  `test-audit`/`coverage-audit` targeted the removed `./pkg/adapters/auth/...`
  and `./pkg/adapters/audit/...` and now target `./pkg/auth/...` and
  `./pkg/audit/...`; `coverage-memory-storage` and a `bench-storage` line
  targeted `./pkg/storage/memory/...`, a subdirectory that no longer exists
  now that `NewMemoryBackend` is a two-line wrapper directly in `pkg/storage`,
  and now target `./pkg/storage`. `test-authz`/`coverage-authz`,
  `test-rbac`/`coverage-rbac`, and `test-user`/`coverage-user` targeted
  `./pkg/adapters/authz/...`, `./pkg/adapters/rbac/...`, and `./pkg/user/...`;
  none exist — authz is merged into `pkg/auth/authorize.go` (covered by
  `test-auth`), and RBAC and the user/identity model are owned by go-qrdb
  and have no local package to test, so these six targets are deleted rather
  than repointed. Files: `Makefile`. Fixes go-xkms#663.
- **Nightly `Integration Tests` now actually runs, instead of failing
  `integration-test-software` with `[setup failed]` on every scheduled
  run.** `.devcontainer/docker-compose.yml`'s `devcontainer` service
  bind-mounts `..:/workspace:cached`, which a Gitea Actions job resolves
  against the RUNNER HOST's filesystem (the daemon), not the job
  container's own checkout, so `/workspace` came up empty or unrelated and
  every `run_in_devcontainer` / `run_with_server` target died before
  compiling a package. A new CI-only overlay,
  `.devcontainer/docker-compose.ci.yml`, replaces that one bind mount with a
  named volume (Compose merges `volumes:` by container target path, so
  every other mount is untouched); the Makefile's
  `ci_sync_devcontainer_workspace` (wired into `run_in_devcontainer` and
  `run_with_server`) then populates it once per run with `docker compose
  cp`, which streams the tree over the Docker API connection rather than
  depending on a shared filesystem, so it lands correctly regardless of
  which host the daemon runs on. The overlay is layered on only when
  `COMPOSE_RUN_ID != local` (i.e. `GITHUB_RUN_ID` is set); local development
  keeps the plain bind mount unchanged. Files: `Makefile`,
  `.devcontainer/docker-compose.ci.yml`.
- **The TPM2 node-barrier key directory can no longer resolve relative to
  the process's working directory.** `resolveNodeSeal` and `initTPM2Backend`
  both derived the TPM2-sealed key directory as `Storage.Path + "/tpm2-keys"`
  with no guard on an empty `Storage.Path`; a caller that constructs
  `*config.Config` programmatically (embedded/library use of `pkg/server`,
  which never runs `config.Config.Validate`) got the cwd-relative path
  `tpm2-keys`, writing TPM key material wherever the process happened to be
  started from. Both call sites now share one
  `Server.resolveTPM2KeyDir` helper that fails closed with a typed
  `*ErrConfigRequired{Field: "storage.path", Backend: "tpm2"}` (wrapped in
  `*NodeSealError` from `resolveNodeSeal`, in `*ErrBackendCreate` from
  `initTPM2Backend`) when `Storage.Path` is unset, instead of ever writing
  key material under the working directory. Files: `pkg/server/node_seal.go`,
  `pkg/server/backend_tpm2.go`. Fixes go-xkms#609.
- **Certificate-chain integration fixtures no longer collide with the
  reserved chain-record id shape.** `pkg/storage/hardware` refuses any
  certificate id ending in `-chain` (or shaped like a chain member's
  `id-chain-<n>` CKA_ID) via `ErrIDReservedForChain`, because that shape
  names another record's chain. Several PKCS#11 and TPM2 integration
  fixtures named their certificate `test-chain`, `overwrite-chain`,
  `delete-chain`, `nitrokey-test-chain` or `empty-chain` — ids that
  themselves match the reserved shape — so every save/get/delete against
  them failed deterministically with `ErrIDReservedForChain` instead of
  exercising chain storage, masking `CertificateChainOperations` and its
  `SaveAndRetrieveChain`, `OverwriteChain` and `DeleteChain` subtests on
  every run (go-xkms#615). Fixtures are renamed to non-reserved ids
  (`chain-primary-cert`, `chain-overwrite-cert`, `chain-delete-cert`,
  `nitrokey-test-cert`, `empty-chain-cert`); no production code changed,
  the reservation itself is correct. `TestIsReservedChainID` and
  `TestReservedChainIDsAreRefusedByEveryStore` in `pkg/storage/hardware`
  gain a `test-chain` case pinning this exact regression. Files:
  `test/integration/pkcs11/pkcs11_cert_integration_test.go`,
  `test/integration/pkcs11/pkcs11_integration_test.go`,
  `test/integration/pkcs11/pkcs11_nitrokey_hsm_integration_test.go`,
  `test/integration/tpm2/tpm2_cert_integration_test.go`,
  `pkg/storage/hardware/chain_member_test.go`,
  `pkg/storage/hardware/backend_adapter_record_scope_test.go`.
- **xkey: the TPM2 barrier re-unseal path is now verified against a real TPM
  after the inactivity auto-lock (#510, runtime half).** Item 1's setup-time
  guard (#510) landed separately and left this half explicitly open: the
  reported failure was an unlock, after the 15-minute auto-lock, that failed
  with `qrdb/seal: requested strategy not registered` and was then
  misreported to the operator as an invalid PIN. `BarrierService.Unseal`
  already reopens the barrier this process is still holding rather than
  rebuilding one from scratch and re-resolving the strategy against a
  possibly-empty or mismatched ID — the exact rebuild that produced the
  reported sentinel — but nothing exercised that path with the `tpm2`
  strategy specifically: the existing regression coverage
  (`barrier_reunseal_test.go`) only drove it with `passphrase`, and every
  `AppLockService`-level Lock/Unlock test substituted a fully mocked barrier
  double. Two new tests close that gap: `app_lock_tpm2_reunseal_test.go`
  drives a real `BarrierService` through `AppLockService.Lock`/`Unlock` with
  a TPM2 sealer (plus a credential-checking control proving the reopen still
  rejects a wrong credential), and `barrier_tpm2_integration_test.go`
  (`integration && tpm_simulator`) repeats the same lock/unlock cycle against
  the in-process TPM 2.0 reference simulator instead of a mock, so a
  regression in how `TPM2Strategy` is captured or reused across the
  lock/unlock boundary fails here even if it passed against a canned
  `Sealer`. No source change was needed: this closes out the runtime half of
  #510 by proving the fix already in place. Files:
  `xkey/pkg/gui/services/app_lock_tpm2_reunseal_test.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/gui/services/barrier_tpm2_integration_test.go`. Verified with
  `go test -tags 'ble codec_json' ./xkey/pkg/gui/services/... -run
  TestAppLock_TPM2Reunseal` and `go test -tags 'integration tpm_simulator ble
  codec_json' ./xkey/pkg/gui/services/... -run
  TestIntegration_BarrierService_TPM2ReunsealAfterAutoLock`.
- **TrustedCA Serve tests no longer race for a port.** Two tests picked the
  ACME and admin ports with two separate `getAvailablePort` calls. The first
  listener closed before the second call, so the OS could return the same
  port for both, and the admin server failed with "address already in use".
  They now use `getTwoDifferentPorts`, which holds both listeners open until
  both ports are read.

## [0.19.0-alpha] - 2026-09-23

### Security

- **BREAKING: `BackupKey.PrivateKey`, `StoredCredential.PrivateKey` (in both
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator` and `xkey/pkg/cdp`), `OATHCredentialInfo.Secret`
  and `PasswordInfo.Password` are no longer plaintext exported fields — the
  key/secret/password material now lives in mlocked, guard-paged protected
  memory (`*secure.Buffer`) and is reached only through `SetXxx`/`XxxBytes`
  or `SetXxx`/`XxxString` accessors, closing the last of the go-xkms#549
  secure-analyzer findings for `pkg/backup`, `xkey/pkg/authenticator`,
  `xkey/pkg/cdp` and `xkey/pkg/backup`.** Every type keeps its historical
  JSON shape — `BackupKey`, `StoredCredential` (both packages),
  `OATHCredentialInfo` and `PasswordInfo` all gained a custom
  `MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON` pair (matching the `xkey/pkg/oath.Credential`
  pattern) that serializes the protected value under the same historical
  JSON key it always used, so archives and credential stores written by a
  prior build keep decoding byte-for-byte — proven by a golden-fixture test
  per type. `cdp.StoredCredential`'s `MarshalJSON` uses a value receiver
  (not pointer) because that type's public API passes it by value
  throughout the package; a pointer-receiver `Marshaler` would be silently
  skipped by `encoding/json` for a non-addressable value and drop the
  protected field with no error. Every caller across `pkg/backup`,
  `xkey/pkg/authenticator`, `xkey/pkg/cdp`, `xkey/pkg/backup`,
  `xkey/pkg/sync` and `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd` was converted to the new setters
  and accessors, including `MemoryStorage.copyCredential` (now
  error-returning, since cloning a protected buffer can fail) and the
  CDP-capture/sync path in `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/fido2.go`. The five
  corresponding `scripts/secure-analyzer-allowlist.txt` `pre-existing`
  entries are removed.
- **BREAKING: the CTAP2 authenticator PIN carried through the FIDO2 WebAuthn
  ceremonies, the local enrollment driver, and the init ceremony's passkey
  enrollment is now sealed in protected memory (`*secure.Secret`) instead of
  held as a plaintext `string`.** `pkg/fido2.WebAuthnAuthenticationOptions.PIN`,
  `WebAuthnAssertionRequest.PIN`, `WebAuthnRegistrationOptions.PIN`,
  `pkg/factor/fido2.LocalEnrollRequest.PIN`, `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd.CeremonyRequest.PIN`,
  `pkg/init.AdminEnrollmentConfig.PasskeyPIN` and
  `pkg/init.AdminEnrollmentContext.PasskeyPIN` all change from `string` to
  `*secure.Secret` (`go-xkms/sdk/go/secure`); a nil secret replaces the empty
  string as "no PIN configured". `fido2.Authenticator.AuthorizeWithPIN` and
  `GetPINToken` now take the PIN as `*secure.Secret` and open it only for the
  instant the CTAP 2.1 6.5.5.7 pinHashEnc computation needs its bytes, then
  destroy the buffer — the plaintext PIN is never held in a struct. Every
  caller is updated: `cmd/xkmsctl` (`resolvePINInput` now seals the resolved
  PIN, `webAuthnRegistration`/`loginAssertion`/`ceremonyFailure` take
  `*secure.Secret`), `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd` (`sealCeremonyPIN` seals the PIN
  `resolvePINInput` resolves before it reaches `CeremonyRequest`;
  `ceremonyFailure` takes `*secure.Secret`), `pkg/init`/`pkg/factor/fido2`
  (the passkey enrollment plumbing), and `cmd/xkmsd` (`resolvePasskeyPIN`
  now seals the resolved passkey PIN). The `pre-existing` deferred-review
  allowlist lines for these fields are removed from
  `scripts/secure-analyzer-allowlist.txt`.
- **BREAKING: the MCP `ssh.knownHosts.verify` and REST `POST
  /xkms/v1/ssh/known-hosts/{host}/verify` endpoints now take the presented
  host public key instead of a caller-claimed fingerprint, and delegate to
  the canonical `pkg/ssh/known_hosts.Verify` full-key comparison.** Both
  handlers previously did their own `KnownHosts().List` + string compare of
  a client-supplied `fingerprint`/`algorithm` pair against the stored pin's
  `Fingerprint` field — a caller only had to ship a string that matched, not
  the key it claimed to be presenting, so the check trusted the caller's
  claim about the key rather than examining it. `handleSSHKnownHostsVerify`
  (`pkg/api/mcp/handlers_ssh.go`) and `handleVerifyKnownHost`
  (`pkg/api/rest/handlers_ssh.go`) now parse the wire `public_key`
  (`authorized_keys` format) and call the SDK client's
  `KnownHosts().Verify(ctx, scope, owner, host, pub)`, which for the
  embedded client (used by both transports) delegates straight to
  `known_hosts.Verify` — the same full `received.Marshal()` vs.
  `Pin.PublicKey` byte comparison the gRPC transport already relies on. The
  parallel List+compare is deleted from both handlers. Wire shapes changed
  to match: `SSHKnownHostsVerifyParams` (MCP) and the REST verify DTO
  dropped `fingerprint`/`algorithm` for a required `public_key` field; the
  SDK REST and MCP clients (`sdk/go/client/ssh/rest.go`,
  `sdk/go/client/ssh/mcp.go`) now send the presented key's
  `authorized_keys` line instead of computing and shipping a fingerprint.
  A malformed `public_key` is rejected with the existing
  `sdkssh.InvalidPublicKeyError` (now also mapped to HTTP 400 in
  `HTTPStatusForError`, alongside `MissingPublicKeyError`, closing a gap
  where both fell through to 500). `xkmsctl`/`xkey` callers are unaffected:
  they already called `KnownHosts().Verify` with the actual
  `gossh.PublicKey` they held, so only the internal wire encoding changed.
- **BREAKING: PKCS#11/PIV token PINs are now `*secure.Secret` instead of
  plain Go strings across the RNG, PIV certificate storage, PKCS#11 mTLS,
  and SDK PIV-signing surfaces.** `rand.PKCS11Config.PIN`
  (`pkg/crypto/rand/rand.go`), `pivcert.PKCS11StorageConfig.PIN` and
  `.SOPIN` (`pkg/pivcert/pivcert.go`), `auth.PKCS11TLSConfig.PIN`
  (`pkg/auth/pkcs11_tls.go`), `xkms.PIVCryptoSigner.PIN`
  (`sdk/go/piv_signer.go`), and `xkmsctl`'s `Config.PKCS11PIN`
  (`cmd/xkmsctl/config.go`) all change from `string` to `*secure.Secret`, so
  a configured PIN no longer sits in memory as an unwipeable Go string for
  the life of the process. A nil PIN replaces the previous empty-string
  sentinel; every `x.PIN != ""`/`== ""` check became a nil check. Each PIN is
  opened only immediately around the boundary call that requires a plain
  string — miekg/pkcs11's `Login`, the in-house `pkcs11module.Config`, and
  `PIVSignRequest`'s wire transport — and the opened buffer is destroyed
  right after. `xkmsctl`'s `--pkcs11-pin` flag and xkey's PIV PKCS#11
  wiring now seal their raw flag/config strings into a `*secure.Secret`
  before handing them to these APIs. Updated every call site in the root
  module, `sdk/go`, and `xkey` (`pkg/crypto/rand/pkcs11.go`,
  `pkg/pivcert/pkcs11/pkcs11.go`, `cmd/xkmsctl/root.go`, `admin.go`,
  `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/piv_pkcs11.go`, and the corresponding test fixtures).
  Removed the four now-satisfied `pre-existing` rule-3 allowlist lines from
  `scripts/secure-analyzer-allowlist.txt` for these fields.
- **BREAKING: every remaining secret-bearing config field typed as a plain
  `string` is now `types.SecretValue`, closing the last open part of the
  2026-08-17 audit (#3 part 3).** `pkg/config.Config`'s `barrier.passphrase`,
  `rng.pkcs11.pin`, `backends.pkcs11.pin` (the token PIN; `backends.pkcs11.token`
  — a slot label, not a credential — stays a string), `backends.awskms.secret_key`,
  `backends.azurekv.client_secret`, `backends.vault.token`, and
  `backends.phone.noise_static_key`; every hierarchy-auth/password field of
  `pkg/tpm2.Config` (`lockout-auth`, and each of `ek`/`ssrk`/`idevid`/`iak`/
  `ldevid`/`lak`'s `hierarchy-auth`/`password`); `pkg/backend/azurekv.Config.ClientSecret`
  and `pkg/backend/pkcs11.Config.PIN`/`SOPIN`; and `pkg/ca.CAKeystorePKCS11Config.Pin`
  now follow the `types.SecretValue` custody pattern #41 established for
  `KeyConfig.Password` and `CAKeystoreSoftwareConfig.Password`: the resolved
  plaintext is sealed into the field's own memguard enclave rather than kept
  as an unwipeable Go string, and every call site borrows it with
  `types.SecretValueBytes` (WithBytes-first, falling back to `Raw` for a
  value that was never resolved — the same priority `NewPasswordFromSecretValue`
  already used) or, where a third-party SDK requires a plain string or
  `[]byte` (miekg/pkcs11's `Login`, the Azure/AWS/Vault client constructors),
  at that one documented boundary. `SPKIConfig.Pin` (`bootstrap.raft.*.spki_pin`)
  is unchanged: it is a public SHA-256 hash, not a secret. `pkg/backend/tpm2.Config`
  gains a new `HierarchyAuth` field (additive) so the TPM2 backend can
  express an Owner-hierarchy auth for the Storage Root Key it provisions —
  previously that config had no way to express one at all. The YAML/JSON
  wire shape is unchanged for every field: each still decodes from, and
  re-encodes to, the same plain reference string. Go callers that construct
  these structs directly (embedders, tests, the SDK) must update to
  `types.SecretValue{Raw: "..."}` (an unresolved literal, matching a
  straight YAML/JSON decode) or `types.NewLiteralSecretValue([]byte("..."))`
  (a resolved literal, e.g. a CLI-flag value) in place of a bare string.
  `types.SecretValueBytes` now refuses, with the new typed
  `*types.SecretReferenceUnresolvedError`, any value shaped like a secret
  reference (`scheme://name`) that nothing has actually resolved — closing a
  real gap the first pass of this change left open: a `credential://...`
  value for one of these fields previously fell through to being used
  verbatim as the secret (the reference text itself), which is worse than
  the plain string it replaced. `backends.phone.noise_static_key` (resolved
  when a phone connects, well after boot) now resolves a `credential://`
  reference for real, through the same `Server.buildSecretRegistry` the CA
  identity passwords and the cluster CA passphrase already used — no second
  resolver. `barrier.passphrase`, `rng.pkcs11.pin`, `backends.pkcs11.pin`,
  `backends.awskms.secret_key`, `backends.azurekv.client_secret`,
  `backends.vault.token`, and the `tpm2.*` hierarchy-auth/password fields are
  consumed earlier in `Server.New` than the credential service exists to
  resolve anything (`resolveNodeSeal`/`initializeBackends` run before
  `initializeCredentialService`, which itself needs the barrier those fields
  help unseal), so a `credential://` reference for any of them fails
  `Server.New` outright with `*types.SecretReferenceUnresolvedError` instead
  of silently misusing the reference text; a literal value, or one an env
  var/flag supplies, is unaffected. See
  `docs/xkmsd-configuration/engineering.md`'s Decoding notes for the full
  per-field breakdown and the follow-up this leaves open (a boot-time
  resolver that does not depend on the barrier, scoped separately).
- **`Server.resolveConfigSecrets` (`pkg/server/secret_wiring.go`) replaces
  every ad-hoc `buildSecretRegistry().Resolve` call with go-qrdb's canonical
  `secret.ConfigProcessor`, run once over the whole loaded configuration
  right after `initializeCredentialService` — the earliest point in
  `Server.New` a `credential://` reference can actually be claimed — and
  before `initializeCA`, so every consumer it precedes
  (`ca.identity[*].keys[*].password`, `ca.identity[*].keystores.software.password`,
  `cluster.raft_enrollment.ca_key_passphrase`,
  `backends.phone.noise_static_key`) now reads an already-resolved field
  through `types.SecretValueBytes` alone; the per-field resolve loop this
  replaced in `Server.initializeCA`, `resolveClusterCAKeyPassphrase`, and
  `RegisterPhoneBackend` is deleted. A literal value and an unconfigured
  field are both left exactly as decoded — the processor's own
  `secret.UnresolvableTargetError` for either is the expected, tolerated
  outcome, not a failure — and `Server.New` fails only with the new typed
  `*server.ErrConfigSecretResolution` when the registry claimed a reference
  and genuinely could not fetch it (credential store error, missing
  credential). `resolveClusterCAKeyPassphrase`'s pre-node cluster-ACME
  bootstrap caller (`provisionRaftClusterACME`, which still runs before the
  credential service exists) picks up a real fix as a side effect: it used
  to call `buildSecretRegistry().Resolve` directly, so a `credential://`
  reference on that path silently fell through the registry's literal
  fallback and used the unclaimed reference text itself as the cluster CA
  key passphrase; it now goes through `types.SecretValueBytes` like every
  other caller and fails closed with `*types.SecretReferenceUnresolvedError`
  instead. The fields consumed earlier than `initializeCredentialService`
  (`barrier.passphrase`, `rng.pkcs11.pin`, `backends.pkcs11.pin`,
  `backends.awskms.secret_key`, `backends.azurekv.client_secret`,
  `backends.vault.token`, and the `tpm2.*` hierarchy-auth/password fields
  where a config path to them exists at all) are unaffected — the same
  structural chicken-and-egg gap `docs/xkmsd-configuration/engineering.md`
  already documented remains open, scoped separately.

### Added

- **Added a compile-only CI gate (`make vet-integration`) that type-checks
  every suite under `test/integration/` before it can rot silently.**
  `go vet ./...` from the root never reaches a file behind an `integration`
  (or other suite) build tag, because that tag is never set — the reason
  #636/#638 broke `sdk/go` and `acme-tpm` unnoticed, and the `tpm2/idevid`
  and `tpm2/tpm_operations` suites drifted roughly 200 references behind
  `pkg/tpm2/store`'s current API before an agent tripped over it.
  `scripts/vet-integration.sh` discovers every distinct `//go:build` tag
  combination declared under `test/integration/` and runs one
  `go vet -tags "..."` per combination, deliberately never as one tag
  union: several suites are mutually exclusive within the same package
  (`integration && grpc` beside `integration && !grpc`, `pkcs11` beside
  `!pkcs11`), and unioning every tag would compile both halves of a pair
  together and fail on a conflict no real build configuration produces.
  Wired into CI's Lint job alongside `make vet`. Ported
  `test/integration/tpm2/idevid` and `test/integration/tpm2/tpm_operations`
  to the current `pkg/tpm2`/`pkg/tpm2/store` API (`store.NewPassword` now
  returns `(types.Password, error)`; `store.KeyAttributes`,
  `store.TPMAttributes` and the `store.KEY_TYPE_*`/`store.STORE_*`
  constants moved to `pkg/types`) so the new gate starts clean. Resolves
  go-xkms#650.

### Removed

- **`xkmsctl tls get` no longer returns the private key — BREAKING.** The
  command now goes through the canonical `ClientFactory` → SDK `Client` seam
  (`cl.GetTLSCertificate(ctx, backend, keyID)`) instead of constructing a
  local backend directly, and prints the certificate and its chain only;
  `getTLSCertLocal`'s direct `be.GetKey` path is deleted, along with the
  now-unused `--key-type`/`--key-algorithm`/`--key-size`/`--curve` flags it
  needed to look up the key locally (`cmd/xkmsctl/tls.go`,
  `cmd/xkmsctl/output.go`'s `Printer.PrintTLSCertificate`, which drops its
  `key interface{}` parameter). The wire-level cause:
  `pkg/api/transport.GetTLSCertificateResponse`'s `PrivateKeyPEM` field is
  deleted outright — it was never populated on the embedded/REST/Unix/QUIC/
  MCP paths, and the one path that did populate it, the raw gRPC
  `Service.GetTLSCertificate` (`pkg/api/grpc/service.go`), is changed to
  stop encoding and returning the private key at all. The corresponding
  proto field (`GetTLSCertificateResponse.private_key_pem`, field 3) is
  removed from `pkg/api/grpc/proto/xkmsv1/xkms.proto` and regenerated with
  `make proto`; it was unreleased, so the field number is not reserved.
  Every transport mapping that copied the field
  (`pkg/api/transport/grpc/transport.go`,
  `pkg/api/transport/unix/transport.go`) is updated to match. The private
  key for a TLS key stays in the backend that holds it: a server process
  signs and decrypts through that backend, it never receives key material
  over this call. `docs/certificate-authority/cli.md` and `user.md` are
  updated to describe the new, key-free response.
- **The deprecated `BackendFactory` seam is deleted from `cmd/xkmsctl`.**
  With `migrate` and `tls get` both moved off it, `Config.BackendFactory`,
  `BackendFactory` (the type), `Config.CreateBackend()` and
  `Config.CreateCertStorage()` (dead once `tls get` stopped building a local
  cert store) are removed from `cmd/xkmsctl/config.go`, along with their
  dedicated tests in `config_test.go` and the now-dead sentinel errors in
  `errors.go` (`ErrCreateBackendFailed`, `ErrCreateCertStorageFailed`,
  `ErrCreateDestinationBackendFailed`, `ErrCreateMigrationPlanFailed`,
  `ErrCreateMigratorFailed`, `ErrCreateSoftwareBackendFailed`,
  `ErrCreateSourceBackendFailed`, `ErrCreateStorageBackendFailed`,
  `ErrFromToFlagsRequired`, `ErrKeyIDFromToFlagsRequired`,
  `ErrInvalidKeyParameters`, `ErrMigrationFailed`, `ErrValidationFailed`,
  `MigrationResultError`). `ClientFactory` is now the only client-injection
  seam in xkmsctl; every command reaches xkmsd through the SDK `Client`.
- **`xkmsctl migrate` is removed — BREAKING.** `cmd/xkmsctl/migrate.go`,
  `pkg/migration/` and its SDK re-export `sdk/go/migration/` are deleted in
  full, along with their Makefile targets (`test-migration`,
  `coverage-migration`) and every doc mention (`docs/README.md`'s
  migration-record row, `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/crypto-backends/
  engineering.md`, `docs/certificate-authority/engineering.md`,
  `docs/acme-issuance/engineering.md`). `pkg/migration`'s plan/filter/
  batch-execute/verify engine drove two `types.KeyProvider` backends
  directly (`migration.NewMigrator(source, dest)`), an in-process
  capability the SDK `Client` never exposed and that `xkmsctl migrate` only
  ever reached by constructing local backends outside the canonical
  `ClientFactory` seam — the same deprecated pattern `tls get` used. There
  is no client-based replacement: an **exportable** key moves between
  backends one at a time through `xkmsctl key copy` (server-side `CopyKey`,
  already wired through `ClientFactory`); a **non-exportable** key (PKCS#11,
  TPM2, and other hardware-bound backends that refuse `ExportKeyTo`) could
  never move between backend registrations and still cannot.

### Fixed

- **A backup of any key with TPM attributes no longer fails to serialize.** `types.TPMAttributes.SessionCloser` is a process-local `func() error` with no JSON tag, and `encoding/json` refuses a func-typed field whether or not it is nil. So `CreateBackup` returned "failed to serialize backup" for every TPM-backed key, despite its clear-and-restore workaround, and an existing test asserted that failure. The field is now `json:"-"`, the workaround and its test helper are deleted, and the test asserts that a TPM-backed key backs up with its in-memory closer untouched. Found by staticcheck SA1026 once `BackupKey` gained a custom marshaller (#587).
- **Fixed (xkey): the FIDO2 authenticator can no longer be published a
  `PINVerifier` before the PIN service behind it is populated.**
  `xkey/pkg/gui/app.go`'s `initializeDataDir` published `a.pinService` to the
  shared authenticator via `auth.SetPINVerifier` in `initializeAuthenticator`
  before `postDataDirStartup` called `initPINService` to wire the real
  `qrdbsdk.PINService` backend into it. Compat cleanup #638 deleted
  `verifyPINHashLocked`'s local-hash fallback, which had been silently
  masking this window; without it, a correct PIN presented to the virtual
  FIDO2 HID device or browser-extension autofill during that window was
  rejected outright (`PINService.VerifyFIDO2Hash`/`IsPINSet` return `false`
  while their internal `pinSvc` is unset), rather than the request racing a
  local hash comparison that happened to still succeed.

  `initPINService` is now called inside `initializeDataDir`, immediately
  before `initializeAuthenticator`, instead of afterwards in
  `postDataDirStartup`: the PIN service only needs `a.dataDir` (already set),
  `a.tpmAccessor` and `a.storageEngineKind()`, none of which depend on the
  authenticator or the barrier, so this reordering has no cost. The
  authenticator is therefore never handed a `PINVerifier` that is not yet
  fully populated — the race is closed by construction order, not by a
  typed not-ready error. `postDataDirStartup`'s now-redundant
  `initPINService` call is removed; every caller already runs
  `initializeDataDir` immediately beforehand.

  `TestPINService_ConcurrentSetPINServiceNeverReturnsWrongResult`
  (`xkey/pkg/gui/services/pin_service_test.go`) and
  `TestAuthenticator_PINVerifier_ConcurrentPublishNeverReturnsWrongResult`
  (`xkey/pkg/authenticator/pin_verifier_test.go`) drive `IsPINSet` /
  `VerifyFIDO2Hash` concurrently with the backend being populated under
  `-race`: an incorrect hash must never verify, and once the correct hash
  verifies it must never regress. Resolves go-xkms#640.
- **Fixed three `test/integration/pkcs11` suites that could not actually
  compile under the plain `integration` tag they declared.**
  `integration_test.go`, `pkcs11_integration_test.go` and
  `pkcs11_cert_integration_test.go` unconditionally imported
  `pkg/backend/pkcs11`, whose files are all gated behind `//go:build
  pkcs11` (a cgo package), but their own build constraint was
  `//go:build integration` alone. This was invisible everywhere the suite
  had ever actually been built, because `make integration-test`'s
  `INTEGRATION_TEST_FLAGS` always bundles `pkcs11` alongside `integration`
  — it surfaced only once `make vet-integration` (go-xkms#650) vetted
  `integration` on its own, matching each file's own declared constraint.
  Their `//go:build` (and legacy `// +build`) lines now read `integration
  && pkcs11`, matching the sibling
  `pkcs11_nitrokey_hsm_integration_test.go`, which already declared it
  correctly.

## [0.18.0-alpha] - 2026-09-22

### Added

- **Admin read capability for the trust-bootstrap listener's public keys, plus `xkmsctl bootstrap show-keys`.**
  Since the bootstrap listener began generating or unsealing its own Noise_NK
  and P-256 static keys (#35) and the deprecated config fields that used to
  supply them were removed (#631), nothing reported the listener's public
  key. `BootstrapListenerKeys` closes that gap: a `bootstrap:read`-gated,
  admin-only read on every transport (REST `GET /api/v1/bootstrap/keys`,
  gRPC/Unix `BootstrapListenerKeys`, QUIC the same JSON route, MCP
  `bootstrap.showKeys`, and the embedded SDK) reports the hex-encoded public
  key for each suite the listener currently offers, in exactly the form
  `NoiseConfig.ServerStaticKey`/`ServerP256StaticKey` (and `--noise-key`/
  `--p256-key`) already accept — there is no separate SPKI pin, since no
  consumer in the stack hashes this key before pinning it; the raw public
  key is the pin. Only public material ever crosses the boundary — the
  private scalars stay in `pkg/server/bootstrap_key_custody.go`'s protected
  memory — and a listener that has not finished starting, or is not
  configured, answers the typed `xkms.ErrBootstrapListenerNotEnabled`
  (503 / `Unavailable`) rather than a response with empty fields.
  `xkmsctl bootstrap show-keys` (`--output json` for machine-readable
  output) is the CLI surface; `test/integration/bootstrap` now discovers the
  running server's key through it, pins it into a real `NoiseConfig`, and
  completes a handshake, instead of relying on a pre-shared config value.

### Removed

- **BREAKING: `pkg/ca` no longer falls back to a single shared keystore for
  every key, or to the object store for revocation/CRL persistence — both
  compat paths are deleted outright.** Every CA constructor (`New`,
  `NewParentCA`, `NewIntermediateCA`, `NewCA`, `NewFromMultiIdentityConfig`,
  `NewHierarchicalCA`) now requires `Params.BackendForStore` /
  `MultiIdentityParams.BackendForStore`; a nil factory returns the new
  `ErrBackendForStoreRequired` instead of silently routing every key to
  `Params.KeyStore` regardless of its declared `StoreType`. `resolveKeyBackend`
  and `buildKeystoreMap` no longer have a legacy path: a `StoreType` missing
  from the constructed `keystoreMap` returns `ErrKeyStoreRequired` rather than
  falling back. A caller with one uniform backend for every key now states
  that explicitly with a trivial factory (`func(cn string, st types.StoreType)
  (xkms.Backend, error) { return backend, nil }`) instead of relying on an
  implicit default.

  `Params.RevocationStore` / `MultiIdentityParams.RevocationStore` are now
  required; the new `ErrRevocationStoreRequired` replaces the silent fallback
  to the object store or to in-memory-only revocation tracking.
  `putRevocationBlob`, `getRevocationBlob`, `listRevocationBlobs`,
  `putCRLBlob`, and `getCRLBlob` (`pkg/ca/ca_extensions.go`,
  `pkg/ca/crl_persistence.go`) now talk to `revocationStore` unconditionally;
  the object-store branches, the `(persisted bool, err error)` return shape
  that reported an unpersisted write, and the directory-key skip guard that
  branch needed are gone.

  The redundant `Identity.KeystoreType` field (duplicated `Keys[0].StoreType`
  in every caller) is deleted; `Identity.GetStoreType()` now derives from
  `Keys[0].StoreType`, defaulting to `types.StoreSoftware` when unset.

  Fixed a latent bug found while making `RevocationStore` mandatory:
  `NewParentCA` and `NewIntermediateCA` (`pkg/ca/constructors.go`) built their
  inner `New(&Params{...})` call without forwarding `params.RevocationStore`,
  so any caller of those two constructors got in-memory-only revocation
  tracking regardless of what it passed in `Params.RevocationStore`.

  Production callers now wire `BackendForStore` explicitly:
  `cmd/xkmsd/init_ceremony.go` (single software backend), `pkg/server/server.go`
  (`s.backends[string(storeType)]`, extending the per-key routing the design
  already called for but no in-repo caller had wired), and
  `pkg/trust/clusterca/acme.go` (`p.opts.Backends(string(st))`).
- **BREAKING: `pkg/ssh/known_hosts` no longer trusts or creates fingerprint-only
  (v1) host-key pins — every pin now carries, and is matched against, the full
  SSH wire-format public key.** `Store.Add` rejects a `*Pin` with no
  `PublicKey` with the new `*PublicKeyRequiredError`, so a fingerprint-only
  pin can no longer be created. `Verify` no longer compares
  `keys.Fingerprint(received)` against `Pin.Fingerprint`; it compares
  `received.Marshal()` against `Pin.PublicKey` byte-for-byte (the fingerprint
  fields are still populated and still appear in `*MismatchError` for safe
  logging, but they are no longer what decides trust). `decodeEnvelope`
  (`pkg/ssh/known_hosts/store.go`) now returns the new `*LegacyPinError` for
  any stored envelope that predates envelope v2 (no `pub` field) instead of
  silently reconstructing a `Pin` with an empty `PublicKey` — `Get` and
  `Verify` (single-host lookups) fail closed with it, telling the caller the
  host must be re-pinned (`Store.Remove` then `Store.Add` with a current
  `PinFromPublicKey`). `Store.List` skips a legacy pin rather than aborting
  the whole scan, so one host needing re-pinning does not hide every other
  pin in scope from discovery/export tooling. Every transport that creates a
  pin now requires the full key too: `sdk/go/client/ssh.AddKnownHostRequest`
  and `Pin` both gained a required `PublicKey` field (embedded transport
  returns the new `*MissingPublicKeyError` / `*InvalidPublicKeyError` when
  it's missing or unparsable); `xkmsctl ssh known-hosts add` dropped its
  `--fingerprint`/`--algorithm` flags for `--key`/`--file`, which supply an
  `authorized_keys`-format line; and the gRPC `SSHAddKnownHostRequest` /
  `SSHPin` messages gained a `public_key` field so the gRPC transport can
  carry it end to end (regenerated via `make proto`). `xkey ssh host-keys add`
  dropped the same `--fingerprint`/`--algorithm` flags for `--key`/`--file`,
  mirroring xkmsctl; xkey's own TOFU accept path (`pkg/ssh/console`, already
  present in the root module) already pinned the full key it had in hand and
  needed no change, and a repo-wide grep found no other xkey producer of a
  known-hosts pin (GUI services, pairing, and `pkg/sshstore` never construct
  one — they only route an already-full-key `*Pin` through the store).
- **BREAKING: `pkg/backend/phone`'s attestation platform no longer defaults
  to `"android"` — it must be set explicitly.** `Config.Validate()`
  (`pkg/backend/phone/config.go`) previously defaulted an empty
  `AttestationConfig.Platform` to `DefaultPlatform` ("android") "for
  backward compatibility"; it now returns the new typed
  `ErrMissingAttestationPlatform` instead. The `DefaultPlatform` constant is
  deleted. A caller that configures `Config.Attestation` (attestation
  verification is opt-in — a nil `Attestation` still skips verification
  entirely, unchanged) must now name `Platform` explicitly ("android" or,
  in future, "ios").
- **`xkey/pkg/phone`'s `pkg/pairing` re-export shim is gone — BREAKING for
  any external importer of the `phone.X` aliases.** `pairing_reexports.go`
  (roughly 415 type, var, const and function aliases forwarding
  `pkg/pairing`'s wire protocol under the `phone` package name) and the
  `type Transport = pairing.Transport` alias in `transport.go` are deleted
  outright (owner rule 2026-09-22: no backward compatibility). Every
  in-tree caller that referenced a forwarded symbol as `phone.X` now
  imports `xkey/pkg/pairing` and references `pairing.X` directly; symbols
  the `phone` package genuinely owns (`PhoneKeyBackend`, `BLETransport`,
  `USBTransport`, `TCPPairingServer`, `ScanResult`,
  `BLECapableTransport`, `PeripheralRequestHandler`, and its own sentinel
  errors) are unaffected and stay `phone.X`. `handshake_fingerprint_binding_test.go`,
  which existed solely to pin the deleted re-export surface for #82, is
  deleted with it — the regression it guarded against (a re-export that
  silently stops forwarding) cannot recur once there is no re-export layer.
  Rewritten: ~63 files across `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd`, `xkey/pkg/gui/services`,
  `xkey/test/integration/{ble,phone}`, and the root module's
  `pkg/backend/phone`, `pkg/api/transport/usb`, `pkg/server`,
  `cmd/xkmsctl`; plus ~25 files inside `xkey/pkg/phone` itself that used
  the aliases unqualified. A consumer outside this repository that still
  imports `phone.NoiseSession`, `phone.Request`, `phone.HandshakeConfig`,
  `phone.MethodPing`, or any of the other forwarded protocol types must
  switch to `xkey/pkg/pairing` directly; there is no compatibility path.
- **BREAKING: the tenant "legacy path" that served CRUD and barrier
  operations directly off `*seal.BarrierRegistry` when no `TenantService` was
  composed is deleted — `TenantService` is now required everywhere a tenant
  operation is served.** `pkg/xkms/servicer_tenant.go`
  (`XKMSService.CreateTenant`, `GetTenant`, `ListTenants`, `DeleteTenant`,
  `TenantBarrierInit`, `TenantBarrierUnseal`, `TenantBarrierStatus`) no longer
  falls back to `s.barrierRegistry` when `s.tenantService` is nil; every one
  now returns the typed `ErrTenantServiceNotConfigured`. `XKMSService`'s
  `barrierRegistry` field and `SetBarrierRegistry` method, and the
  `ErrBarrierRegistryNotConfigured` sentinel, are deleted along with the
  three helper functions (`validateTenantStrategy`, `tenantInitCredentials`,
  `tenantUnsealCredentials`) the deleted branches alone used.

  `pkg/api/rest.NewTenantHandlers` now returns `(*TenantHandlers, error)`
  instead of `*TenantHandlers`: it requires both `registry` and `svc`, and
  requires `svc.TenantService()` to already be composed, rejecting a
  barrier-registry-only configuration with the existing
  `ErrTenantNotConfigured` at construction time rather than serving some
  routes and 500ing others at request time. Every handler
  (`CreateTenantHandler`, `ListTenantsHandler`, `GetTenantHandler`,
  `DeleteTenantHandler`, `TenantBarrierStatusHandler`,
  `TenantBarrierInitHandler`, `TenantBarrierUnsealHandler`) lost its
  registry-direct branch; `TenantBarrierInitHandler` / `UnsealHandler` now
  build their response via `xkmsService.TenantBarrierStatus` instead of
  reading `h.registry.TenantStatus` directly, matching
  `TenantBarrierStatusHandler`'s existing path. `pkg/api/rest/errors.go`'s
  `mapErrorToStatusCode` gained mappings for go-qrdb's own
  `qrdbsdk.ErrTenantMissing` (404) and `qrdbsdk.ErrTenantExists` (409): the
  servicer-routed path was previously under-exercised (every existing test
  wired only the registry, not a `TenantService`, so the internal fallback
  silently absorbed the gap), and now that the fallback is gone these
  sentinels are the ones a composed `TenantService` actually returns.

  `pkg/server/server.go` no longer calls the deleted `svc.SetBarrierRegistry`
  when wiring `XKMSService`.
- **BREAKING (xkey): `Authenticator.verifyPINHashLocked` no longer re-checks
  a locally persisted PIN hash after a configured `PINVerifier` rejects a
  hash.** `xkey/pkg/authenticator/authenticator.go`'s `verifyPINHashLocked`
  previously fell through to `hmac.Equal(hash, a.state.PINHash)` whenever
  `PINVerifier.VerifyFIDO2Hash` returned false, "for backward compatibility
  during lazy-init or sync race scenarios" (e.g. the PIN backend not yet
  re-initialized after a restart). That fallback let a second, potentially
  stale source of truth override a configured verifier's explicit negative
  result and is deleted: when a `PINVerifier` is set, its result is now
  final. The local `hmac.Equal` comparison against `a.state.PINHash` remains
  the verification mechanism for standalone mode (no `PINVerifier`
  configured at all — tests and offline authenticators), which is a
  different, still-supported case from a configured verifier's rejection.

  `TestAuthenticator_VerifyPINHash_FallbackAfterRestart` (a named regression
  test for the restart/lazy-init scenario the fallback existed to cover) is
  replaced by `TestAuthenticator_VerifyPINHash_VerifierRejectionIsFinal`,
  which asserts the opposite: the verifier's rejection now stands even
  though the persisted hash would itself have matched.
  `TestVerifyPINHashLocked_VerifierFailsFallsBackToState` is similarly
  replaced by `TestVerifyPINHashLocked_VerifierRejectionIsNotOverridden`. A
  new `TestAuthenticator_VerifyPINHash_NoVerifierUsesLocalState` covers the
  still-supported no-verifier-configured path explicitly.

  **Note for follow-up:** the deleted fallback existed to paper over a real
  scenario — a `PINVerifier` (e.g. `pkg/gui/services.PINService`) returning
  `false` because its own backend was not yet initialized after a restart,
  not because the PIN was wrong. `PINService.VerifyFIDO2Hash` still returns
  `false` when its internal `pinSvc` has not been loaded
  (`xkey/pkg/gui/services/pin_service.go`), so that race is structurally
  still possible; deleting the caller-side workaround did not touch it. If
  restart timing still allows a `PINVerifier` to answer before its own
  backend is ready, PIN verification can now fail transiently right after
  restart instead of silently succeeding via the deleted fallback. This
  needs verifying against current initialization ordering, or the
  `PINService` side needs to report "not ready" distinctly from "PIN
  incorrect" so callers can retry instead of treating it as a wrong PIN.

## [0.17.0-alpha] - 2026-09-22

### Security

- **FIPS 140 algorithm enforcement, and FIPS 140 mode detection itself, are now the Go standard library's job; go-xkms keeps no approved-algorithm allowlist and no second copy of the mode signal (#21). BREAKING for anything reading `pkg/crypto/fips.ApprovedAlgorithm` / `AlgorithmPermitted` / `Compiled` / `Enabled` / `EnvGOFIPS140`, `sdk/go.FIPSMode` / `FIPSEnabled`, or relying on `GOFIPS140` set as a plain runtime environment variable to activate FIPS behaviour.** `pkg/crypto/fips`'s `approvedAlgorithms` table, `ApprovedAlgorithm`, and `AlgorithmPermitted` (including the `builtFunc` indirection #219 added for it) are deleted along with every call site: `pkg/validation.isValidAlgorithm` and `pkg/xkms/keyid.validateAlgorithm` are now grammar checks only — is `algo` a spelling the package recognizes — never a FIPS policy decision.

  Enforcement now happens where the algorithm actually runs. Under `GODEBUG=fips140=only`, or a binary built with an enabling `GOFIPS140`, the standard library crypto package that implements an algorithm refuses it on its own — `crypto/ecdh` already refused X25519 this way before this change, and `crypto/mldsa`, added in this change, refuses ML-DSA the same way under a build selecting the FIPS 140-3 Go Cryptographic Module v1.0.0 (which predates ML-DSA support). A key ID naming `chacha20-poly1305`, `x448`, or a `frost-*` ciphersuite — algorithms the grammar accepts but no backend in this repository currently wires up, or (for ChaCha20) whose own FIPS posture is already handled where it is selected, in `pkg/crypto/aead.SelectOptimal` — now validates in FIPS mode where it previously did not; the downstream crypto call for a wired algorithm still refuses exactly as before.

  **`pkg/crypto/fips.Compiled` and `Enabled` are also deleted, along with `EnvGOFIPS140`, `sdk/go`'s re-exports `FIPSMode`/`FIPSEnabled` (the file is removed), and `pkg/pkcs11/module`'s `fipsEnvForTest` constant. Every caller now calls `crypto/fips140.Enabled()` directly.** `Compiled` was `crypto/fips140.Enabled()` under another name; `Enabled` read `os.Getenv("GOFIPS140")` as a runtime policy switch, but `GOFIPS140` is exclusively a `go build`/`go test -c` selector the toolchain records into the binary at link time — the Go runtime never reads it as a process environment variable, unlike `GODEBUG`. Setting `GOFIPS140` in a running process's environment (`export GOFIPS140=latest; ./xkmsd`) therefore never did anything real; it was this repository's own invented signal. Deployments must switch to `GODEBUG=fips140=on` (module active) or `GODEBUG=fips140=only` (module active and strict) at runtime, or build with `GOFIPS140=<value>` to activate the module by default. `pkg/crypto/fips` keeps only `Built`/`BuildSetting` (build provenance, for the PKCS#11 module's FIPS artifact labels) and the `DefaultKDF`/`DefaultLUKSKDF` selectors, both now driven by `crypto/fips140.Enabled()` directly. `pkg/pkcs11/module.fipsModeEnabled` becomes an overridable function variable defaulting to `crypto/fips140.Enabled`, so its ~30 existing behaviour tests drive both sides of the FIPS gate without a live `GODEBUG=fips140` subprocess per case; `xkey/pkg/oath` and `xkey/cmd/e2eprobe` call `crypto/fips140.Enabled` directly instead of going through the now-deleted SDK re-export. `test/integration/pkcs11/module/fips`'s harness now drives the built `.so` through `GODEBUG=fips140=on`, not `GOFIPS140=on`, for the same reason.

  **`pkg/quantum/dilithium2`, `pkg/quantum/mldsa65` and `pkg/quantum/mldsa87` (ML-DSA-44/65/87) move from `github.com/cloudflare/circl` to the Go standard library's `crypto/mldsa`, added in Go 1.26.** `pkg/ca` (X.509 certificate signing/verification) and `pkg/keyprovider/quantum` (the `QuantumBackend`, `MLDSAPrivateKey`/`MLDSAPublicKey`) move with them. This is not a data migration: FIPS 204's seed-to-keypair derivation is a standardized deterministic algorithm, and CIRCL and `crypto/mldsa` were verified to produce byte-identical public keys from the same 32-byte seed and cross-verify each other's signatures, so every existing stored ML-DSA seed reconstructs the identical key pair under the new implementation. `pkg/quantum/mlkem512` (ML-KEM-512, which `crypto/mlkem` does not implement) stays on CIRCL and is this repository's one remaining production CIRCL-backed algorithm; its `New` and `Create` constructors are now the shared seam that refuses with the new `ErrFIPSMode` under `crypto/fips140.Enabled()`, since CIRCL sits outside the Go Cryptographic Module boundary the standard library polices and cannot refuse itself.

  `pkg/quantum/kyber768` and `pkg/quantum/mlkem1024` already used `crypto/mlkem`; ML-DSA is the only algorithm family this change moves. `docs/fips/README.md`, `docs/backends/quantum.md`, `docs/architecture/post-quantum-cryptography.md` and `docs/pkcs11/module/v32-compliance.md` are updated to match.
- **`xkey oidc login`'s CLI token store now moves behind the go-qrdb barrier
  the same way the OATH, FIDO2, and Noise-key stores already do, and holds
  the access/refresh/ID tokens in mlocked protected memory while resident in
  the process (go-xkms#4). BREAKING: existing logins do not survive the
  upgrade — the CLI never reads the old plaintext `~/.xkey/tokens.json`
  format, and there is no migration; run `xkey oidc login` again.** The CLI's
  own hand-rolled plaintext JSON writer/reader (`storeToken`/`loadToken`/
  `saveTokenStore` over `os.WriteFile`) is deleted outright and replaced by
  `openOIDCTokenStore` (`xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/oidc_token_store.go`), which
  reuses the CLI's one barrier-or-warn decision
  (`resolveSecretStoreBackend`, `barrier_store.go`): a barrier-encrypted
  `xkms.StorageBackend` when a barrier is initialized, or the historical
  unencrypted file with the one standard "unencrypted at rest" warning
  otherwise — never a second encryption scheme. An explicit `--token-store
  <path>` still bypasses barrier auto-detection and writes exactly that
  file, matching `xkey oath`'s `--store` override.

  `OIDCStoredToken.AccessToken`/`RefreshToken`/`IDToken` are no longer plain
  Go string fields: they live in `*secure.Buffer` (`sdk/go/secure`), reached
  through accessor/setter methods (`AccessToken()`, `SetAccessToken`, …),
  mirroring how `xkey/pkg/oath`'s `Credential` holds its shared secret.
  `Destroy()` wipes them; every command and the auto-refresh loop now calls
  it once the token is no longer needed.

  The `--background`/`--auto-refresh` worker (`runAutoRefresh`) opens its
  token store once, before the refresh loop starts, and reuses that same
  open store — and, for a barrier-backed store, the same unsealed barrier —
  on every tick, rather than reopening (and re-unsealing) it each interval.
  The detached background process forwards `--barrier-password-file` to
  itself when set, since it has no terminal to prompt on; a bare
  `--barrier-password` value is never forwarded on argv, to keep it out of
  `ps` output, and `XKEY_BARRIER_PASSWORD` reaches the child through normal
  environment inheritance instead.
- **Four more root-module secrets that used to sit as plain `[]byte`/`string`
  now live in protected memory (`*secure.Buffer` / `*secure.Secret` /
  `types.SecretValue`), closing another slice of #587's inventory (refs
  #41).** `luks.TPMSealResult.Passphrase` (`pkg/luks/tpm.go`) is now a
  `*secure.Buffer`; `SealPassphrase` seals the random passphrase into it
  immediately after the TPM2_Create call consumes the plaintext, and the
  narrow `Seal()` wrapper — whose signature callers still depend on — borrows
  and copies out only at that one required `[]byte` boundary, then destroys
  the buffer.

  `pkcs11/module.ExportKeyMaterialResponse.KeyMaterial` and
  `ImportKeyMaterialRequest.KeyMaterial` (`pkg/pkcs11/module/crypto.go`) are
  now `*secure.Buffer`. The export path seals the backend's response the
  moment it crosses into the module's own response type; the import path
  seals `C_CreateObject`'s CKA_VALUE before handing it to the BYOK wrap
  ceremony. `Module.secretKeyValue` — which fills a revealable secret key's
  CKA_VALUE for `C_GetAttributeValue` — borrows and copies out at the one
  place that protection necessarily ends: PKCS#11's C ABI has no enclaved
  `CK_ATTRIBUTE.Value`, so only that last copy is unbounded Go-heap memory.

  `clusterca.KeyProtection.Passphrase` (`pkg/trust/clusterca/keyprotect.go`)
  is now a `*secure.Secret`, and its config source,
  `RaftEnrollmentConfig.CAKeyPassphrase` (`pkg/config/config.go`), is now a
  `types.SecretValue` rather than a plain string — the same protected-config
  pattern #41 established for CA identity passwords. `Server.
  resolveClusterCAKeyPassphrase` (`pkg/server/cluster_ca_strategy.go`)
  resolves any `credential://` reference through the server's secret
  registry and reseals the plaintext into the `*secure.Secret`
  `KeyProtection.Passphrase` needs; the tpm-kek strategy's seed-derived KEK
  (`kekProtection` in `pkg/trust/clusterca/keystrategy_tpmkek.go`) is sealed
  the same way, preserving the existing hex-string passphrase exactly so
  already-sealed keystores keep decrypting.

  `acme/client.CertificateResource` (`pkg/acme/client/types.go`) had no
  constructor or consumer anywhere in the tree outside its own coverage
  tests, so it — and its four methods (`GetCertificate`, `GetPrivateKey`,
  `GetTLSCertificate`, `SaveToFiles`) and the error values only they used —
  were deleted rather than converted; `encodePrivateKeyPEM` and
  `ErrUnsupportedKeyType`, which serve a different, still-live test path,
  were left in place.
- **Ten xkey leaf secrets move into protected memory, and one unimported
  duplicate PIV package is deleted** (#587, #41, #133). String-like secrets
  become `*secure.Secret`, byte secrets `*secure.Buffer`, always borrowed at
  the point of use rather than materialized as an unwipeable Go string: `usb.ImageConfig.Passphrase`
  (`formatLUKS` opens and borrows it for the whole LUKS format/unlock/lock
  sequence); `pwimport.ParsedEntry.Password` (the CSV, KDBX and XML parsers
  seal the parsed password immediately, and `ToStaticPassword` opens it only
  at the storage boundary); `authenticator.pinReadResult.pin`, whose
  `readPIN` now returns a `*secure.Buffer` the caller destroys, trimming
  surrounding whitespace on the raw bytes instead of a heap string; `gui/services.SudoElevator.password`,
  whose `Run` assembles the sudo stdin payload into a wipeable slice instead
  of an unwiped `bytes.Buffer`; `cmd/xkey/cmd.sharedKeyMaterial.KeyMaterial`,
  borrowed only for the duration of the phone share request; `cmd/xkey/cmd.FIDO2Config.PIN`,
  sealed once from viper and opened only to seed the authenticator's initial
  PIN; and `cmd/xkey/cmd.passwordListEntry.Password`, written to the CLI
  writer directly from the borrowed bytes rather than through a `%s` verb.
  `authenticator.UserVerificationResult.PIN` is deleted outright along with
  its only writers (`AutoGrantHandler`'s `simulatedPIN` and
  `NewAutoGrantHandlerWithPIN`): nothing in the tree ever read it. The
  unimported `xkey/pkg/pivcert` package, a stale duplicate of the canonical
  `pkg/pivcert`, is deleted. `scripts/secure-analyzer-allowlist.txt` drops
  the ten now-enforced entries; `make secure-analyzer` is green with no
  stale entries.

### Added

- **`xkey/skills/xkey-agent/SKILL.md`: an Agent Skill for driving an existing xKey instance from the CLI (#1).** It teaches an AI agent the read-only and status verbs it may run (`barrier status --json`, `cert show|export`, `piv list|show|status`, `fido2 status`, `agent status`, `oath list|generate`, `version`) and marks every human-only step as off-limits: barrier unseal, `unlock`, `touch`, `fido2 init-token`, certificate requests, auth ceremonies, PIV generate/delete and OATH add/scan/remove. An agent never supplies a PIN, passphrase or secret by stdin, environment or flag. Every command and flag in the skill was checked against the built CLI's `--help` output. Per-agent headless instances are a separate design, #624.

    and `Config.Barrier` are gone: this struct always rejected

    field and its dead `embedded.BarrierConfig` wiring in `service.go`
    carried no reachable behavior. Encryption at rest for the embedded ACME
    data plane is configured through the parent xkmsd barrier only.

    carries `Auto`/`DaysBefore`) — none of those fields drove real renewal

    used a hardcoded interval, ignoring `Config.Renewal.CheckInterval`.

  Config loaders stay lenient (unknown YAML/JSON keys are ignored), so a
  file that still names a removed key parses without error — it is simply
  never read. A shipped config or script naming an old environment variable
  or flag silently stops taking effect; there is no warning and no fallback.
  Every shipped config (`configs/xkmsd*.yaml`), example
  (`examples/config.example.yaml`), integration-test compose/Dockerfile/
  script under `test/integration/{bootstrap,cluster,pkcs11/module,api,sdk}/`,

The package-level `activeResponder`/`serverMu`/`fatalHandler` state backing them is deleted along with the tests that only existed to exercise it; `docs/acme/challenges.md` and `docs/acme/sdk/README.md` drop the references.

Not removed despite matching the survey: `pkg/pivcert/pkcs11.NewFromSession` has a genuine production caller (`xkey/pkg/gui/pivcert_pkcs11.go`, the no-`soPin` branch of `newPKCS11PIVCertStorageFromConnection`) and stays. `cmd/xkmsctl/config.go`'s `BackendFactory`/`Config.BackendFactory`/`CreateBackend` are the live dependency-injection seam behind two production commands (`migrate.go`, `tls.go`, 7 call sites) and roughly 40 test call sites across `config_test.go`, `migrate_test.go`, `tls_test.go`, `tls_run_test.go` — rewriting those commands onto `ClientFactory` is an architecture change outside this PR's no-behaviour-change scope and needs an explicit ruling.
- **Every remaining backward-compatibility shim in the root storage formats is gone — BREAKING (on-disk data).** Per the owner's 2026-09-22 ruling ("we dont need to preserve any backward compatibility at the expense of bloating and complicating our codebase"), the dual readers, version-gated inference and silent fallbacks below are deleted outright; old data now fails with a typed error instead of being interpreted. The stack is pre-release alpha, so no migration tool is provided.
  - **`pkg/keyprovider/symmetric.Marshal`/`Unmarshal`** now write and accept only wire version 2 (version byte + explicit GCM nonce mode marker byte). The version-1 layout (no marker byte) is refused by `Unmarshal` with a typed error naming the removed format; there is no dual reader. `GCMNonceMode` itself is unaffected.
  - **`pkg/keyprovider/symmetric`'s key metadata** is a single schema version. `loadKeyMetadata` now returns `(*keyMetadata, error)`: a missing record, an unparseable record, or a record stamped with any other schema version is `ErrKeyMetadataNotFound` or a parse/version error, not a silently-defaulted `Exportable=false, Sensitive=true` record. `deleteKeyMetadata` no longer swallows a missing record — it also reports `ErrKeyMetadataNotFound`. `ListKeys` and `DeleteKey` now fail on a key with no valid metadata record instead of listing/deleting it with guessed attributes.
  - **`pkg/keyprovider/pkcs8`'s key metadata** is a single schema version. `resolveKeyOrigin` is a plain read of the record's `key_origin` field with no version-gated inference: a record with no origin recorded (including a record whose schema version does not match, which is now discarded exactly like a corrupt record) resolves `types.KeyOriginUnknown`, not `types.KeyOriginGenerated`. `pkg/xkms`'s PIV attestation path (`refuseUnattestableKey`) already treats `KeyOriginUnknown` as safe-to-attest for backends that never record provenance (PKCS#11, TPM2, cloud KMS), so this only changes behavior for pkcs8-backed keys whose metadata record predates the origin field or fails to parse.
  - **`BackendFor`/`getBackendForKID` (go-xkms#312) no longer fall back to treating `StoreType` as a registry name.** `ParseKeyIDToAttributes` now sets `KeyAttributes.Backend` from a Key ID string's backend segment (previously only `StoreType`), matching what `ListKeys`'s `stampBackendName` has already done for listed keys. Attributes that carry only `StoreType`, with no `Backend`, now resolve to `DefaultBackend` instead of to whichever registered backend happens to report that `StoreType`.
  - **`pkg/storage/hardware.TPM2CertStorage`** requires every NV certificate record to carry its magic header (`XKC1`) and, for a chain, the explicit chain-marker PEM header on every block. The headerless record shape and the NV-handle addressing form that existed only to reach it (`"0x01800000"` as a certificate ID) are gone, as is the member-count inference that classified an unmarked multi-block record as a chain. A record missing the magic header now fails a direct lookup with `ErrCertRecordMissingHeader` and is skipped by `ListCerts` (indistinguishable from another subsystem's use of the same NV index range) instead of being listed under its NV handle.
  - **`pkg/pkcs11/module.ModuleStorage.LoadFailedAttempts`** drops its `recordUser, recordSO uint32` parameters and no longer seeds the dedicated lockout-counter key from the token record's embedded snapshot. A dedicated key that is absent now reads as zero attempts, not as the record's stale snapshot value.
  - **`pkg/xkms.Unseal`** no longer falls back to the default auto-generated sealing key when a supplied `KeyID` fails to parse (the legacy `storeType:keyType:CN:algo` `ID()` shape). A non-empty `KeyID` that fails `ParseKeyIDToAttributes` now always returns `ErrKeyIDParse`, matching `Seal`'s existing behavior; the auto-resolve-to-default-sealing-key path still applies only when no `KeyID` is supplied at all.

### Fixed

- **A TPM endorsed through endorse-01 can now enroll an IDevID: its EK certificate records the TPM manufacturer code where enroll-01 reads it.** Every enroll-01 of an endorsed TPM (one with no manufacturer EK certificate — swtpm, many platform TPMs) was refused with a bare `500 serverInternal: Failed to sign TCG-CSR-IDEVID`, because `SignTCGCSRIDevID` could not find the tcg-at-tpmManufacturer code TCG DevID v1 r12 §8.1 puts at the head of the hardwareModuleName (`ErrTCGEKManufacturerUnknown`). Two defects combined. The endorse-01 finalize handler never passed a manufacturer to `IssueEKCertificate`; and when one was passed, `IssueEKCertificate` wrote it as a standalone extension under the attribute's own OID, which `TCGTPMManufacturer` does not read. Now the endorse-01 client reads the code from the TPM (`TPMModule.TPMManufacturer`, from `TPM_PT_MANUFACTURER`) and asserts it in the finalize CSR as a subjectAltName directoryName; the handler validates its form (`id:` + eight uppercase hex digits, `ValidateTCGTPMManufacturer`), holds it to any `deviceInfo.tpmManufacturer` the account's EAB names, and refuses with `badCSR` / `unauthorized` otherwise; and `IssueEKCertificate` records it in a subjectAltName directoryName per the TCG EK Credential Profile.
